PURPOSE OF THE ROLE:
The Revenue and Quality Control (QC) Clerk is responsible for ensuring the accuracy, completeness and integrity of operational revenue, customer billing, supplier costs and supporting documentation. The incumbent will perform quality control checks across operational and financial transactions to safeguard company profitability, minimise revenue leakage, validate supplier costs and ensure compliance with company policies, customer agreements and operational procedures.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:
1. Revenue Quality Control:
• Verify all customer revenue prior to invoicing.
• Ensure approved customer tariffs, pricing agreements and contractual rates have been correctly applied.
• Validate freight charges against approved customer rate schedules.
• Verify actual versus volumetric weights, and confirm pallet quantities, dimensions and service types.
• Ensure fuel surcharges, documentation fees and all applicable accessorial charges have been correctly applied.
• Ensure all billable services have been accurately captured before invoices are released.
• Identify underbilling, overbilling and revenue leakage, and investigate billing discrepancies before invoicing.
• Ensure invoices are processed within agreed service level agreements (SLAs).
2. Destination and Routing Verification:
• Verify that all collection and delivery destinations have been accurately captured by Operations, Inhouse Teams and Customers.
• Ensure destination branches, delivery points, service locations and routes are correctly allocated.
• Validate that all waybills are assigned to the correct customer account, destination and service type.
• Identify and investigate incorrect destination captures that could result in operational delays, incorrect billing or misrouted freight.
• Ensure destination amendments are authorised and supported by appropriate documentation.
• Liaise with Operations, Customer Service and Customers to resolve destination discrepancies.
• Monitor recurring destination capture errors and recommend corrective actions.
3. Cost of Sales (COS):
Quality Control Primary focus on validating all Cost of Sales suppliers, including Third Party Suppliers, Linehaul Suppliers and Labour Suppliers:
• Verify supplier invoices against approved pricing agreements and contracts.
• Confirm services billed were performed and authorised.
• Validate routes, kilometres, vehicle allocations and operational activities.
• Verify labour hours and supporting documentation.
• Identify duplicate, incorrect or unauthorised supplier invoices, and resolve discrepancies before payment.
• Identify opportunities to reduce unnecessary operational expenditure.
4. Operational Invoice Verification:
Perform detailed quality control checks on all operational invoices, including freight rates, customer tariffs, supplier rates, weights, consolidations, pallet quantities, delivery zones, regional and outlying delivery charges, fuel calculations, documentation fees, insurance charges and other applicable surcharges, collection and delivery dates, Proof of Delivery (POD), duplicate billing, missing waybills, incorrect customer allocations, supporting documentation and customer purchase orders where applicable.
5. Revenue Protection:
• Identify and eliminate revenue leakage, and recover missed billable revenue.
• Ensure all operational costs are recoverable where applicable.
• Protect company profitability through accurate billing and quality control, minimising financial losses from billing inaccuracies or operational errors.
6. Reporting Prepare daily, weekly and monthly reports on revenue, billing and supplier discrepancies, QC findings, revenue recovered, cost savings identified, outstanding investigations, operational exception reports, revenue leakage analysis and supplier overcharge reports.
7. Compliance and Governance Ensure compliance with company policies, approved customer tariffs and pricing agreements, supplier contracts, operational SOPs, internal financial controls, quality standards and audit requirements. Maintain complete audit trails for all corrections, adjustments, approvals and supporting documentation.
8. Continuous Improvement:
• Identify recurring operational and billing errors and recommend process improvements.
• Assist in developing and maintaining Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs).
• Support continuous improvement initiatives that improve billing accuracy, operational efficiency and customer service.

about_role:
Introduction:
The Business Process Analyst (Store Operations) supports the CIO’s enterprise transformation programme by analysing, standardising, and optimising store-level operational processes across TBCo’s retail and distribution network.
Description:
The Business Process Analyst (Store Operations) supports the CIO’s enterprise transformation programme by analysing, standardising, and optimising store-level operational processes across TBCo’s retail and distribution network.
This role ensures that store operations, including Sales, Receiving, Stock Control, Deliveries, Customer Service, and Facilities, are efficient, standardised, and digitally enabled, driving consistency, capacity creation, and superior customer experience across all branches.
The incumbent serves as the bridge between store operations and head office, translating strategic objectives into executable processes that simplify work, reduce waste, and improve service delivery.
Key Responsibilities
1. Process Analysis & Design
• Map and document As-Is and To-Be workflows for core store functions, including:
• Sales and Customer Service
• Goods Receiving and GRN
• Stock Control
• Deliveries and Logistics
• Cash Management and Administrative Procedures
• Store Maintenance and Compliance
• Identify operational inefficiencies, redundant activities, and non-standard practices across stores.
• Design optimised “To-Be” processes that promote standardisation, simplicity, and efficiency.
• Ensure all process models align with TBCo’s enterprise architecture, technology systems, and CIO strategy.
• Maintain updated store process documentation in the central process repository.
2. Process Optimisation & Continuous Improvement
• Apply Lean and Six Sigma methodologies to eliminate waste, reduce transaction time, and improve throughput.
• Collaborate with Store Managers and Regional Operations teams to implement best practices.
• Develop Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and store execution checklists.
• Monitor operational KPIs such as customer wait time, order fulfilment accuracy, inventory management and delivery turnaround.
• Establish continuous improvement loops to embed learning and drive operational maturity.
3. Digital & Automation Enablement
• Partner with IT, Architecture, and ERP teams to automate manual workflows (e.g., GRN capture, delivery confirmations, sales order tracking).
• Support rollout and training on digital tools and mobility solutions.
• Identify and document opportunities for RPA and workflow automation at store level.
• Support system testing, UAT, and change adoption for new digital initiatives.
• Ensure alignment of store processes with ERP, CRM, and e-commerce integrations.
4. Governance, Compliance & Risk
• Ensure store operations comply with King IV governance, POPIA, Health & Safety, and internal policies.
• Conduct operational compliance checks and audits of key store processes.
• Identify risks related to inventory handling, cash control, and data privacy, and recommend mitigations.
• Support standardisation of Delegation of Authority and store-level approval processes.
• Ensure full documentation and audit readiness of all store workflows.
5. Business Process Auditing
• Perform scheduled process audits across stores to ensure compliance with approved SOPs and standards.
• Develop and maintain operational audit templates and process risk registers.
• Analyse recurring issues and process deviations, recommending corrective and preventive measures.
• Partner with Operations, Finance, and Compliance to address findings and verify closure of audit actions.
• Report audit outcomes and improvement opportunities to the Risk Committee and CIO.
6. Collaboration & Stakeholder Engagement
• Work closely with Store Managers, Regional Managers, Shared Services, and Merchandise to ensure end-to-end process alignment.
• Facilitate process improvement workshops and training at store level.
• Capture on-the-ground insights to inform process design and future system enhancements.
• Support communication and change management initiatives for process rollouts.
• Act as the liaison between stores and head office to ensure operational feedback is incorporated into strategic planning.
Requirements:
• Bachelor’s Degree or Diploma in Operations Management, Industrial Engineering, Business Administration, or related field.
• 3–5 years’ experience in retail operations, process improvement, or business analysis.
• Experience mapping and optimising operational processes using BPMN or similar tools.
• Lean Six Sigma Yellow or Green Belt (preferred).
• Working knowledge of ERP, POS, inventory, and logistics systems (e.g., Syspro, SAP, Klipboard, Babbage).
• Experience with data analysis and dashboard tools (Excel, Power BI).

Join a top team and be involved in prestigious corporate projects in the built environment.
About Our Client
Our client is a leading national interior design firm with a solid reputation for quality interior design and reliability in the corporate market. Operating since the early 90’s, the firm provides solutions across interior architecture, project management, and turnkey solutions. They serve a diverse client base across Cape Town and Johannesburg.
The Role: Senior Project Manager
This role exists to lead a small project management team in Cape Town and oversee projects from inception to delivery. The position contributes to the business by collaborating with management to determine project feasibility, fee structures, margins, and project profitability while acting as a brand ambassador. Key focus areas include team supervision, budget compilation, project master programming, procurement, site management, client liaison, and project close-out.

• Apply 5-7 years of project management experience in the built environment to lead a small project management team in Cape Town and oversee projects from inception to delivery.

Description
The Mid-Level Full-Stack Developer is responsible for designing, developing, testing, and supporting high-quality software solutions across the full technology stack, including user interfaces, backend services, APIs, databases, and cloud-based infrastructure. Working closely with senior team members, product stakeholders, and cross-functional stakeholders, the role focuses on delivering well-defined product features that are secure, scalable, maintainable, and aligned with business requirements.
This role requires a developer who is comfortable taking ownership of scoped work from implementation through testing, review, and deployment while collaborating effectively with the broader engineering team. The successful candidate will contribute to technical excellence through adherence to software engineering best practices, automated testing, secure coding principles, and continuous improvement.
Why This Role Matters
The Mid-Level Full-Stack Developer plays a critical role in transforming business requirements into reliable, scalable software solutions that deliver value to customers. By contributing across the frontend, backend, API, and database layers, this role ensures that product features are developed efficiently while maintaining high standards of quality, security, and maintainability. Through collaboration with senior team members and product stakeholders, the role helps accelerate product delivery, improve platform stability, and support the long-term evolution of the organisation's technology ecosystem. This position also strengthens engineering capability by contributing to technical documentation, knowledge sharing, and continuous improvement initiatives that enhance development practices across the team.
Key Responsibilities
1. Full-Stack Software Development
• Design, develop and maintain application features across frontend, backend, APIs, workers and databases.
• Deliver production-ready functionality using modern software engineering practices.
• Take ownership of assigned features from development through deployment.
• Ensure software meets functional and technical specifications.
• Produce maintainable, scalable and well-structured code. 2. Frontend Development
• Develop responsive user interfaces using React and Next.js.
• Build accessible and user-friendly web applications.
• Implement reusable UI components and layouts.
• Optimise application performance and responsiveness.
• Ensure consistent user experiences across supported browsers. 3. Backend & API Development
• Develop backend services using TypeScript and Node.js technologies.
• Build validated RESTful APIs using Hono, Zod and OpenAPI.
• Implement secure authentication and authorization mechanisms.
• Apply consistent client-scoping and access control principles.
• Develop integrations with third-party systems and SaaS platforms. 4. Database Design & Data Management
• Create and maintain PostgreSQL database schemas.
• Develop efficient database queries and stored logic where required.
• Design and execute database migrations.
• Implement constraints and row-level security.
• Ensure data integrity, performance and scalability. 5. Application Security & Compliance
• Apply secure coding principles throughout development.
• Implement authentication, authorization and audit capabilities.
• Validate user inputs and protect against common security vulnerabilities.
• Support compliance with POPIA and applicable data protection standards.
• Handle sensitive data with care and professionalism. 6. Testing & Quality Assurance
• Develop unit, integration, contract and browser-based automated tests.
• Participate in Test-Driven Development (TDD) and specification-driven development.
• Verify AI-assisted generated code before implementation.
• Resolve defects identified during testing.
• Maintain high standards of software quality. 7. System Integration & Cloud Technologies
• Develop integrations with external APIs and cloud services.
• Implement asynchronous processing and messaging workflows.
• Support Azure Container Apps and cloud-native deployments.
• Contribute to Infrastructure-as-Code implementations using Bicep and Terraform.
• Assist in maintaining reliable CI/CD pipelines. 8. Defect Resolution & Production Support
• Investigate issues across frontend, backend, database and worker services.
• Troubleshoot production incidents with senior team support.
• Participate in software releases and deployment activities.
• Monitor application behaviour and recommend improvements.
• Contribute to operational stability and system reliability. 9. Collaboration & Agile Delivery
• Work closely with product owners to clarify business requirements.
• Break work into manageable delivery increments.
• Participate in sprint planning, reviews and retrospectives.
• Collaborate effectively with senior developers and peers.
• Seek guidance when architectural or security decisions require escalation. 10. Code Quality & Continuous Improvement
• Participate in peer code reviews.
• Provide constructive feedback during development reviews.
• Follow established coding standards and architectural guidelines.
• Maintain clear technical documentation and operational runbooks.
• Identify opportunities to improve development practices and engineering processes. 11. Technical Documentation & Knowledge Sharing
• Produce accurate technical documentation.
• Maintain operational runbooks.
• Document implementation decisions and design considerations.
• Share technical knowledge with team members.
• Contribute to continuous learning within the engineering team. 12. Professional Development
• Stay current with emerging development technologies.
• Continuously improve technical capabilities.
• Learn new frameworks and tools where required.
• Develop broader understanding of business processes.
• Demonstrate initiative in expanding technical expertise.

• Participate and contribute actively to the IGTM process and plans
• Ensure consistent messaging across all communication channels and support multi-channel promotion.
• Establish clear communication channels for experiential execution.
• Ensure the use of various communication channels (as aligned with the IGTM plan and PlayBooks) to maximise attendance and enhance the Brand and stakeholder experience

• Source and secure MCs, entertainment, and speakers for non-technical events, ensuring they align with the objectives of the experience and audience expectations.

• Ensure the coordination of all logistics for speakers, including travel, accommodation, technical requirements, and other related arrangements by the Experiential Marketing Assistants.

• Manage enrolments and delegate communication.
• Responsible for on-site management, ensuring positive stakeholder experiences.
• Implement risk management strategies to mitigate potential issues.
• Provide guidance and oversight to experiential marketing assistants
• Keep your finger on the pulse of industry trends and best practices
• Implement lessons learned from previous experiences

• Support SAICA’s transformation into an insights-driven organisation by leveraging data and analytics to enhance decision-making, improve processes, and drive continuous improvement in your area of work.
• Effectively utilise digital tools and technology to enhance productivity, streamline workflows, and improve service delivery. Stay informed about new and emerging technologies relevant to your role.
• Adopt and embrace AI-driven tools and automation to enhance efficiency, accuracy, and effectiveness in job-related tasks, while continuously seeking opportunities to improve processes through innovative technology solutions. Output 3: Stakeholder Communication and Collaboration
• Conduct regular meetings with experiential champions and stakeholders to understand requirements and provide updates.
• Proactively share project plans and regular updates with stakeholders, ensuring they are informed of developments and task completion.
• Provide timely updates on logistics, status, and any potential issues.
• Maintain positive and transparent relationships with all stakeholders. Output 4: Insights-Driven Reporting & Organisational Transformation
• Support SAICA’s transformation into an insights-driven organisation by leveraging data and analytics to enhance decision-making, improve processes, and drive continuous improvement in your area of work

• Ensure data collection methods are effective, providing relevant, high-quality data for analysis and reporting. Proactively address data inconsistencies

Introduction:
Mascor is a Company consisting of franchised Automotive and fuel divisions. With more than 50 years in the industry, we offer prestige brands while our highly skilled staff provides professional and high-quality service and standards of workmanship.
Description:
Mascor is a Company consisting of franchised Automotive and fuel divisions. With more than 50 years in the industry, we offer prestige brands while our highly skilled staff provides professional and high-quality service and standards of workmanship.
The following position has become available at Mascor in Greytown: Creditors Clerk.
RESPONSIBILITIES:
Invoice Processing and Creditors Administration
• Receive, verify, code and process supplier, administration and internal invoices accurately and within agreed deadlines.
• Confirm that invoices are valid, correctly authorised and supported by the required documentation.
• Allocate transactions to the correct supplier, general ledger account, cost centre and business entity.
• Follow up with branches and suppliers regarding missing or outstanding invoices, statements, credit notes and supporting documents.
• Maintain complete, accurate and orderly electronic or physical creditors records.
Reconciliations and Month-End
• Reconcile each supplier statement to the creditors ledger monthly and investigate all reconciling items.
• Reconcile internal accounts between Mascor, Fuel and FuelCo and resolve discrepancies promptly.
• Prepare and process journals, transfer journals and contras on the applicable accounting systems.
• Review creditor balances and outstanding items to support accurate and timely month-end close.
• Retain reconciliations and supporting documentation for management review and audit purposes.
Payments and Banking Preparation
• Prepare accurate payment runs for Fuel, FuelCo, Equip SA, Dalton Toyota, Greytown Toyota and other assigned entities.
• Verify supplier details, approved invoices, payment terms and amounts before submitting payment batches for authorisation.
• Prepare CSV payment files for upload to the bank in accordance with approved controls and cut-off times.
• Ensure that suppliers are paid accurately and timeously and distribute remittance advice where required.
• Support the prevention of duplicate, unauthorised or incorrect payments by applying established financial controls.
Transaction Review and Allocations
• Review E-Wallet transactions for Fuel, FuelCo, Dalton Toyota, Greytown Toyota and Head Office.
• Check credit card allocations and ensure that transactions are supported and allocated correctly.
• Process other required invoices and finance transactions for assigned entities.
• Identify unusual or incomplete transactions and escalate them to the appropriate manager.
Supplier and Stakeholder Management
• Act as a professional point of contact for supplier, branch and internal stakeholder queries.
• Investigate and resolve invoice, statement, allocation and payment queries within agreed turnaround times.
• Communicate clearly and timeously regarding outstanding information, disputed items and payment status.
• Maintain constructive working relationships and uphold the company’s reputation in all interactions.
Compliance and General Administration
• Comply with company policies, delegated authority levels, financial controls, applicable laws and regulations, occupational health and safety requirements and relevant franchise requirements.
• Protect confidential financial and supplier information and maintain appropriate records.
• Provide documentation and information for internal and external audits when requested.
• Perform reasonable ad hoc finance and administrative duties as assigned.
Requirements:
REQUIREMENTS:
Minimum Requirements
• Grade 12 / National Senior Certificate, preferably with Accounting or Mathematics.
• A certificate or diploma in Accounting, Bookkeeping, Finance or a related field is advantageous.
• At least two years’ relevant experience in a creditor, accounts payable or finance administration role is preferred.
• Practical experience in high-volume invoice processing, supplier reconciliations and payment preparation.
• Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and accounting or ERP systems; experience with Equip SA and Kerridge is advantageous.
• Working knowledge of basic bookkeeping principles, creditor controls and financial documentation.
Core Competencies
• High numerical accuracy and attention to detail.
• Strong planning, organisation and record-keeping skills.
• Ability to prioritise, meet deadlines and work effectively under pressure.
• Analytical thinking and practical problem-solving ability.
• Clear, professional written and verbal communication.
• Integrity, confidentiality, accountability and reliability.
• Ability to work independently and collaborate across branches and departments.
• Customer- and supplier-service orientation.

Representing a diverse portfolio of the world’s leading passenger, commercial, and emerging electric vehicle brands, our client's dealerships offer an all-inclusive motoring solution—encompassing new and pre-owned vehicle sales, finance and insurance (F&I) services, specialized workshops, aftermarket performance tuning, and genuine parts procurement. Tokai Automotive Replacement Parts Sales Specialist – Counter & Telesales
Position Type: Full-Time, Permanent
Industry: Automotive Sector
Salary: R9,500.00 – R10,500.00 Basic Salary (Negotiable based on experience) + Commission & Benefits
About the Role
On behalf of our client, a reputable leader in the automotive sector, we are seeking an energetic, driven, and knowledgeable Automotive Replacement Parts Sales Specialist to join their dynamic team.
If you have a passion for the automotive industry, a stable work history, and a knack for meeting sales targets, this is the perfect move for your career! You will be responsible for providing an exceptional level of customer service, handling parts sales seamlessly across multiple platforms, and driving branch targets forward.
Key Responsibilities
- Customer Service: Provide an exceptional level of customer service to current and prospective clients to build long-term loyalty and satisfaction.
- Multi-Platform Sales: Handle replacement parts sales seamlessly across counter, online, and telesales channels.
- Parts Identification: Assist customers in understanding product offerings and accurately identify the right solutions for their specific vehicle needs.
- Target Drive: Proactively drive sales and renewals to consistently meet and exceed established branch targets.
Minimum Requirements & Qualifications
- Experience: Proven experience in Automotive Spare Parts Sales is strictly essential.
- Knowledge: Extensive and deep knowledge of vehicle replacement parts is required.
- Work History: A stable employment track record with minimal gaps.
- Traits: High energy, excellent communication skills, and a strong customer-service orientation.
- References: Must be able to supply contactable references from previous employers for verification.
Strict Legal Requirements
Please note that due to the nature of this role, the following criteria are non-negotiable. Background screening will be conducted on all shortlisted candidates.
- Citizenship: Must be a South African-born Citizen with a valid South African ID.
- Criminal Record: Must have a clean criminal background. A person with a criminal record will not be considered.
- Credit History: Must have a clear ITC (financial/credit history) with no judgments or defaults.
Remuneration, Incentives & Benefits
- Basic Salary: R9,500.00 – R10,500.00 per month (Negotiable based on experience).
- Incentives: Commission earned based on reaching branch targets.
- Benefits: Membership in the company Provident Fund and a December Annual Bonus.
Working Hours & Environment
- Standard Hours: Monday to Friday from 08:00 to 17:00, and Saturdays from 08:00 to 13:00.
- Environment: This is strictly a branch-based environment, operating directly on the front sales counter and handling phone-based telesales.
Required Documentation for Application
Please ensure that you submit the following documentation with your application:
- Detailed CV: Must include contactable references clearly reflecting your automotive parts sales history.
- ID Copy: Required as proof of South African born citizenship.
- Qualifications & Certificates: Copies of any relevant industry training or certificates.
How to Apply
If you meet all the strict requirements above and are ready for a new challenge, please submit your updated CV, along with the required documentation listed above, to https://www.easternpersonnel.co.za/click on Register CV.
Please Note: Only shortlisted candidates who meet all requirements, will be contacted. If you do not hear back within two weeks, please consider your application unsuccessful. Eastern Personnel is fully POPIA compliant, and all personal information will be processed securely and solely for recruitment purposes.

• The manager is accountable for maximising cash collections, protecting cash flow, ensuring credit governance, maintaining customer master integrity, managing debtor risk, driving tender compliance and reporting requirements, ensuring credit insurance compliance, leading claims resolution and root-cause analysis, and producing accurate cash collection forecasts while developing a high-performing debtors team.
Minimum Requirements
EDUCATION
• BCom Accounting/Finance
• Credit Management qualification advantageous.
EXPERIENCE
• 6+ years accounts receivable experience.
• 3+ years managing a debtors team.

• Pharmaceutical/FMCG experience preferred.
• Tender customer experience.
• Strong understanding of credit risk management and collections processes
• ERP experience (Sage Evolution or Intacct advantageous).
• Intermediate to advanced Excel.
Key Performance Areas (Core, essential responsibilities –outputs of the position)
• Working Capital & Cash
- Achieve debtors day targets on both private and tender
- Minimise aged debt
- Deliver accurate weekly and monthly collections forecasts.
- Escalate collection risks proactively.
- Drive customer payment term compliance.
• Debtors Governance
- Maintain complete debtor files.
- Ensure credit limits, terms and approvals comply with policy.
- Maintain customer master data integrity.
- Ensure all supporting documentation is electronically retained.
• Tender Administration & Compliance
- Ensure supporting documents such as PODs are submitted timeously
- Visit tender customers regularly and develop strong relationships
- Oversee tender account reconciliations and issue resolution
- Monitor payment cycles and proactively resolve payment delays.
- Ensure monthly Delivery Uploads and Transaction Uploads to RSA Pharma databases are completed
accurately and on time.
- Ensure compliance with all pharmaceutical governance requirements.

- Lead investigation and resolution of pricing, shortages, returns, rebates and deduction claims.
- Reduce aged unresolved claims.
- Perform root-cause analysis and implement controls for prevention of controllable claims issues
• Credit Insurance
- Ensure credit insurance compliance.
- Submit required reporting accurately and on time.
- Monitor insured limits and escalate exposures.

- Build relationships with key customers.
- Lead payment review meetings.
- Resolve disputes quickly.
• Reporting - Aged debt reports. - Cash collection forecasts. - Claims dashboards and clearing
- Statement submissions
- Account reconciliations

• Strong communication and stakeholder engagement skills

about_role:
This is customer centric, multi-skilled role supporting the sales & purchasing departments of this SA subsididary of a large global.  They provide local industrial technology, specializing in compression technology components, gas-powered engine sales and parts, and field maintenance services for the energy and process industries.
Please avoid disappointment and time wastage and review the full job brief carefully before applying.
Your skills and related previous experience should equip you for this role.  It is a combination of hands-on involvement in customer & supplier interaction, sales order processes,  imports and exports control (understanding of incoterms) etc. - see below
In support of French speaking clients it would be wonderful advantage if you were fluent in French, but not essential.
A strong work ethic, performance driven with stable work history are valued attributes.
This closely-knit successful SA team value their people and have an extremely low turnover.
Remuneration - R23-25k neg. gross basic + Excellent benefits i.e., Co. contributes 50% of medical aid up to Discovery Cassic Priority regardless of dependents; Co. contributes up to 10.5% of basic n terms of retirement fund; guaranteed 13th + discretionary additional bonus based on individual & Co.'s performance up to 12% of  annual salary.
Overview - Role requires an individual who communicates effectively with customers, suppliers & colleagues, addresses their concerns and ensures a seamless exerience with their products and services. Strong problem-solving skills & a customer-centric approach is necessary. You would be performing clerical / administrative support duties for the sales & purchasing departments. Prepare & distribute various sales reports when required. Maintain customer & supplier files, assist sales team & handle inquiries about products or services. Project a professional company image through all interactions.
Key Responsibilities:
Customer Interation -  Respond to customer inquiries via phone, email and online channels regarding required services and parts. Check & assist with reviewing internal costings leading to preparing customer quotations.
Supplier Interaction - Obtain RFQ's from suppliers based on customer requirements. Respond to vendor inquiries via phone, email and online channels. Prepare Vendor Purchase Orders, monitor supplier deliveries.
Order Management -  Process customer orders, ensuring accuracy in product specifications, delivery dates, Incoterms and payment details. (Capture orders and goods received notes on relevant systems, eg: SAP/Service Next. Procure spares, co-ordinate deliveries, Raise, send & save documentation.
Import & Export Control - Prepare & collate required documentation and deal with freight forwarders to obtain Import Licenses, enure that correct Inco-terms are being applied.
Issue Resolution - Handle customer complaints or issues, escalating to the appropriate department when necessary, while maintaining a professional and positive demeanor.
Sales Support - Assist with upselling parts, service agreements, and additional products based on customer needs.
Documentation - Maintain accurate records of customer interactions, transactions, inquiries, and complaints in relevant systems.
Collaboration - Work closely with the sales, technical support, and stores teams to ensure timely and accurate delivery of products and services as well as controlling/maintaining stock levels in relation to open sales orders and customer contracts. Liase with the workshop  regarding processing of Job cards/picking lists and production orders.
Follow-up - Proactively follow up on customer satisfaction, order status and any post-purchase support needs.

About the Role
The Product Manager: Managed AI Services is responsible for owning, developing and continuously enhancing Numata's Managed AI Services portfolio as a commercially successful recurring managed service. This role exists to ensure that Numata does not simply resell AI platforms but delivers a differentiated managed service that enables clients to continuously realise business value from Artificial Intelligence. The Product Manager serves as the custodian of the product strategy, roadmap, commercial performance, client adoption, vendor relationships, marketing alignment and service evolution.
The role acts as the central point of coordination between Sales, Marketing, Client Experience, Professional Services, Managed Services, Finance and Technology Partners to ensure one cohesive product experience for both clients and internal stakeholders. This position establishes Numata's Product Management capability and will become the blueprint for future Product Management disciplines across additional strategic service portfolios
Why this Role Matters
Artificial Intelligence is transforming the way organisations operate, with new models, capabilities and business applications emerging at an unprecedented pace. As Numata expands its Managed AI Services portfolio, it is essential that the organisation does more than simply provide access to AI technologies, it must deliver a differentiated, continuously evolving managed service that enables clients to realise measurable business value. Without dedicated product ownership, advancements in AI platforms may not be translated into meaningful client outcomes, resulting in inconsistent product messaging, limited client adoption, outdated marketing, missed sales opportunities and reduced customer engagement. Over time, this creates a significant risk to client retention, recurring revenue and Numata's competitive position in the market.
The Product Manager: Managed AI Services plays a pivotal role in ensuring that the Managed AI portfolio remains commercially successful, strategically aligned and focused on delivering exceptional customer value. This role is responsible for connecting technology innovation with business outcomes by translating vendor developments into compelling service enhancements, client communications, go-to-market initiatives, sales enablement, training and measurable value realisation. Acting as the central point of coordination across Sales, Marketing, Client Experience, Professional Services, Finance and Technology Partners, the Product Manager ensures that all stakeholders work together to deliver one coherent and consistently improving product experience.
As Numata's first dedicated Product Manager, this position also establishes the organisation's Product Management discipline and provides the framework for future product leadership across other strategic service portfolios. Through strong commercial judgement, structured product management and cross-functional leadership, the role will drive client adoption, improve retention, increase recurring revenue, identify expansion opportunities and strengthen Numata's position as a trusted Business Technology Strategist and leader in managed AI services

about_role:
Introduction:
Wembley College is a leading, English Medium, co-educational, independent school situated on a beautiful campus amongst the rolling hills of Greytown in the KwaZulu Natal Midlands.
Description:
Wembley College is a leading, English Medium, co-educational, independent school situated on a beautiful campus amongst the rolling hills of Greytown in the KwaZulu Natal Midlands. An hour from Pietermaritzburg and an hour from Ballito makes for an ideal ‘country school’ within easy striking distance of a Central Business District and the warm KwaZulu Natal coast. RESPONSIBILITIES
You are responsible and accountable for the following:
Aspects of Handling Horses and Ponies at Wembley Equestrian Academy:
• Daily handling of horses and ponies on Academy premises – making use of the ACADEMY’S DESIRED/PRESCRIBED methods to execute and complete tasks allocated by the Academy Manager to the Employee.
• Handling of all horses as required by The Academy, ACCORDING TO THE ACADEMY’S METHODS, STANDARDS AND PRINCIPES of horsemanship.
• Grooming of all horses falling under The Academy’s jurisdiction as requested and required by the Academy INCLUDING, BUT NOT LIMITED TO brushing of body, neck and face, picking up- and cleaning of all four hooves (front and hind feet) maintenance of manes and tails (as required, and meeting Academy standards), cooling down and hosing of horses after their work sessions, meeting Academy standards. Washing/bathing, show turn-out including pulling, plaiting and trimming horses as the need arises on occasion.
• Regularly monitoring The Academy horses’ general- and overall wellbeing INCLUDING, BUT NOT LIMITED TO ANY injuries, cuts, swellings, growths, lameness or discharge noticed/observed whilst handling/working- or coming into contact with whilst on company grounds, AND REPORTING IT TO THE ACADEMY MANAGER IMMEDIATLEY.
• Reporting on any loose or lost shoes of shod horses, and any chips, cracks or damages to unshod horses’ feet whilst handling/working- or coming into contact with whilst on Academy grounds.
• Ensure that ANY horses you are handling/working- or coming into contact with whilst on Academy grounds has access to ample clean water to drink.
• Ensure EVERY safety precaution is taken to facilitate the safety of any horse, handler, rider, bystanders and any other horses in the immediate surrounding vicinity at all times, whilst handling/working- or coming into contact with, whilst on Academy grounds.
Tack and Equipment:
• Responsibly handling, using & packing away of ANY & All horse tack belonging to or being utilized by WEA.
• Maintenance (cleaning and oiling as and when required) of saddles, girths, surcingles, bridles, brushing boots, lunging equipment, numnahs, grooming kits ect.
• Maintenance (cleaning and safeguarding of implements ie. Brush cutters, wheelbarrows, forks, spades, hoes and brooms.)
• Report any damages and/or problems on above mentioned to the Academy Manager immediately.
Stable yard and Surrounds:
• Checking on paddock fences (electrical and wooden) situated at and around your section division, of horses whilst handling/working- or coming into contact with them, on Academy grounds and reporting any concerns, damages or potential problems regarding such immediately to the Academy Manager.
• Report any damages to stables, deterioration or damages to surrounding structures ie lungering, as well as watercrib- hosepipe-, waterpipe and tap leaks to the Academy Manager immediately.
• Keeping stable yard and surrounding areas clean, tidy and presentable at all times. This includes, but is not limited to paddocks, lawns and flowerbeds situated in proximity to your section division.
Duties:
• Feeding of concentrates and roughage to horses on Academy premises, as determined by The Academy, on a daily basis.
• Leading horses to- and from stables and paddocks respectively, as required by The Academy on a daily basis.
• Lunging of horses as per WEA’s requirements.
• Schooling of horses as per WEA’s requirements
• Giving riding tuition to WEA riders as per WEA’s requirements.
• Show turn out and show assistance as per WEA requirements
• Weekend duties as per protocol, and/or determined by the Academy Manager.
Miscellaneous:
• Being timeous at your specific division station of employment agreed upon pertaining to your hours of work between yourself and The Academy.
• Protective clothing in terms of hardhats, brushcutting bibs and protective eye gear (visors) are provided and available to you in hours of work by The Academy. Failure to utilize these items for the benefit of your own safety will then be at your own risk.
• On occasion, you might be required to assist the Academy Manager with regards to holding horses if needed with medical treatments/farrier/vet/physio/inspector visits to and for horses on Academy premises.
• On occasion, you might be required to assist in other section divisions of Wembley College for short periods of time should such a need/situation arise, for whatever reason.
• Ensure you always appear neat, displaying courteous and respectful behavior to your co-workers, superiors as well as clients, riders and visitors at The Academy or when representing the Academy at an away-venue, because you are an Employee of The Academy. As such you are expected to behave within the guidelines of The Academy’s image.

• Be able to speak English or Afrikaans
• 2-3 years experience in an Equine related set up
• Drivers License will be beneficial

Millwright-Cape Winelands
Looking for a trade-tested Millwright to maintain, fault-find, repair and continuously improve the mechanical and electrical equipment throughout our MegaPlant.
This is a hands-on factory-floor role for someone highly efficient, technically proficient, dependable and able to work independently.
We are looking for an artisan who finds the root cause of failures, not someone who simply replaces failed components
Requirments:
• Trade Test Millwright 5–10+ years relevant post-trade experience
• Industrial/Manufacturing maintenance experience.
• Strong mechanical and electrical fault-finding ability.
• Able to work efficiently with minimal supervision.
• Able to read mechanical and electrical drawings.
• Strong practical problem-solving ability.
• High standard of workmanship and safety.
• Comfortable working in a heavy industrial factory environment.
Strong experience with:
• Motors, gearboxes, bearings and couplings.
• Shaft, pulley and drive alignment.
• Conveyors, belts, chains and sprockets.
• Crushers, screens, mixers and production machinery.
• Pumps, fans and rotating equipment.
• Hydraulics and pneumatics.
• Fabrication and welding.
• Three-phase electrical systems.
• MCCs, contactors and overloads.
• Variable Speed Drives (VSDs).
• Sensors, limit switches and interlocks.
• Basic PLC fault finding and PLC I/O.
• Automated production equipment.
Key Responsibilities
• Respond rapidly and efficiently to production breakdowns.
• Diagnose mechanical, electrical, control and process-related faults.
• Identify and correct the root cause of failures.
• Carry out preventative and planned maintenance.
• Inspect machinery proactively and identify developing problems.
• Ensure correct bearing installation, alignment, lubrication and equipment mounting.
• Test equipment properly before returning it to production.
• Record significant failures and corrective actions.
• Identify critical spare-part requirements.
• Support shutdowns and major maintenance work.
Continuous Improvement
• Our Millwrights are expected to improve the factory, not simply maintain it.
• They should actively identify opportunities to:
• Reduce repetitive breakdowns.
• Increase plant availability and production throughput.
• Reduce maintenance costs.
• Improve equipment reliability.
• Improve electrical and mechanical efficiency.
• Reduce unnecessary motor loading and power consumption.
• Improve guarding, safety and maintainability.
• Improve sensors, controls and automation.

job_title: Head of Amazon Advertising & Performance Marketing
about_role:
Head of Amazon Advertising & Performance Marketing
Location: Remote (Preference for Western / Western-aligned time zones)
Type: Full-Time
Reports to: CEO
Compensation: Top-decile base + aggressive profit-based upside
The Role – In One Sentence
You are the money engine on Amazon.
You own every dollar that comes in the door through Amazon PPC/DSP and retail media — and you know exactly how to turn ad spend into profitable, compounding growth. No excuses, no "seasonality," no "the algorithm changed."
Amazon is your home field. Other channels are tools you wield to support it.
First 90 Days – Non-Negotiable Outcomes
If this doesn't excite you as a challenge, this isn't your role.
• Full Amazon Audit – Nothing Unchecked
• Sponsored Products, Sponsored Brands, Sponsored Display, DSP
• Campaign structure, keyword targeting, audience segmentation, placements
• Listing quality: titles, bullets, images, A+ content, reviews, pricing, bundles
Result: full teardown with clear kill/scale/rebuild plan.
• New Testing Machine Live (Amazon-First)
• Minimum 20 new tests/week across: keywords, bids, creatives, angles, funnels, audiences
• Systematic framework for A/B testing and rapid iteration
• Clear "what we test / why we test / how we decide" playbook
• Amazon Profitability Benchmarks Hit or Clearly Tracked Toward
• Target TACoS, ACOS, and blended ROAS defined and tracked
• Path to 3.5x+ blended ROAS across Amazon
• $50k+/month in controlled, profitable ad spend (or ready to scale to that level sustainably)
• Founder Independence
• Zero reliance on the CEO for copy, angles, hooks, or approvals
• You bring the ideas, tests, and decisions — Founder stays in vision and product, not ads. What You Own
You are Head of Amazon Ads, but you understand the whole growth ecosystem.
Amazon – Your Core Battlefield
• Amazon PPC: Sponsored Products, Sponsored Brands, Sponsored Display
• Keyword research, search term mining, and negative keyword strategy
• Campaign architecture (structure for scale, not chaos)
• Bid strategies (down-only, up/down, fixed bids, placement adjustments)
• TACoS/ACOS optimization and margin protection
• Launch strategy for new products, variants, and bundles Conversion & Creative
• Listing optimization: titles, bullets, imagery, A+ content, brand store
• Review strategy, social proof, and UGC alignment with Amazon page assets
• Creative strategy for Amazon ads (thumbnails, video, lifestyle, comparison ads)
• Angle and hook testing: performance-driven storytelling specifically for Amazon shoppers Cross-Channel Support (Performance Marketing)
• Using TikTok selectively where they support Amazon growth
• LTV/CAC modeling across channels with Amazon as the core revenue driver Measurement & Economics
• LTV/CAC and payback windows on Amazon-first journeys
• Blended ROAS across Amazon and supporting channels
• Reporting that the CEO can scan in 5 minutes and know exactly what's working You don't just "run ads." You design the acquisition system that scales profitably.
Mandatory Prerequisites – No Exceptions
We will check. This is not a "figure it out as you go" seat.
• You have personally scaled Amazon advertising profitably for a CPG/supplement or similar product brand.
• Not agency "I advised" fluff. Actual ownership of P&L outcomes.
• You can point to real brands, real spend, real results.
• You have taken a brand from weak returns (under 2x ROAS / unprofitable TACoS) to strong performance (4x+ ROAS or materially improved TACoS) in under 6–9 months.
• Before/after numbers and what you changed.
• You still run accounts yourself.
• No "I just manage the team now" distance.
• You're in the platforms, making decisions, and testing ideas.
• You can look at a search term report, listing, or ad creative and have a strong POV in under 30 seconds.
• Pattern recognition from heavy reps, not vibes. How You'll Be Judged
This is a scoreboard role. You will live and die by the numbers:
• Blended ROAS across Amazon and supporting channels
• Amazon TACoS and ACOS by product line
• New customer CAC (Amazon-first and blended)
• Margin after ad spend (not just top-line hero screenshots)
• Speed of learning – a new winning angle or structure every 7–14 days If you need "more time" and "more budget" before you can show results, this will be a painful role. If you love moving fast and pressure-testing your ideas, you'll thrive.
How to Apply
Send your CV + a short Loom video.
In your Loom (5–7 minutes), answer:
• Biggest Amazon (or Amazon-led) turnaround you've ever led — what was the monthly spend, TACoS/ROAS before vs. after, and what levers you pulled.
• Current training routine + proof you live it — show us how you train, compete, or otherwise live the athlete lifestyle.
• One Amazon angle, structure, or campaign strategy you'd test for a fast-growing supplement/CPG brand tomorrow — and why. This is not a "VP of Marketing" vanity title.
This is the Head of Amazon Growth in a brand that intends to dominate its category and expects its acquisition leader to think — and operate — like an owner.
Apply only if you're ready to own the numbers end to end.
I also swapped the × symbols for plain x, since those are the next most likely thing a form chokes on.

about_role:
ROLE PURPOSE
The Senior Property Portfolio Manager is responsible for the strategic and operational management of an allocated portfolio of industrial properties, ensuring optimal financial performance, tenant satisfaction, regulatory compliance and service delivery.
The role is responsible for maximising portfolio returns, driving profitability, managing leasing and new business opportunities, overseeing property operations and maintenance, and leading the property management team. The incumbent will build and maintain strong relationships with clients, tenants, brokers, service providers and other key stakeholders while identifying opportunities to grow the managed portfolio.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
Portfolio & Property Management
• Manage an allocated portfolio of industrial properties to ensure effective, efficient and commercially sound operations.
• Maximise portfolio performance, profitability and returns for clients.
• Oversee day-to-day property management, administration and service delivery.
• Monitor property conditions and ensure appropriate maintenance and repairs are undertaken.
• Oversee planned and reactive maintenance programmes.
• Manage service contractors and ensure service contracts are aligned with property requirements.
• Conduct and oversee regular property inspections and ensure identified issues are resolved.
• Oversee tenant installations and ensure projects are completed according to agreed specifications and timeframes.
• Ensure compliance with the Occupational Health and Safety Act and other applicable statutory requirements.
• Maintain accurate property records, documentation and administration.
Financial Management & Budgeting
• Develop and manage property income and expense budgets.
• Monitor actual income and expenditure against approved budgets.
• Identify opportunities to optimise income and control costs.
• Monitor rental income and outstanding rent rolls, implementing corrective action where required.
• Monitor and provide input into financial performance and property management reporting.
• Oversee relevant financial and administrative processes relating to the portfolio.
Leasing & Tenant Management
• Manage leasing activities, including prospecting, canvassing, negotiations and conclusion of deals.
• Develop and implement strategies to maintain sustainable occupancy and income streams.
• Manage tenant relationships and address tenant requirements effectively.
• Negotiate lease agreements within approved mandates and frameworks.
• Ensure lease agreements and related documentation are accurate, complete and properly administered.
• Monitor tenant retention, replacement and new tenant opportunities.
• Ensure tenant installations are coordinated effectively and delivered within agreed specifications and timeframes.
• Maintain strong relationships with tenants, brokers and other stakeholders.
New Business Development
• Identify and evaluate new properties and business opportunities in line with organisational strategy.
• Develop and maintain a comprehensive prospect database.
• Proactively pursue new business opportunities to expand the managed portfolio.
• Prepare and deliver professional pitches, proposals, deal analyses and financial evaluations.
• Develop tailored presentations and proposals for prospective clients.
• Negotiate and conclude management agreements and mandates with new clients.
• Build and maintain strong relationships with prospective and existing clients.
Stakeholder & Relationship Management
• Develop and maintain effective relationships with clients, tenants, brokers, service providers, contractors and other stakeholders.
• Negotiate effectively with internal and external stakeholders to achieve optimal outcomes.
• Liaise with local government and relevant authorities on property-related matters.
• Participate in business and property-related forums to promote the organisation and its services.
• Support relevant community and corporate social responsibility initiatives.
• Represent the organisation professionally in property and industry-related engagements.
Team Leadership & People Management
• Lead and manage the property management team to achieve operational and financial objectives.
• Manage employee performance, development and training.
• Ensure team members have the required skills and competencies to perform their roles effectively.
• Address performance issues promptly and appropriately.
• Promote a positive working environment and a culture aligned with organisational values.
• Drive continuous improvement and professional development within the team.
Compliance, Risk & Administration
•  Ensure compliance with applicable property legislation, regulations and organisational policies.
• Maintain awareness of statutory requirements, including OHS, POPIA, FICA and relevant labour legislation.
• Ensure appropriate record keeping and administration across the portfolio.
• Monitor compliance with lease agreements, service contracts and property-related requirements.
• Identify and manage operational and property-related risks.
• Ensure accurate reporting and documentation across the portfolio.

Introduction
Komatsu South Africa is seeking a Senior Administrator: GRF Support to provide comprehensive administrative support for retail funding operations by facilitating customer financing applications, supporting credit control activities, ensuring compliance with legislative and company requirements, and maintaining accurate financial and customer records. The role contributes to efficient processing of customer finance transactions and supports effective risk management and debt collection activities.
Key Responsibilities
1. Retail Funding Administration
• Assist with the preparation and administration of customer financing applications.
• Gather and verify transaction information from internal stakeholders.
• Capture and maintain customer information on relevant systems.
• Prepare finance quotations, agreements, and schedules.
• Distribute transaction documentation to customers and follow up on outstanding paperwork.
• Scan, file, and maintain customer and transaction records in accordance with company procedures.
• Liaise with internal departments to facilitate invoicing and transaction processing.
2. Payment and Payout Administration
• Prepare payment documentation for approval.
• Capture and allocate payments accurately and timeously.
• Ensure all payments comply with company policies and legislative requirements.
• Verify that approved payments are successfully received by intended beneficiaries.
• Update system records with payment information and supporting documentation.
3. Credit Control
• Monitor customer accounts and age analyses.
• Follow up on overdue accounts and outstanding invoices.
• Identify and escalate bad debt risks and payment issues.
• Implement debtor order holds for overdue or over-limit accounts.
• Process credit notes and maintain debtor records.
• Issue customer statements, reconciliations, invoices, and related correspondence.
• Support the processing of credit applications received from business units.
4. Monitoring and Compliance
• Ensure adherence to Komatsu Africa Holdings Finance (KAfH) policies and procedures.
• Support audit preparation activities and provide required documentation.
• Monitor data integrity and accuracy of customer records.
• Ensure confidentiality of customer and financial information.
• Verify completeness and accuracy of supporting transaction documents.
5. Reporting
• Prepare monthly and ad hoc reports for management.
• Assist with reporting on funding metrics, performance statistics, and account status.
• Escalate discrepancies, risks, and compliance concerns to management.

Reports To Head of Finance
PURPOSE OF THE ROLE:
To lead the company's procurement function: manage the sourcing, purchasing, contracting and supplier-performance cycle in line with the approved procurement procedure, financial controls, budgets and Head of Finance/Group Operations Director instructions.
The Procurement Manager is the primary point of contact between the company and its suppliers of goods, services and capital items, and is accountable for cost-effective, quality-assured and timely procurement that supports manufacturing output.
DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:
Manage purchases and costs in accordance with financial controls, procurement procedures, approved budgets and board / Group instructions.
Cultivate and maintain good working relationships with suppliers, service providers and contractors.
Resolve vendor or contractor grievances and claims against suppliers.
Review the selected strategic suppliers / service providers on their supply, delivery and pricing, in accordance with prescribed procurement procedures.
Negotiate costs and best pricing for purchases made, whilst ensuring quality of goods and services procured.
Maintain and update the Approved Suppliers List (ASL) and their certification / accreditation, delivery times, and potential future development.
Work with all Heads of Department to prioritise procurement of supplies effectively and timeously against the production plan.
Represent the Company and annually review suppliers' agreements or contracts to ensure compliance to contracts, terms of supply and company policies.
Develop and implement purchase and contract management instructions, policies and procedures.
Participate in the development and specifications for equipment, products or substitute materials where applicable, in conjunction with engineering and production.
Maintain the integrity of the financial / ERP accounting system (e.g. Evolution) in terms of pricing, costing and supplier terms.
Ensure the storeroom is sufficiently stocked with minimum stock levels as per agreed levels, and that replenishment is planned and ordered in good time.
Prepare, issue and adjudicate Requests for Quotation (RFQs) and Requests for Proposal (RFPs) for both local and international supply;
Manage import and export logistics, customs clearance (SARS), foreign-exchange exposure and cross-border supplier compliance (including inbound and outbound documentation, certificates of origin and SADC / EU / Asia origin rules);
Evaluate quotations on price, quality, BBBEE, lead-time and total cost of ownership; recommend awards within the delegation of authority.
Compile and submit weekly and monthly procurement reports to the Group Operations Director: spend, cost-savings, supplier performance, open POs and aged creditors.
Drive continuous improvement of the procurement function: cost-savings initiatives, supplier-development programmes, process automation and full compliance with the Business Management System,
AUTHORITY:
Recommend and approve supplier awards, contract renewals and Approved Suppliers List additions/removals within the procurement delegation of authority; escalate to the Group Operations Director as required.
Authority to instruct the staff responsible for inventory counts to perform re-counts if necessary.
Authority to manage import / export logistics, customs clearance, foreign-exchange transactions and cross-border supplier compliance within the procurement delegation of authority; escalate material FX exposure and customs disputes to the Group Operations Director.
Recommend and approve inventory adjustments, strategic sourcing decisions and supplier development support within the delegation of authority; escalate to the Group Operations Director as required.
To Identify and report potential risks and opportunities in accordance with the Company's ERMF policy. Report proposals to Group Operations Director

Job Purpose:
The Receiving Clerk is responsible for the accurate receipt, inspection and recording of all incoming goods delivered to the warehouse. This role ensures that all stock received matches purchase orders and supplier documentation, is inspected for quantity and quality, and is processed promptly into the system. The Receiving Clerk plays a key role in maintaining inventory accuracy and ensuring a smooth flow of goods from receiving through to storage.
Key Responsibilities:
Receiving Goods:
Receive all inbound deliveries from suppliers, transport companies and inter-branch transfers.
Verify deliveries against Purchase Orders (POs), delivery notes and packing lists.
Ensure correct quantities, product codes, batch numbers and descriptions are received.
Check all goods for visible damage, shortages, overages or quality defects.
Report discrepancies immediately to the Receiving Supervisor or Management.
Ensure all received goods are unloaded safely and efficiently.
Documentation Control:
Complete Goods Received Notes (GRNs) accurately and timeously.
Verify supplier documentation before sending for processing.
File receiving documentation according to company procedures.
Maintain accurate receiving records.
Stock Identification & Labelling:
Ensure all received stock is correctly labelled where required.
Verify product  item codes, batch numbers and expiry dates.
Attach internal warehouse labels when applicable.
Ensure products are correctly identified before put-away.
Quality & Inspection:
Perform visual inspections of incoming goods.
Identify damaged, incorrect or poor-quality products.
Segregate damaged or quarantined stock accordingly.
Report quality concerns immediately to Receiving Supervisor.
Inventory Accuracy:
Ensure accurate stock quantities are recorded during receiving.
Investigate and report receiving discrepancies.
Assist with inventory reconciliations relating to received stock.
Support cycle counts and annual stock takes when required.
Maintain high levels of inventory accuracy.
Warehouse Operations:
Assist with directing machinery and warehouse staff during unloading.
Ensure received goods are staged correctly for put-away.
Maintain an organized receiving area.
Coordinate with Inventory staff regarding stock put-away priorities.
Assist with internal stock transfers where required.
Health, Safety & Housekeeping:
Ensure all receiving staff are wearing required Personal Protective Equipment (PPE).
Ensure safe unloading practices are followed.
Keep receiving areas clean, organized and free from hazards.
Report unsafe conditions, incidents or damaged equipment immediately.
Communication:
Communicate effectively with suppliers, drivers and warehouse personnel.
Liaise with Procurement, Inventory and Warehouse teams regarding receiving issues.
Notify management of urgent shortages or damaged deliveries.
Provide accurate feedback on receiving progress.
General Support:
Assist all your colleagues and other departments when required.
Perform any adhoc duties as assigned by your Supervisors or Managers.

About Wholechain
Wholechain is a supply chain traceability platform that makes product journeys transparent,
helping responsible businesses meet regulatory, customer, and sustainability expectations. Built
on global data standards such as GS1 and GDST, Wholechain supports complex,
multi-commodity supply chains across food, agriculture, and consumer goods industries. The
platform enables interoperable, event-based, and lot-level traceability across suppliers,
processors, distributors, logistics providers, retailers, foodservice operators, and certification
bodies worldwide.
Wholechain helps organizations capture, share, and validate critical supply chain data across
sourcing, transformation, shipping, receiving, and production events. By creating a connected
digital chain of custody, businesses can improve food safety, strengthen recall readiness, verify
sourcing claims, meet ESG and sustainability goals, and comply with evolving regulatory
frameworks such as FDA FSMA 204 and international traceability requirements.
The platform is designed for enterprise scalability and integration, supporting APIs, EDI
workflows, ERP integrations, and interoperability with external traceability and certification
ecosystems. Wholechain works closely with industry groups, standards organizations, seafood
and agriculture partners, retailers, and global suppliers to simplify traceability adoption without
requiring all participants to use the same internal systems.
In addition to regulatory compliance, Wholechain enables businesses to build trust and
operational visibility throughout their supply networks. Customers use the platform to manage
traceability programs, verify certified products, monitor supply chain integrity, support

The Civil Engineer provides oversight of civil infrastructure across the 128-site South Africa portfolio. The position is responsible for the structural integrity, inspection, maintenance planning, and standards compliance of all civil works — elevated reinforced-concrete reservoirs, tank towers, distribution networks, standpipes, pump houses, borehole chambers, cattle troughs, and solar frame structures — and for coordinating specialist chartered engineering inspections of high-capacity 30-kilolitre tank-class infrastructure in accordance with applicable SANS standards.
The role is central to the Year 1 technical condition assessment of all 128 sites, the site-tier triage (A/B/C), the remediation of named Tier C sites, and the drawdown planning of the Replacement Capex Reserve for civil components.
3. Key Responsibilities
3.1 Technical condition assessment and site-tier triage (Year 1)
• Lead the civil and structural component of the site-by-site technical condition assessment across all 128 South African sites within the first three months of the programme (Stream B of the Day 1 transition), covering tanks, towers, distribution networks, valves and fittings, pump houses, and civil structures.
• Contribute civil condition data to the site-tier triage (Tier A/B/C) to be confirmed by Month 3 and identify civil components requiring Day 1 or Year 1 replacement funded from the Replacement Capex Reserve.
• Support full condition assessment and Tier C remediation at the named priority sites, including Jabulani and the five untested Mpumalanga sites (Igliton Hotel Section, Igliton Mdluli Section, Mihlanguleni, Rhandzekile A, Rhandzekile B), under the 48-hour remediation initiation protocol.
• Verify and reconcile the civil elements of the Innovation: Africa handover package, including as-built and structural drawings (3m, 7m, and 10m tank towers; the 30-kilolitre high-capacity tank class), borehole completion reports, and site asset registers.3.2 Routine civil inspection and maintenance oversight (Years 1-3)
• Design and implement the routine structural inspection cycle for civil infrastructure across the portfolio, integrated into the Tier 2 quarterly inspection programme (structural inspection of concrete towers, reservoirs, and distribution infrastructure).
• Procure, scope, and supervise specialist-chartered engineering inspections of 30-kilolitre reinforced-concrete tanks in compliance with applicable SANS standards, managing the specialist sub-contract and certifying deliverables.
• Develop civil maintenance specifications, bills of quantities, and scopes of work for repairs, rehabilitation, and upgrades; supervise contractors and certify completed works.
• Assess and prioritise Parent-site civil infrastructure within the cluster maintenance model, recognising that a Parent borehole failure cascades to hydraulically dependent Child sites (56 Child sites in South Africa).
• Support reactive repair response for civil failures in line with the tiered service-impact protocol (critical failures within 48 hours; reduced-service issues within five working days).3.3 Standards compliance, quality assurance and reporting
• Ensure all civil works, inspections, and rehabilitation comply with applicable SANS standards and relevant national and municipal regulations, and that water infrastructure supports compliance with SANS 241:2015 water quality requirements.
• Maintain the civil asset register, structural inspection records, drawings library, and defect logs within the programme's field management system.
• Contribute civil infrastructure data and analysis to monthly cluster reports, quarterly donor reports to Donor, and the MEAL dashboard (KPI Categories 1 and 2: sustained service delivery and technical compliance).
• Support the DMEAL team with means-of-verification documentation for infrastructure-related KPIs.3.4 Capacity building and transition
• Train ForAfrika field engineers, community pump attendants, and Water Management Committee members in basic civil infrastructure surveillance (visual inspection of tanks, towers, standpipes, and soakaways) as part of the Tier 1 community operator curriculum.
• Contribute civil O&M content to site-level O&M manuals, sustainability plans, and handover documentation supporting the Year 3 transition to community and Water Services Authority management.
• Advise on civil aspects of Capital Sinking Fund calibration, aligning contribution rates to civil component lifecycles (10/20-year classes).3.5 Stakeholder engagement
• Liaise with the Department of Water and Sanitation (DWS), provincial Water Services Authorities (Ehlanzeni DM, Greater Tzaneen, Makhado, uMkhanyakude DM), and municipal engineers on infrastructure standards, co-maintenance arrangements, and cost-sharing Service Level Agreement negotiations.
• Coordinate with DWS-listed certified solar technical partners and Mvula Borehole Drilling (Pty) Ltd to ensure integrated electromechanical and civil maintenance delivery.
• Represent ForAfrika in technical forums and site meetings with government, communities, and Innovation: Africa counterparts during the transition period.
4. Qualifications and Experience
Essential
• Bachelor’s degree in civil engineering (BEng/BSc Eng) from a recognised institution.
• Registration with the Engineering Council of South Africa (ECSA) as a Candidate Engineer, with Professional Engineer (Pr Eng) or Professional Engineering Technologist (Pr Tech Eng) registration strongly preferred.
• Minimum five (5) years of progressive experience in civil/structural engineering for water supply infrastructure — reservoirs, elevated tanks, pipelines, and rural water schemes.
• Demonstrated working knowledge of SANS standards applicable to water infrastructure (including SANS 241:2015 and structural/civil codes for reinforced-concrete water-retaining structures).
• Proven experience in condition assessment, structural inspection, and rehabilitation of water-retaining structures.
• Experience preparing scopes of work, bills of quantities, and supervising contractors.
• Valid driver's licence and willingness to travel extensively (up to 60%) to remote rural sites across three provinces.Desirable
• MSc/MEng in Civil, Structural, or Water Engineering.
• Experience in the NGO/development sector or donor-funded WASH programmes.
• Familiarity with solar-powered water systems, borehole infrastructure, and rural water utility operations.
• Experience engaging municipal Water Services Authorities and DWS regulatory frameworks (Water Services Act, including Section 19 Water Service Intermediary arrangements).
• Proficiency in AutoCAD/Civil 3D, EPANET or equivalent hydraulic modelling tools, and GIS applications.
• Proficiency in one or more of IsiZulu, Sepedi, or Siswati is an advantage.

job_title: Senior Substation Primary Plant Design Engineer
about_role:
Our client is seeking a highly experienced Senior Substation Primary Plant Design Engineer to lead the delivery of complex transmission and distribution substation projects. This opportunity is ideal for a technically accomplished engineer with extensive experience in high-voltage substation design, strong leadership capabilities, and a proven track record delivering projects up to 400kV. Experience on 765kV projects will be highly advantageous.
Key Responsibilities
• Lead the preliminary, conceptual, detailed design, and construction support for high-voltage substation projects.
• Prepare and review conceptual designs, technical specifications, bills of quantities, and tender documentation.
• Develop detailed primary plant designs for transmission and distribution substations.
• Review contractor designs and ensure compliance with project specifications and applicable standards.
• Provide technical leadership throughout project execution, construction support, testing, and commissioning.
• Participate in design reviews, FATs, SATs, site inspections, and commissioning activities.
• Prepare technical reports, engineering calculations, project methodologies, schedules, and budgets.
• Liaise with clients, contractors, utilities, and multidisciplinary engineering teams.
• Mentor junior engineers and contribute to the ongoing development of the engineering team.
• Ensure compliance with SHEQ requirements and industry best practices.
Minimum Requirements
• BSc or BEng in Electrical Engineering or a related discipline.
• Professional registration with ECSA or an internationally recognised engineering institution.
• Minimum of 15 years' experience in substation design within transmission and distribution environments.
• Extensive experience delivering detailed substation primary plant designs up to 400kV.
• Experience on 765kV substation projects will be highly advantageous.
• Strong knowledge of Eskom standards, IEC, IEEE, NRS, and SANS requirements.
• Experience working within utilities, EPC contractors, or engineering consulting environments.
Advantageous Experience
• Exposure to renewable energy grid connection projects.
• Proficiency with engineering software such as AutoCAD, EPLAN, DigSilent, ETAP, PowerFactory, or PSSE.
• Strong understanding of transmission infrastructure and high-voltage engineering.
Key Competencies
• Excellent technical leadership and engineering judgement.
• Strong client relationship management and communication skills.
• Ability to manage multiple projects within demanding schedules.
• Commitment to quality, safety, and engineering excellence.

• Perseverance.
