🚀 We're Hiring: Assistant Accountant
📍 Location: Johannesburg
📊 Reporting Line: Financial Reporting Manager
💼 Function: Finance — Assistant Accountant
💼 Job Purpose
To administer the Lesaka POS rental billing and collections cycle, support general accounting activities, and perform assigned SOX compliance controls. The role ensures accurate rental records, secure processing of merchant information, reliable accounting support and complete audit evidence.
🔍 Key Responsibility Areas
💰 Rentals
• Prepare monthly rental debit-order upload files by extracting, cleansing and validating CRM data.
• Capture monthly and recurring rental invoices.
• Verify banking details, signed mandates, accepted terms and applicable grace periods before processing.
• Process, capture and match collected debit orders to debtor accounts and accounting records.
• Maintain the Master Rental File as the accurate record of active agreements, changes, new management and decommissioned outlets.
• Process threshold exclusions and ensure only eligible merchants are included in rental pay runs.
• Coordinate payment reminders, rental queries and collections activity with merchants, internal teams and third-party collection agents.
• Process bad-debt write-offs relating to incorrect banking details and decommissioned outlets in accordance with approved procedures.
• Calculate and record doubtful-debt provisions for failed debit orders.
• Perform monthly reconciliations of rental revenue, rental receivables, bad debts and doubtful-debt provisions.
• Reconcile rental information across CRM, Xero and supporting agreements, escalating discrepancies promptly.
• Protect merchant banking and personal information in line with POPIA and internal security requirements.
📊 Other Accounting Functions
• Process and verify supplier invoices for payment and load approved purchase orders in the ERP system.
• Prepare and execute weekly payment proposals in the ERP system.
• Provide accounts payable administration support and ensure supplier payments are accurate and made on time.
• Match payments to accounting records and reconcile supplier statements, resolving discrepancies promptly.
• Raise customer invoices and prepare monthly customer statements.
• Follow up with customers on overdue payments and assist with collections activity.
• Investigate and resolve customer account queries and follow up on reconciling items.
• Reconcile cashbooks, maintain supporting records and resolve discrepancies.
• Support month-end close by preparing and reviewing assigned financial records and schedules.
• Assist with age-analysis, write-off and collections information as required.
🛡️ SOX Compliance Activities
• Perform assigned SOX controls in accordance with documented procedures and frequencies.
• Complete control coversheets and retain clear supporting evidence, including preparer and reviewer sign-off.
• Validate information produced by the entity and information used in controls, including CRM extracts, Power BI reports, Xero data, reconciliations and master data files.
• Maintain controlled Excel working files and templates, including formula integrity, version control, access protection and review evidence.
• Archive source data, final files and audit evidence in approved locations.
• Identify and escalate control exceptions, late performance and evidence gaps to Finance management and relevant SOX stakeholders.
🎓 Experience & Qualifications
Minimum Qualification
• Matric / Grade 12 is essential.
• A diploma or certificate in Finance, Accounting, Bookkeeping or Business Administration is advantageous.
Minimum Experience
• Two to three years’ experience in finance administration, billing, collections or accounting support.
• Experience with recurring billing or debit-order cycles and fixed monthly deadlines.
• Strong Excel skills, including lookups, conditional formatting, data cleansing and de-duplication.
• Experience with CRM and accounting systems; Microsoft Dynamics and Xero are advantageous.
• Exposure to SOX controls, audit evidence or a controlled finance environment is advantageous.
🧠 Key Skills & Attributes
• High attention to detail and commitment to accuracy.
• Strong planning, organisation and deadline management.
• Analytical problem-solving and reconciliation skills.
• Clear communication and effective stakeholder coordination.
• Integrity and discretion when handling confidential financial information.
• Ability to work independently and perform reliably under pressure.

Main Responsibilities – Regional Activation & Market Execution
The Regional Marketing Specialist Africa is responsible for the regional activation of the company's marketing strategy, ensuring marketing activities contribute to funnel generation, brand visibility, and the roll-out of regional marketing deliverables in line with agreed strategy and budgets.
The successful candidate must have native-level English proficiency.
The Africa office is located in Umhlanga, South Africa. Office presence is required (minimum 2 days per week). Occasional travel across Africa for events, meetings and visits to the Casablanca office in Morocco is also required. The role reports to the Head of Marketing and Communications EMEA.
The Regional Marketing Specialist Africa comprises of 4 main areas:
1. Event Management
End-to-end planning, coordination, and execution of regional events aligned with the company's marketing strategy and commercial priorities.
This includes:
- Trade shows and exhibitions
- Industry seminars and technical events
- Company-hosted customer and industry events
- Distributor and partner events in company offices or at partner sites
- Technical webinars (native or in cooperation with partners)
Responsibilities include management and delivery of the event KPIs, coordination with internal stakeholders and/or partners, brand messaging, and post-event reporting to ensure activities contribute to the region's sales opportunity funnel.

Generation, activation, monitoring and analysis of marketing activities executed jointly with channel partners and distributors. These initiatives may include:
- Sponsorships

- Co-branded literature and promotional assets
- Videos and webinars
- Media packs
- Promotional merchandising
- Other co-op marketing initiatives agreed with partners

Localisation and activation of central marketing campaigns within the region's markets, as well as development and execution of targeted regional initiatives. This includes:
- Activation of global or central marketing campaigns in the region
- Regional campaign activation ("market-making")
- Influencer collaboration and management
- Vertical Media & PR activation
- Regional newsletters, case studies, videos, and market research initiatives designed to increase brand awareness, reach and relevance within the region.

- Monitoring marketing activity, performance and ROI

- Coordinating with central marketing teams and commercial stakeholders to ensure alignment with strategy and budgets

Digital marketing, website management, design, and social media channel management are handled by the central marketing team. Regional Marketing Specialists will provide regional content as relevant. Senior Credit Risk Analyst - PayJustNow
Purpose of the role:
This role exists to turn fragmented data into profitable lending decisions. The business originates credit across two very different products — a high-volume, thin-margin, short-tenor BNPL book and a longer-dated retail instalment loan book — and the data that should inform those decisions currently sits in silos: bureau feeds in one system, transactional and behavioural data in another, merchant and collections data elsewhere again.
The Senior Credit Risk & Decision Scientist is accountable for three connected outcomes:
• Data optimisation across silos — building a single, governed, decision-ready view of the customer by integrating bureau, internal and alternative data sources, and eliminating duplicated or unused data spend.
• Scorecard build and monitoring — developing, validating, deploying and continuously monitoring application, behavioural, affordability and collections scorecards across both product lines.
• Account origination — designing and optimising the end-to-end origination decision engine: policy rules, cut-offs, limit assignment, affordability assessment, fraud screening and champion/challenger strategy.Success is measured commercially. The role is expected to demonstrably improve risk-adjusted return — higher approval rates at constant or lower loss, lower cost of data acquisition, and faster decisioning — not simply to produce models.
Key Responsibilities:
Data Optimization across business silo's:
• Map the full credit data estate across origination, servicing, collections, merchant/partner and marketing systems; document lineage, ownership, refresh cadence, quality and cost of every source.
• Design and own a consolidated credit data mart / feature store that serves modelling, decisioning and reporting from a single set of definitions, removing conflicting versions of the same metric.
• Integrate and rationalise the three data families the business depends on:
• Bureau data — scores, enquiry data, tradeline and payment-profile history, adverse and judgment data, affordability indicators.
• Internal data — application, transactional, repayment and arrears behaviour, customer tenure, cross-product holdings, merchant and basket-level data, servicing and contact history.
• Alternative data — bank transaction / open-banking data, device and digital footprint, telco and payment-behaviour signals, geospatial and psychometric indicators where lawful and predictive.
• Run a continuous cost-to-value assessment of every paid external data source: quantify incremental lift per Rand of bureau or alternative-data spend and retire, renegotiate or re-sequence calls that do not pay for themselves.
• Implement tiered / cascaded data-call strategies so expensive attributes are only purchased where they change the decision.
• Define and enforce data quality standards, reconciliation controls and monitoring for all decision-critical feeds; own the resolution path when a feed degrades or a bureau attribute drifts.
• Partner with Data Engineering to productionise pipelines, and with Product and Finance so that a single agreed set of risk and profitability metrics is used across the business.Scorecard Development:
• Own the full model lifecycle for application, behavioural, affordability, fraud-propensity and collections scorecards across BNPL and retail loan portfolios.
• Construct reliable modelling samples: target definition, performance and outcome windows, exclusions, reject inference, and correction for the short performance windows and rapid repeat-usage cycles typical of BNPL.
• Engineer and select features from bureau, internal and alternative sources; apply appropriate binning, WoE/IV analysis, segmentation and multicollinearity treatment.
• Build models using the right tool for the job — logistic regression and scorecard scaling where explainability and regulatory defensibility are required; gradient boosting and other machine-learning techniques where lift justifies them, supported by explainability output (SHAP or equivalent).
• Validate rigorously: out-of-time and out-of-sample testing, Gini/KS/AUC, calibration, stability, segment-level performance and fairness/disparate-impact testing.
• Produce model documentation to internal model-risk and audit standard, and present models to the Credit or Model Risk Committee for approval if needed.
• Support deployment into the decision engine and sign off implementation testing — confirming that the scored production population matches the development specification, attribute for attribute.Scorecard monitoring and model governance:
• Own the full model lifecycle for application, behavioural, affordability, fraud-propensity and collections scorecards across BNPL and retail loan portfolios.
• Construct reliable modelling samples: target definition, performance and outcome windows, exclusions, reject inference, and correction for the short performance windows and rapid repeat-usage cycles typical of BNPL.
• Engineer and select features from bureau, internal and alternative sources; apply appropriate binning, WoE/IV analysis, segmentation and multicollinearity treatment.
• Build models using the right tool for the job — logistic regression and scorecard scaling where explainability and regulatory defensibility are required; gradient boosting and other machine-learning techniques where lift justifies them, supported by explainability output (SHAP or equivalent).
• Validate rigorously: out-of-time and out-of-sample testing, Gini/KS/AUC, calibration, stability, segment-level performance and fairness/disparate-impact testing.
• Produce model documentation to internal model-risk and audit standard, and present models to the Credit or Model Risk Committee for approval if needed.
• Support deployment into the decision engine and sign off implementation testing — confirming that the scored production population matches the development specification, attribute for attribute.Account Origination and Decision Strategy:
• Own the origination decision logic end-to-end: pre-screen, identity and fraud checks, bureau and alternative data calls, scorecard execution, affordability assessment, policy rules, cut-off setting, limit assignment and referral treatment.
• Optimise approval-rate versus loss trade-offs using swap-set analysis; quantify the profit impact of every proposed cut-off or policy change before it goes live.
• Design initial credit limit and limit-increase strategies for BNPL, balancing basket-size conversion and merchant experience against exposure at risk.
• Build and run a disciplined champion/challenger and A/B testing programme, including test design, sample sizing, holdout maintenance and readout, so that strategy changes are evidence-based rather than opinion-based.
• Reduce friction and decision latency: increase straight-through-processing rates, cut manual referrals, and shorten time-to-decision without increasing loss.
• Work with Fraud to separate first-party and third-party fraud losses from credit losses, and ensure origination strategy treats them differently.
• Feed origination insight back into Product, Merchant and Marketing teams — which channels, merchants, baskets and segments originate profitable accounts, and which do not.Commercial and Profitability impact:
• Translate analytics into commercial recommendations with quantified rand-value impact, and defend them to Credit, Finance and Exco.
• Contribute to credit loss forecasting and to the annual budget and business planning cycle.Other:
• Act as the analytical authority in Credit Committee forums; present clearly to non-technical audiences.
• Mentor junior analysts, review their code and models, and raise the analytical standard of the team.

The ideal candidate is someone who understands apparel and footwear retail, enjoys working with stock and data, and can turn information into practical action.
This person must not only be able to pull reports, but must also understand what the numbers mean, why stock issues happen, and how to solve them. They must understand the mechanics of inventory planning from the ground up and be able to follow through from planning, to communication, to execution.
The right candidate will be structured, analytical, practical, and hands-on, with a strong ability to solve problems and improve how stock flows through the business.
Job Purpose
The Apparel Inventory Planner is responsible for ensuring that the right products are available in the right stores, in the right quantities, at the right time.
This role manages stock planning, replenishment, allocations, size curves, transfers, stock balancing, and inventory reporting across retail stores, online channels, and warehouse locations.
The role requires someone who understands inventory planning from the ground up — not only the reporting side, but also the working mechanics behind stock movement, replenishment, allocations, store demand, ERP accuracy, warehouse flow, and execution across the business.
The Apparel Inventory Planner plays a critical role in improving stock availability, reducing stock-outs, managing slow-moving stock, supporting better buying decisions, and ensuring that inventory supports sales, customer demand, and profitability.
Key Responsibilities
1. Stock Planning & Replenishment
●    Plan and manage stock levels across all stores, online channels, and warehouse locations.
●    Monitor weekly sales, stock-on-hand, sell-through, weeks-of-cover, and stock availability.
●    Identify fast-moving, slow-moving, and out-of-stock products.
●    Recommend replenishment actions based on sales trends, stock holding, store performance, and customer demand.
●    Ensure key styles, best sellers, and core products are available in the correct quantities and sizes.
●    Maintain proper size curves across footwear, apparel, and accessories.
●    Identify gaps in stock availability before they become sales problems.
●    Support the business in maintaining the correct balance between stock availability and stock efficiency.
2. Allocations & Store Stock Balancing
●    Allocate new stock to stores based on sales history, store grading, product type, size demand, store capacity, and available stock.
●    Review stock distribution regularly and recommend store-to-store transfers where required.
●    Ensure stores are not overstocked or understocked in specific products, categories, or sizes.
●    Support new store openings, promotional launches, campaigns, and seasonal product drops with correct stock allocations.
●    Ensure stock is placed where it has the highest chance of selling.
●    Monitor store stock levels and recommend corrective actions where stores are carrying poor size curves, excess stock, or insufficient depth.
3. Inventory Reporting & Analysis
●    Prepare weekly and monthly inventory reports to support decision-making.
●    Report on key inventory metrics, including:
○    Stock-on-hand
○    Sell-through
○    Weeks-of-cover
○    Stock-outs
○    Slow movers
○    Best sellers
○    Store performance by category
○    Size availability
○    Transfer requirements
○    Replenishment needs
●    Analyse product, store, category, and size performance.
●    Identify risks and opportunities in the stock position.
●    Translate sales and stock data into clear, practical actions.
●    Provide management with meaningful insights, not just reports.
4. ERP & System Management
●    Maintain and monitor accurate product, stock, and planning information on the ERP system.
●    Ensure ERP data supports accurate planning, replenishment, reporting, and stock decision-making.
●    Monitor transfers, shipments, receipts, and stock movements to ensure they are processed correctly.
●    Follow up on unconfirmed shipments, outstanding transfers, receiving issues, and system discrepancies.
●    Work closely with the Stock Controller to identify and resolve stock accuracy issues.
●    Assist with stock take preparation, variance analysis, and stock accuracy improvement.
●    Understand how system transactions impact physical stock, store availability, and reporting accuracy.
5. Planning Principles & Execution
●    Understand planning principles from the ground up through to execution.
●    Understand the full working mechanics of inventory planning, including how sales, stock, replenishment, allocations, transfers, buying, warehouse movement, and store performance all connect.
●    Build planning recommendations that are practical, executable, and aligned with business reality.
●    Identify the root cause of stock issues rather than only reacting to symptoms.
●    Ensure that planning decisions are followed through into action.
●    Work across teams to make sure that plans are implemented properly and that stock movements are completed.
6. Buying & Product Support
●    Support the buying team with stock history, sales data, product performance, and size curve insights.
●    Provide recommendations on reorder quantities, product depth, store allocations, and replenishment requirements.
●    Assist in identifying products that should be repeated, discontinued, marked down, transferred, or rebalanced.
●    Support seasonal, capsule, promotional, and core product planning.
●    Provide input into future stock buys based on actual store and product performance.
●    Help ensure that buying decisions are informed by data, store demand, and practical stock flow.
7. Store & Warehouse Communication
●    Communicate stock movements, transfer requirements, replenishment priorities, and stock actions clearly to stores and warehouse teams.
●    Follow up with stores on receiving, transfers, stock discrepancies, and stock availability issues.
●    Work with store teams to understand customer demand, stock gaps, size requests, and product feedback.
●    Ensure stores follow the correct processes for stock movement, receiving, transfers, and reporting.
●    Work with warehouse teams to ensure stock is dispatched, received, and processed accurately and timeously.
●    Escalate stock issues where needed and drive practical solutions.
8. Problem Solving & Continuous Improvement
●    Identify stock-related problems and work through them logically.
●    Understand the root cause of issues relating to stock-outs, overstocking, poor size curves, delayed transfers, system inaccuracies, or poor sell-through.
●    Recommend practical solutions that improve stock flow and store performance.
●    Continuously look for ways to improve planning processes, reporting, stock accuracy, replenishment, and execution.
●    Take ownership of problems and follow through until they are resolved.
●    Help create better structure, discipline, and consistency in inventory planning across the business.
Required Skills & Experience
●    Previous experience in apparel, footwear, fashion, retail planning, inventory planning, merchandising, or a similar role.
●    Strong understanding of retail stock flow, store replenishment, size curves, allocations, and seasonal product planning.
●    Understanding of planning principles from the ground up through to execution.
●    Deep understanding of the working mechanics of inventory planning, including how sales, stock, replenishment, allocations, transfers, buying, store performance, ERP accuracy, and warehouse movements all connect.
●    Strong problem-solving ability, with the ability to identify stock issues, understand the root cause, and recommend practical solutions.

●    Strong Excel or Google Sheets skills are essential.

Maintenance Manager
A permanent opportunity to lead, plan, and control all maintenance activities across production equipment and site facilities to ensure maximum plant availability, operational reliability, and safety. The role is based in the Ottery or Philippi branch within the packaging sector.
About Our Client
The company operates within the manufacturing and packaging sector, focusing on production equipment, site facilities, and utilities. The organization utilizes advanced engineering systems, automation, and structured maintenance frameworks to drive sustainability and environmental impact awareness.
The Role: Maintenance Manager
The Maintenance Manager exists to lead, plan, and control all maintenance activities across production equipment and site facilities. The role contributes to the business by ensuring maximum plant availability, operational reliability, and safety at an optimal total cost while driving preventive and predictive maintenance strategies. The main focus areas involve governing legal compliance as the legally appointed GMR 2.1 competent person, leading a multi-disciplinary technical team, and directly supervising the safe use, operation, and maintenance of all machinery on site.
Key Responsibilities
• Manage 7–10 years of industrial maintenance experience, including 3–5 years in a leadership or supervisory role within a manufacturing environment.
• Act as the designated, legally appointed GMR 2.1 competent person supervising site machinery to ensure total compliance with the OHS Act and General Machinery Regulations.
• Own and execute the maintenance master plan across preventive, predictive, and corrective maintenance frameworks using a Computerized Maintenance Management System.
• Implement Reliability-Centred Maintenance, Failure Mode and Effects Analysis, and root cause analysis methodologies to resolve operational losses.
• Deploy and govern the Computerized Maintenance Management System, including the asset register, Bills of Materials, PM routines, work order management, backlog control, and equipment history.
• Support high equipment availability and Overall Equipment Effectiveness through disciplined PM compliance, breakdown responses, and effective technical escalation.
• Lead, coach, and develop the technical maintenance team consisting of Maintenance Supervisors, Artisans, and Technicians while managing the annual maintenance OPEX and CAPEX budgets.
• Apply company quality principles, adhere to Good Manufacturing Practices, and strictly comply with site-specific Food Safety Management Systems and FSSC standards.

1. Programme Background
ForAfrika is a leading African humanitarian and development organisation operating in eight countries, with a vision of an Africa that thrives. Under a three-year grant from the donor, ForAfrika South Africa will assume full operational responsibility for solar-powered rural water systems across Mpumalanga, Limpopo and KwaZulu-Natal.
Each system comprises five integrated sub-systems: solar power generation and storage (2–4 kWp PV arrays with MPPT charge controllers and battery banks), a borehole with a Grundfos SQFlex or equivalent solar-direct submersible pump, automated inline chlorination, a 10 m³ elevated reservoir with gravity-fed distribution, and a standpipe network with volumetric metering. ForAfrika's role is to maintain, operate, and transfer these systems to community ownership, with water quality compliance against South African National Standard SANS 241:2015 as a Day 1 obligation.
2. Purpose of the Position
The WASH Field Engineer is part of the programme's technical delivery role — the qualified engineer responsible for quarterly full-system inspections, preventive and reactive maintenance, water quality field monitoring, and first-line technical problem-solving across an assigned cluster of sites. The position sits between trained community pump operators performing daily checks and specialist contractors performing manufacturer-level servicing, and is accountable for keeping systems operational, compliant, and well-documented.
The Field Engineer plays a central role in the technical condition assessment of all sites in the assigned cluster.
3. Key Responsibilities
3.1 Technical condition assessment
• Conduct the site-by-site technical condition assessment across the assigned cluster within the first three months: pump, controller, panels, batteries, tank and tower, distribution network, valves and fittings, and civil structure.
• Participate in joint site visits with Water supply system contractor including asset register verification, documentation review, and monitoring dashboard familiarisation.
• Support country team activities: tiered water quality field testing, sanitary surveys at risk-flagged sites, GPS verification, and yield measurement at sites with missing yield records.
• Contribute technical findings which need to be confirmed by Month 3, and identify end-of-life components for replacement under the Year 1 Replacement Capex Reserve.
• Execute Tier C remediation works at named priority sites under the 48-hour remediation initiation protocol and support the portfolio-wide water quality baseline assessment within 90 days of operational kickoff.3.2 Preventive and reactive maintenance
• Perform quarterly full-system inspections at all assigned sites: borehole yield testing, pump efficiency assessment, solar panel output measurement, battery and charge controller checks, chlorination system verification, structural inspection of concrete towers, and water committee performance review.
• Deliver reactive repairs in line with the tiered service-impact protocol: critical failures; reduced-service issues within five working days; minor issues at the next quarterly inspection.
• Diagnose faults using Water supply system contractor remote monitoring telemetry and support the shift from schedule-driven to condition-based, predictive maintenance at monitored sites.
• Escalate manufacturer-level pump servicing, borehole rehabilitation, and solar system overhauls to DWS-listed certified solar technical partners and supervise their work on site against service-level agreements.
• Prioritise Parent-site maintenance within the cluster maintenance model, recognising that Parent borehole failures cascade to hydraulically dependent Child sites
• Manage cluster-level spare parts inventories at Hub anchor locations, forecast consumables and coordinate replenishment with the Finance and Logistics Officer.3.3 Water quality monitoring and compliance
• Conduct monthly water quality field testing at all assigned sites using portable field kits and maintain calibration of field instruments.
• Collect and dispatch quarterly bacteriological samples (E. coli, total coliforms) to SANAS-accredited laboratories and apply elevated (monthly) sampling frequency at sites until restored.
• Verify automated inline chlorination performance (0.2–0.5 mg/L free chlorine residual at the most distant standpipe) and adjust dosing as required.
• Maintain water quality records in the programme database, flag non-compliance against SANS 241:2015 immediately, and initiate corrective action plans in coordination with the WASH Programme Manager.3.4 Community technical capacity building
• Train and mentor community pump operators in daily system checks, monthly pump performance logging, and water quality field testing, cross-referencing operator logs with remote monitoring telemetry.
• Deliver pump-attendant training cohorts and support the certification pathway from community operator toward established standard for community-hired technicians.
• Support Water Management Committees with technical inputs to O&M planning, tariff-setting consultations and Capital Sinking Fund calibration against component lifecycles (5/7/10/20 years).
• Contribute technical content to site-level O&M manuals any other documentation.3.5 Documentation, reporting and coordination
• Complete site inspection reports, maintenance job cards, and asset register updates in the field management system after every visit.
• Contribute technical data to monthly cluster reports, the MEAL dashboard, and quarterly donor reports, in coordination with the DMEAL team.
• Coordinate site visit scheduling with Community Mobilisation Officers so that maintenance activities are communicated to and coordinated with communities.
• Support the pump overhaul cycle for 2018-vintage systems and solar system overhauls for remaining vintage systems
4. Qualifications and Experience
Essential
• Bachelor's degree or national diploma in Mechanical, Electrical, Civil, or Water Engineering, or a closely related engineering field.
• Registration with the Engineering Council of South Africa (ECSA) as a Candidate Engineer or Candidate Engineering Technologist (or eligibility to register); DWS registration/recognition as applicable.
• Minimum three (3) years of hands-on experience in the operation and maintenance of rural water supply systems, with demonstrable experience on solar-powered pumping systems (solar-direct submersible pumps, PV arrays, MPPT controllers, battery systems).
• Working knowledge of water quality monitoring and SANS 241:2015 requirements, including use of portable field test kits and bacteriological sampling protocols.
• Practical fault-diagnosis and repair skills across electromechanical, hydraulic, and basic civil components of borehole-based water systems.
• Valid driver's licence (Code B minimum; Code C1 an advantage) and willingness to travel extensively (up to 75%) to remote rural sites, including overnight stays — the KwaZulu-Natal position requires residence in-region, as day trips to the uMkhanyakude sites are not feasible from other bases.Desirable
• Grundfos certification or documented experience servicing Grundfos SQFlex or equivalent solar submersible pump fleets.
• Experience with remote monitoring/telemetry platforms and condition-based (predictive) maintenance approaches.
• Experience training community-based operators or artisans.
• Familiarity with borehole yield testing, sanitary survey methodology, and inline chlorination systems.
• Prior experience on donor-funded WASH programmes in the NGO/development sector.
• Proficiency in the dominant language of the assigned cluster (IsiZulu, Sepedi, or Siswati) in addition to English.

We are venture builders and technology investors, partnering with startups and corporate ventures to design, build, and scale ambitious products.
MOHARA is a globally distributed team across the UK, Thailand, Mexico, and South Africa. We work as one team across regions, combining deep technical expertise with strong product thinking.
Our values are grounded in:
• Craft - high standards and pride in our work
• Clarity - simple, reliable ways of working
• Ownership - vision, long-term thinking and accountability
• Curiosity - asking questions, being brave and challenging assumptions
We care deeply about the people we build with - our clients, their users, and each other - and we continuously look for ways to improve how we work.
Culture
Although we work in project teams, we operate as a single company. We actively collaborate, share knowledge, and draw on the collective experience of the wider team.
We’re looking for people who want more than just a role; people who want to contribute to how we build, not just what we build.
Our engineers:
• Are curious and proactive, with a strong point of view
• Communicate clearly and challenge constructively
• Show empathy for teammates, clients, and end users
• Take ownership, going beyond the brief to find better solutions
Our work with early-stage and scaling ventures means ambiguity is the norm. We value people who:
• Push their own boundaries and continuously grow
• Help shape client thinking, not just deliver against it
• Are honest about trade-offs, risks, and constraints
We treat every client’s product as if it were our own, recognising the investment, ambition, and trust behind it.
The Role: What we’re looking for
Our engineering team is at the core of what we build. As a full stack engineer at MOHARA, you’ll work in cross-functional teams to design, build, and scale products from early concept through to production.
You’ll be responsible for the full software development lifecycle: shaping ideas with clients, building robust systems, and continuously improving what we ship.
We’re looking for engineers who:
• Are comfortable building full-stack web and mobile applications end-to-end
• Care deeply about understanding users and product outcomes, not just writing code
• Think critically and challenge decisions when something doesn’t feel right
• Pay attention to detail, while keeping sight of the bigger picture
• Collaborate effectively across engineering, product, and design
• Have strong engineering fundamentals
Our environment requires balancing speed and quality, pragmatism and scalability knowing when to move fast and when to invest in stronger foundations.
AI Native Engineering
We believe AI is a fundamental accelerator for how modern software is built.
You’ll be expected to:
• Use AI tools as a core part of your development workflow
• Continuously refine how you work with AI to improve speed and quality
• Contribute to evolving our AI-native engineering practices across the team
Strong fundamentals still matter as AI amplifies good engineers, it doesn’t replace them.

• Own significant parts of the product, from architecture through to deployment and iteration

Duties & Responsibilities
Operations
• Be able to start up boiler fire properly.
• Monitor water holding JoJo tanks hourly and keep them full of water at all times.
• Monitor low level water alarm on your hotwell tank.
• Complete daily boiler maintenance checklist and ensure supervisor signed it after completion.
• Adjust coal bed as and when required.
• Close valves and stop supply of steam to production when boiler is not running for minimum 30 minutes due to power outage or breakdown and maintain steam.
• Change the use of coal screw conveyor weekly with the standby screw conveyor.
• Keep coal water bath clean and at right level all the time.
• Keep boiler drains clean all the time.
• Change the use of boiler water pump weekly with the standby pump.
• Ensure safety by monitoring safety equipment, identifying potential issues and taking appropriate steps to suspend the operation with consultation with your shift supervisor/maintenance team.
• Maintain steam pressure for production operation as per steam demand for processing.
• Continuously communicate with the production operator on steam demand hourly.
• Monitor and control boiler performance and settings by reading gauges, meters and charts to track boiler operation.
• Monitor boiler water and chemicals and coal levels hourly.
• Maintain the housekeeping of boiler room/area all the time.
• Monitor your stocker movement every hour to ensure it is still aligned on its path.
• Receive delivery of coal and inspect whether it complies with Grade A pea size specifications without excessive duff/loose powder before tipping.
• Inform your shift supervisor if coal delivered is out of specification.
• Keep your coal bund pit full at all times.
• Report low coal levels to your shift supervisor for ordering.
• Ensure sufficient coal stock is available to last at least two days.
• Grease boiler components that require greasing. If unsure, ask the maintenance team to show you the greasing points.
• Update log sheet/book hourly.
• Perform soot blowing.
• Blow down the boilers as instructed by the guideline to remove impurities.
• Monitor water level and temperature in the hotwell tank hourly.
• Continuously check blowdown valve to avoid blockages.
• Ensure water treatment and sampling is conducted to prevent boiler damage.
• Trim coal and remove ash from grit arrester.
• Remove ash trolley as and when required.
• Clean the brine tank and water filter.
• Clean grit collector.
• Ensure plant equipment hygiene is of top quality.
• Ensure compliance with AEL licence requirements under the boiler section.
• Provide a written handover to the next shift.
• Follow the boiler operating procedure by conducting blowdowns, doing TDS tests and recording results during your shift.
• Ensure boiler softener system is working correctly.
• Keep all boilers clean and shiny.
• Clean boiler tubes after every three months.
• Ensure Mobrey automatic water level controller is functioning correctly. If not, report to your shift supervisor and maintenance team.
• Be able to bank the fire.
• Replace broken links and rods on your stocker.
Quality
• Ensure coal received complies with Grade A pea size specifications.
Policy
• Ensure you follow and apply company policies in your work area.
Safety
• Ensure you use the correct PPE provided.
• Use safety harnesses when working at height.
• Apply Health and Safety Regulations inside the boiler house.
Desired Experience & Qualifications
• Ability to work independently and work within a team.
• Strong work ethic.
• Willingness to work overtime and accept off-shift assignments.
• Ability to work with minimum supervision.
• Good communication skills.
• Ability to work under pressure.
Important Notes
• Candidates must be willing to relocate to Greylingstad (Nthorwane), Mpumalanga.
• Applicants residing in Johannesburg or other metropolitan areas who intend to commute will not be considered.
• The role requires shift work (07:00 – 19:00 on a rotational basis), making daily commuting impractical.
• A guaranteed 13th cheque is included.
• Performance-based bonuses are awarded based on individual performance and achievement of KPIs.

Primary Function
The Financial Manager is responsible for leading the day-to-day financial management of the business, ensuring accurate financial reporting, effective financial controls, regulatory compliance, budgeting, forecasting, and business performance analysis.
The role serves as a strategic business partner to management by providing financial insight to support operational and commercial decision-making while maintaining sound governance and risk management practices.
Roles and Responsibilities
Financial Management
Manage the monthly, quarterly, and annual financial reporting processes.
Prepare and review monthly management accounts.
Oversee month-end and year-end close procedures.
Review journals, accruals, prepayments, and general ledger transactions.
Ensure the integrity of financial records and balance sheet reconciliations.
Monitor cash flow and working capital requirements.
Budgeting and Forecasting
Lead the quarterly & annual budgeting process.
Prepare rolling forecasts and financial projections.
Monitor departmental expenditure against approved budgets.
Analyse financial variances and recommend corrective actions.
Support long-term financial planning.
Financial Analysis
Provide financial analysis to support strategic and operational decision-making.
Develop financial models and business cases.
Monitor revenue, profitability, and cost performance.
Analyse operational costs and cost recovery models.
Present financial reports and recommendations to executive management.
Support commercial initiatives with financial input.
Compliance and Governance
Ensure compliance with applicable accounting standards, tax legislation, and company policies.
Oversee VAT calculations and statutory submissions.
Coordinate annual external audits and resolve audit queries.
Maintain and improve internal financial controls.
Assist with risk management and governance initiatives.
Operational Finance
Oversee customer billing and revenue reconciliations.
Review supplier payments and financial controls.
Manage fixed assets and depreciation schedules.
Monitor capital expenditure.
Support procurement and contract evaluations from a financial perspective.
Process Improvement
Identify opportunities to improve financial systems and reporting.  Implement process improvements and automation initiatives.
Enhance reporting accuracy and efficiency.
Team Leadership
Provide guidance and support to finance team members.
Allocate and monitor finance workloads.
Develop and mentor junior finance staff.
Foster a culture of accountability, accuracy, and continuous improvement

Description:
THE JOB AT A GLANCE
To provide strategic leadership and direction for the development, execution, and continuous refinement of RMA's commercial strategy and partnership ecosystem, ensuring alignment with the organisation's mandate as a social insurer. The role is responsible for identifying growth opportunities, strengthening strategic partnerships, enhancing customer value propositions, and translating market, customer, and data-driven insights into sustainable organisational outcomes across COIDA, Life Insurance, and AIT Administration portfolios.
The incumbent serves as a strategic advisor to executive leadership and plays a critical role in shaping enterprise direction, driving commercial sustainability, fostering innovation, leading organisational transformation initiatives, and delivering meaningful societal impact through partnerships and strategic interventions.
WHAT WILL YOU DO?
Strategic Leadership
Develop and continuously refine RMA's commercial and partnership strategy. Drive enterprise strategic initiatives supporting long-term growth and sustainability. Align strategic priorities with organisational purpose, mandate, vision and operating model. Lead strategic reviews and environmental scanning activities.
Commercial Strategy & Growth
Identify new market opportunities and innovative business models. Develop growth strategies for COIDA, Life and AIT portfolios. Drive revenue optimisation and customer value creation initiatives.
Partnerships & Ecosystem Development
Identify, negotiate and manage strategic partnerships. Establish collaborative ecosystems that improve customer outcomes. Develop partnership governance frameworks. Measure and optimise partnership effectiveness and value delivery.
Strategic Planning & Performance
Lead annual and multi-year planning processes. Define strategic measures and scorecards. Monitor strategic outcomes and enterprise performance. Present strategic insights and recommendations to executive forums.
Organizational Transformation & Innovation
Lead strategic transformation programmes. Promote innovation and agile ways of working. Drive customer-centricity and data-informed decision making. Support digital transformation initiatives.
Stakeholder Influence
Influence executive decision making through evidence-based recommendations. Represent RMA at industry, government and executive forums. Build strategic relationships that advance RMA's positioning.
People Leadership
Lead and develop a high-performing strategy and partnerships team. Foster a culture of accountability, innovation and collaboration. Drive workforce capability, succession planning and talent development. Create an inclusive and high-engagement environment.
Governance & Risk Management
Ensure compliance with regulatory and governance requirements. Identify and manage strategic risks. Maintain effective controls and reporting mechanisms.

The following position has become available at the Mascor Malelane OK Mini Market: Stock Controller.
RESPONSIBILITIES:
• Maintain accurate stock records within the Point of Sale (POS) and inventory management systems.
• Ensure all stock movements are correctly captured and reconciled.
• Conduct daily, weekly, and monthly stock counts according to company procedures.
• Investigate and resolve stock variances promptly.
• Maintain inventory accuracy levels of at least 98%.
• Receive stock deliveries from suppliers.
• Verify quantities, product descriptions, expiry dates, and quality against delivery documentation.
• Ensure all received stock is correctly captured on the system.
• Report shortages, damages, and discrepancies immediately.
• Maintain proper receiving documentation and audit trails.
• Monitor stock levels and identify replenishment requirements.
• Assist management with ordering based on sales trends, minimum stock levels, seasonality, and promotional activities.
• Ensure fast-moving lines remain available to customers.
• Prevent overstocking that may lead to wastage, expiry, or excessive working capital investment.
• Monitor product expiry dates and implement First-In-First-Out (FIFO) principles.
• Identify slow-moving and ageing stock.
• Coordinate markdowns or promotions to reduce potential losses.
• Ensure compliance with food safety and quality standards.
• Monitor and investigate stock losses, theft, damages, and wastage.
• Participate in security and loss prevention initiatives.
• Implement controls to reduce shrinkage.
• Report suspicious stock movements or irregularities to management.
• Prepare daily, weekly, and monthly stock reports.
• Analyse stock variances and provide recommendations for corrective action.
• Assist with month-end stock valuations and audits.
• Maintain accurate filing and recordkeeping systems.
• Work closely with store management to ensure optimal stock availability.
• Assist with merchandising initiatives and promotional stock planning.
• Support operational activities during peak trading periods.

Turn Your Commercial Experience into Entrepreneurial ImpactAre you a financially astute business professional who understands more than just the numbers?
Perhaps you are a financial analyst, commercial manager, finance leader, business operator or entrepreneur with a strong understanding of how business finance, strategy, sales, and operations work together. You may have reached a point in your career where you are looking for something different: an opportunity to use your experience to guide business owners, develop entrepreneurs and create measurable impact.
If you have run your own business, understand the realities of entrepreneurship and are ready to move from analysing or managing businesses to helping entrepreneurs build stronger ones, this could be the career change you have been looking for.
Raizcorp is looking for a seasoned, well-rounded business professional to join us as a business coach.
This is a full-time, salaried role in which you will coach a portfolio of entrepreneurs across every area of their businesses, including finance, strategy, sales, marketing, operations, people and personal development.
You do not need any previous coaching experience. Raizcorp will train you in our internationally recognised coaching methodology. What you do need is substantial business experience, strong commercial judgement, empathy for entrepreneurs and a genuine desire to help others succeed.
What you’ll do
· Hold structured monthly one-on-one coaching sessions with entrepreneurs.
· Help business owners interpret their financial information and use it to make better commercial decisions.
· Guide entrepreneurs in strengthening their strategies, sales approaches, marketing activities, operational systems and people practices.
· Facilitate business simulations and group learning sessions using Raizcorp’s proven programmes and methodology.
· Manage a defined portfolio of entrepreneurs and track progress in areas such as revenue, profitability, business capability and founder development.
· Challenge entrepreneurs to think critically, evaluate trade-offs and take accountability for their decisions.
· Connect the different areas of a business so entrepreneurs can make integrated, forward-looking decisions.
· Remain informed about economic conditions, market shifts and regulations that may affect entrepreneurs and their businesses.
· Collaborate closely with other coaches and specialists to support each entrepreneur’s development journey.
This role may be a strong fit for you if you are:
· A financial analyst or finance professional who has developed a strong understanding of business operations and commercial decision-making.
· A commercial or operational leader who wants to use your experience in a more purpose-driven role.
· A current or former entrepreneur who understands both the rewards and pressures of building a business.
· An experienced business professional looking for a meaningful career change.
· Someone who enjoys developing people, asking insightful questions and helping others arrive at better decisions. Empathy in this role is super important.
· Motivated by the opportunity to influence real business results rather than simply report on them.
What you’ll need
· Between 10 and 15-plus years of experience across corporate, commercial and entrepreneurial environments.
· Experience owning or running your own business at some point in your career. This is a non-negotiable requirement.
· Strong financial and commercial acumen, with the ability to interpret business performance beyond the income statement.
· Experiential depth in business finance, strategy and sales.
· A practical understanding of how marketing, operations, people and finance influence one another.
· The ability to identify patterns, challenge assumptions and help entrepreneurs evaluate business trade-offs.
· High emotional intelligence and genuine empathy for the realities of entrepreneurship.
· A mature, accountable and non-judgemental approach.
· Strong communication and facilitation skills.
· An organised, systematic and proactive working style.
· Confidence using technology and business systems, including Microsoft 365 or Microsoft Office and learner management systems.
· A commerce-related tertiary qualification. An MBA or other master’s-level qualification will be an advantage.
· A valid driver’s licence and your own vehicle.
What you’ll gain
· The opportunity to turn years of commercial and entrepreneurial experience into meaningful impact.
· A career in which you work directly with entrepreneurs and their businesses every day.
· Formal training in an internationally recognised business-coaching methodology.
· Continuous professional development and exposure to businesses across different industries and stages of growth.
· The opportunity to influence revenue, profitability, founder capability and long-term business sustainability.
· A supportive, fiercely caring team culture that backs the jockey—the entrepreneur—not only the horse.
· A rare opportunity to build a new career without leaving the world of business behind.
Ready for a different kind of business career?
You have spent years analysing businesses, leading teams, making commercial decisions or building something of your own.
Now, you could use that experience to help entrepreneurs make better decisions, build stronger businesses and become more capable business leaders.
Move from measuring business performance to helping create it.

job_title: Silverton General Ledger Clerk (Motor Industry exp essential)
about_role:
Silverton General Ledger Clerk (Motor Dealership exp essential)
Please note: Only applicants who worked as a General Ledger Clerk at a motor dealership will be contacted and shortlisted. All other industries will be unsuccessful. Do not apply if you have not worked at a Dealership and can provide contactable references.
Financial Division – Motor Industry Group
Location: Silverton, Pretoria
Position Type: Full-Time, Permanent (Following a successful 3-month probation period)
Industry: Automotive / Motor Sector
Salary: R25,000.00 – R32,000.00 Basic Salary per month (Negotiable based on experience) + Benefits
About Our Client
Representing a diverse portfolio of the world’s leading passenger, commercial, and emerging electric vehicle brands, our client's dealerships offer an all-inclusive motoring solution—encompassing new and pre-owned vehicle sales, finance and insurance (F&I) services, specialized workshops, aftermarket performance tuning, and genuine parts procurement. Backed by a strong balance sheet, entrenched standard operating procedures, and industry-leading systems, this group is built on a culture of integrity, a "can-do" attitude, and a continuous commitment to the training and development of its workforce.
About the Role
On behalf of our client, we are seeking a meticulous, accurate, and experienced General Ledger Clerk to join their finance team.
If you have a strong background in accounting principles, a sharp eye for detail, and solid hands-on experience within the motor industry, this is an excellent opportunity to advance your career. You will play a pivotal role in maintaining core financial records, performing account reconciliations, ensuring data accuracy, and supporting month-end close procedures.
What’s on Offer?
- Basic Salary: R25,000.00 – R32,000.00 Basic Salary per month (Negotiable based on experience).
- Medical Aid: 50% company contribution (capped at a maximum of R9,260.50).
- Gap Cover: Compulsory at R199.00 per month for all employees joining the medical aid scheme.
- Pension Fund: 8% company contribution (Only applicable to permanent employment following the successful completion of a 3-month probation period).
- Leave Days: 15 days per annum (Subject to company policy: leave cannot be taken for more than 10 consecutive working days and may not be taken over month-end).
Working Hours & Environment
- Standard Hours: Monday to Friday from 08:00 to 17:00.
- Environment: Professional, office-based corporate finance environment.
- Standard Working Procedures (SWP): A standard working procedures manual must be obtained from HR for your position; it must be read, signed, and returned to HR within your first week of employment.
Key Responsibilities
- Transaction Posting: Accurately post daily financial transactions and routine journal entries into the accounting system.
- Account Reconciliations: Perform complete monthly reconciliations for assigned general ledger accounts.
- Error Investigation: Proactively investigate, troubleshoot, and resolve accounting errors or data mismatches.
- Audit Support: Prepare and compile detailed supporting documentation for internal and external audits.
- Period Closing: Assist the financial team with month-end and year-end closing tasks according to set timelines.
Requirements & Qualifications
- Experience: Proven, stable experience as a General Ledger Clerk within the Motor Sector is strictly essential and non-negotiable.
- Bookkeeping Knowledge: Strong, practical grasp of basic bookkeeping principles and accounting workflows.
- Systems Knowledge & Skills: Advanced proficiency with spreadsheets (MS Excel) and financial/accounting software.
- Attributes: High attention to detail, exceptional data accuracy, strong analytical capabilities, and the ability to work under pressure to meet strict deadlines.
- References: Must be able to supply contactable references from previous employers for verification.
Strict Legal Requirements
Please Note: Due to the financial and sensitive nature of this role, the following criteria are non-negotiable. Background screening will be conducted on all shortlisted candidates.
- Must be a South African-born citizen with a valid South African ID.
- Must have a clean criminal background (Candidates with a criminal record will not be considered).
- Must have a clear ITC (financial/credit history) with no judgments or defaults.
Required Documentation for Application
Please ensure that you submit the following documentation with your application:
- Detailed CV: Must include contactable references clearly reflecting your dealership financial experience.
- ID Copy: Required as proof of South African-born citizenship.
- Drivers’ License Copy: Required for the operation of company vehicles.
- 3 Months Recent Payslips: Your latest three consecutive months of salary advice.
- Supporting Documents (Optional): Copies of all relevant qualifications, achievements/awards, and reference letters.

job_title: DC Inventory Clerk - Day Shift - Cosmetics  -DC Midrand
about_role:
Dis-Chem Pharmacies’ in Midrand has an opportunity available for a DC Inventory Clerk to join the team. The main purpose of this role will be to ensure that replenishment gets done on the various bins, within the Distribution system in the warehouse on a continuous basis. Ensure efficient and accurate continuous cycle counting of stock, in line with company standard operational procedures, and customer needs, if required to do so and ensure physical stock integrity and accuracy in the warehouse is maintained.
Minimum Requirements…
Essential:
• Grade 12 or Senior Certificate
Advantageous:
• Supply-Chain or Logistics Degree or Diploma
• 2 Years relevant experience, in a Distribution, Logistics or Supply Chain EnvironmentJob Specification…
Inventory:
• Interpret and initiate continuous inventory, as well as annual stock counts.
• Ensure accuracy of counts and process the counts according to standard operating procedure.
• Prevent, analyse and interpret all potential departmental shrinkage indicators (adjustments) and act accordingly.
• Ensure high level responsibility.
• Maintain a stock rotation on an inventory based on FEFO (first expiry, first out) principle.
• Continuously resolve stock issues and errors.
• Update stock reports as required by management. Customer Service:
• Effective and efficient resolution of internal and external customer day-to-day queries.
• Deal with all aspects of store or customer queries.
• Effective and efficient relationships with internal customers to improve operating efficiencies.
• Effective direction within the operational team through involvement and communication and sound people practices.
• Ensure everything, within reason has been done to meet customer expectations and ensure customer satisfaction. Planning and Administration:
• Ensure optimal planning and forecasting of department resources to meet the day-to-day strategic objectives.
• Efficient and accurate administration, filling and reporting for transactional excellence.
• Adhere to Good Warehousing Practises, SHE programme and Occupational Health and Safety act.
• Anticipate issues and opportunities and take act on them pro-actively.
• Adherence and delivery against shift specific targets, with emphasis on accuracy.
• The effective and efficient performance of clerical functions in the Inventory department, according to standard operating procedures.
• Comply with minimum standards of efficiency and accuracy, in order to meet company requirements. Cycle Counting / Penalty Area:
• Be responsible for ensuring that good cycle counting is performed on a regular cyclic basis.
• Maintain a high level of accuracy while performing duties.
• Spot-check accuracy of counters and take corrective action, with repeat offenders.
• Keep the penalty area clear on a daily basis.
• Be aware of all pick and reserve positions in different warehouse sections.
• Analyse adjustment trends and take appropriate action by drawing to management attention.
• Capture cycle count correction and other daily data.
• Produce daily empty bin reports and other enquiries as designated by department manager. Remuneration and benefits:
• Market related salary
• Medical aid
• Provident fund
• Staff account

Introduction:
The following position has become available for a Tunnel Manager in Kempton Park.
Description:
Starke Ayres is the foremost African specialist and global supplier of premium vegetable, flower and lawn seed varieties – both for commercial and home garden planting. The following position has become available for a Tunnel Manager in Kempton Park.
RESPONSIBILITIES:
Facility Maintenance & Hygiene
• General hygiene, appearance and tidiness around all tunnel structures including roads, lawn and fences.
• Monitor, maintain and service:
a. Greenhouse structures
b. Pump room and fertigation systems
c. Wet walls
d. Fresh water supply
e. Spraying equipment
f. Heating equipment (Boiler)
g. Weather station (with long term record keeping)
Climate Control Management
• Program/adjust seasonal/daily settings influencing climate control with regards to:
a. Day length
b. Cooling
c. Heating
d. Ventilation
e. Radiation
Breeding & Production Support
• Working closely with breeders to determine ideal growing conditions with regards to breeding requirements (manipulating plants for optimum pollination and seed production) and screening conditions (representative of commercial practices).
Plant Health Monitoring & Management
• Monitor general plant appearance throughout the day with regard to the below. Apply corrective measures on a continuous basis:
a. Wilting/heat stress
b. Nutritional abnormalities
c. Chemical burn
d. Physiological abnormalities
e. Physical damage
Fertigation & Nutritional Management
• Programming of fertigation system according to fertilizer recommendation based on commercial practices.
• Consulting with fertilizer/nutrition expert on a monthly basis to prevent and eliminate potential problems before they arise.
• Monitoring of EC, pH and run-off figures on a daily basis with appropriate record keeping and reporting.
• Be confident in changing fertigation programmes after consultation with breeder and fertilizer expert.
• Identify and solve nutritional deficiencies/toxicities.
• Recommendation regarding adjustment in growing medium composition.
• Taking of leaf samples and interpret analysis in collaboration with nutritional expert and adjust fertigation programme accordingly.
Pest & Disease Control
• Sanitise and disinfect facility on a daily/seasonal basis.
• Ensure availability and correct application of sanitiser, gloves, boots & coats to prevent spreading of disease.
• Scouting for pest and disease on a daily basis.
• Recommendation of spraying programmes after consultation with internal and external experts.
• Monitoring efficiency of spray recommendations resulting in the necessary adjustments.
Staff Supervision & Health & Safety
• Hiring and management of staff/labour with regard to:
a. Assigning work schedules
b. Spraying responsibilities
c. Pump room and fertigation activities
d. General greenhouse activities
e. Health and safety protocols with special reference to hazardous chemicals
• Training of staff with regards to the above.
Requirements:
REQUIREMENTS:
Qualification:
• Tertiary qualification in Horticulture (essential) (knowledge in agronomy and pathology will be an advantage)
Experience:
• Minimum 3–5 years’ experience in tunnel or protected environment crop production
• Minimum 2–3 years’ experience managing tunnel operations, including planting schedules, crop cycles, and harvest planning
• Demonstrated experience managing teams of 5–20+ staff, including scheduling, supervision, and basic labour relations
• Proven experience in tunnel or protected environment crop production
• Experience managing full tunnel operations, including planting schedules, crop cycles, and harvest planning
• Experience supervising and managing a production team, including workforce scheduling, performance management, and basic labour relations
• Hands-on experience with irrigation systems, fertigation programmes, and climate control equipment within a tunnel environment
• Experience implementing pest and disease management programmes in a protected growing environment
• Experience maintaining accurate production records, including yields, input usage, crop performance, and forward planning schedules
Technical Knowledge:
• Strong knowledge of plant physiology and the impact of tunnel conditions (temperature, humidity, light, and ventilation) on crop growth, yield, and quality
• Sound understanding of irrigation scheduling, EC and pH management, and fertigation principles
• Ability to accurately assess plant health, including early identification of nutrient deficiencies, physiological stress symptoms, and pest or disease pressure
• Knowledge of integrated pest and disease management (IPM) principles specific to tunnel production systems
• Understanding of post-harvest handling practices required to maintain product quality from harvest through to dispatch
Other:
• Valid driver's license
• Reside on farm (essential)
• Willing to work unexpected hours

Introduction:
The following position has become available for a Tunnel Manager in Kempton Park.
Description:
Starke Ayres is the foremost African specialist and global supplier of premium vegetable, flower and lawn seed varieties – both for commercial and home garden planting. The following position has become available for a Tunnel Manager in Kempton Park.
RESPONSIBILITIES:
Facility Maintenance & Hygiene
• General hygiene, appearance and tidiness around all tunnel structures including roads, lawn and fences.
• Monitor, maintain and service:
a. Greenhouse structures
b. Pump room and fertigation systems
c. Wet walls
d. Fresh water supply
e. Spraying equipment
f. Heating equipment (Boiler)
g. Weather station (with long term record keeping)
Climate Control Management
• Program/adjust seasonal/daily settings influencing climate control with regards to:
a. Day length
b. Cooling
c. Heating
d. Ventilation
e. Radiation
Breeding & Production Support
• Working closely with breeders to determine ideal growing conditions with regards to breeding requirements (manipulating plants for optimum pollination and seed production) and screening conditions (representative of commercial practices).
Plant Health Monitoring & Management
• Monitor general plant appearance throughout the day with regard to the below. Apply corrective measures on a continuous basis:
a. Wilting/heat stress
b. Nutritional abnormalities
c. Chemical burn
d. Physiological abnormalities
e. Physical damage
Fertigation & Nutritional Management
• Programming of fertigation system according to fertilizer recommendation based on commercial practices.
• Consulting with fertilizer/nutrition expert on a monthly basis to prevent and eliminate potential problems before they arise.
• Monitoring of EC, pH and run-off figures on a daily basis with appropriate record keeping and reporting.
• Be confident in changing fertigation programmes after consultation with breeder and fertilizer expert.
• Identify and solve nutritional deficiencies/toxicities.
• Recommendation regarding adjustment in growing medium composition.
• Taking of leaf samples and interpret analysis in collaboration with nutritional expert and adjust fertigation programme accordingly.
Pest & Disease Control
• Sanitise and disinfect facility on a daily/seasonal basis.
• Ensure availability and correct application of sanitiser, gloves, boots & coats to prevent spreading of disease.
• Scouting for pest and disease on a daily basis.
• Recommendation of spraying programmes after consultation with internal and external experts.
• Monitoring efficiency of spray recommendations resulting in the necessary adjustments.
Staff Supervision & Health & Safety
• Hiring and management of staff/labour with regard to:
a. Assigning work schedules
b. Spraying responsibilities
c. Pump room and fertigation activities
d. General greenhouse activities
e. Health and safety protocols with special reference to hazardous chemicals
• Training of staff with regards to the above.
Requirements:
REQUIREMENTS:
Qualification:
• Tertiary qualification in Horticulture (essential) (knowledge in agronomy and pathology will be an advantage)
Experience:
• Minimum 3–5 years’ experience in tunnel or protected environment crop production
• Minimum 2–3 years’ experience managing tunnel operations, including planting schedules, crop cycles, and harvest planning
• Demonstrated experience managing teams of 5–20+ staff, including scheduling, supervision, and basic labour relations
• Proven experience in tunnel or protected environment crop production
• Experience managing full tunnel operations, including planting schedules, crop cycles, and harvest planning
• Experience supervising and managing a production team, including workforce scheduling, performance management, and basic labour relations
• Hands-on experience with irrigation systems, fertigation programmes, and climate control equipment within a tunnel environment
• Experience implementing pest and disease management programmes in a protected growing environment
• Experience maintaining accurate production records, including yields, input usage, crop performance, and forward planning schedules
Technical Knowledge:
• Strong knowledge of plant physiology and the impact of tunnel conditions (temperature, humidity, light, and ventilation) on crop growth, yield, and quality
• Sound understanding of irrigation scheduling, EC and pH management, and fertigation principles
• Ability to accurately assess plant health, including early identification of nutrient deficiencies, physiological stress symptoms, and pest or disease pressure
• Knowledge of integrated pest and disease management (IPM) principles specific to tunnel production systems
• Understanding of post-harvest handling practices required to maintain product quality from harvest through to dispatch
Other:
• Valid driver's license
• Reside on farm (essential)
• Willing to work unexpected hours

iStore is the home of everything Apple, and Africa’s largest Apple Premium Reseller. With a retail footprint of more than 40 physical and online stores across Africa that provide expert advice, Apple Authorised Repairs, Business, Education, training and technical support for anything and everything Apple.
The iStore Management in Training (MIT) Programme is designed to build the next generation of iStore leaders. It is aimed at high-potential individuals who already have some experience in retail, hospitality, customer service or another fast-paced operational environment and are ready to take the next step into management.
Participants will gain hands-on experience across the key areas required to successfully lead an iStore. The programme combines practical in-store training, mentorship, workshops and formal assessments to build your management and operational capabilities.
You’ll gain exposure to:
• Store Operations: Daily operations, scheduling, standards and problem-solving.
• Customer Experience & Sales: Customer engagement, sales performance, KPIs and coaching.
• Finance & Administration: Cash management, reconciliations, controls, compliance and audit.
• Stock, Tech & Repairs: Inventory management, stock accuracy, shrinkage and the customer repair journey.
• Cellular & Omnichannel: Cellular processes, online fulfilment, collections and digital customer journeys.
• People Management: Recruitment, onboarding, scheduling, feedback, accountability and performance management.
• Product Knowledge: Apple products, the Apple ecosystem, systems and required learning.How you’ll learn:
On-the-job training in designated iStores, Store Manager mentorship, monthly workshops, product and systems training, practical assignments and competency assessments, supported by a structured training workbook and formal sign-off.
You need to have:
• Matric / Grade 12.
• Approximately 2-3 years' experience in retail, hospitality, customer service or another operational environment is advantageous.
• Some exposure to supervising, coordinating or leading others would be beneficial.
• Comfortable working in a fast-paced, customer-facing environment.
• Willing and able to work retail trading hours.
• Flexibility to work across designated Gauteng stores as required.
• Willingness to learn all aspects of store operations.
Apply today!

As a Growth Executive, you will be responsible for identifying, acquiring, activating, and growing new merchants across Lesaka's Card Acquiring portfolio. Beyond acquiring merchants, you'll identify opportunities to cross-sell and upsell additional Lesaka solutions, including cash management and lending products, creating long-term value for both your customers and the business.

Drive Uptime and Lead Engineering Excellence in FMCG!
When a high-speed production plant is humming, it takes a brilliant leader behind the scenes to make sure nothing skips a beat.
Step into the fast-paced FMCG manufacturing sector in the Western Cape, where you will take the reins as Maintenance Manager.
In this vital role, you won't just be putting out fires, you’ll be leading a talented team of technicians, spearheading preventive maintenance programs, managing budgets, and keeping plant equipment running at maximum efficiency.
If you thrive on strategic problem-solving, love optimizing workshop operations, and want your leadership to directly protect plant uptime and profitability, this is your next big career milestone.
Requirements & Qualifications
• Education: National Diploma or Degree in Mechanical or Electrical Engineering, or a relevant trade qualification.
• Experience: Minimum of 5 years of experience in a maintenance management role (including workshop or facility management), ideally within the food manufacturing industry.
• Technical Knowledge: Strong mechanical, electrical, and plumbing expertise, alongside experience with maintenance management systems like Pragma.
• Competencies: Proven leadership and team management capabilities, strong budgeting and cost-control skills, and a solid working knowledge of health, safety, and legal compliance.

job_title: Chief Financial Officer (CFO) - 5 Year Fixed Term Contract
about_role:
The Water Research Commission (WRC) is a dynamic hub for water and sanitation knowledge, innovation and intellectual capital, providing leadership and undertakes research, development and innovation of water and sanitation solutions. It engages stakeholders and partners involving water and sanitation challenges and opportunities, which are crucial to South-Africa’s sustainable development and economic growth and is committed to promoting a better quality of life for all. The WRC is a schedule 3A public entity and adherence to all relevant legislation is imperative to the organization’s strategy and values.
Applications are invited from suitably qualified, experienced and passionate individuals for the Pretoria-based position of:
CHIEF FINANCIAL OFFICER (REF: CFO)
5 -YEAR FIXED-TERM CONTRACT
The Chief Financial Officer (CFO) role at the Water Research Commission (WRC) is a fixed-term executive position requiring a highly qualified, results-driven financial professional. The ideal candidate should have strong financial management, strategic planning, problem-solving, leadership, and decision-making skills. The CFO will be responsible for overseeing the organisation’s financial operations, ensuring sound financial governance, effective resource management, compliance, and supporting the WRC in achieving its strategic objectives. The successful candidate will report to the Chief Executive Officer.
The Chief Financial Officer will be responsible for the development and implementation of the finance strategy; accountable for internal and external audit results; ensure compliance; provide strategic financial support to Board and EXCO; ensure effective and efficient functioning of the Finance Branch; drive performance excellence and demonstrate exemplary leadership behaviours.
Suitable applicants must be in possession of an Honours Degree or Post-graduate qualification (NQF level 8) in Accounting or Finance related field. Chartered Accountant (CA) or equivalent professional qualification would be an added advantage. MBA/MBL/MCOM (NQF level 9) or other equivalent Internationally recognised Finance qualification will also be an added advantage. 10 years’ Financial Management experience is required of which at least 5 years should be at Senior Management level. Experience within the Public Sector would be an added advantage.
The appointment will be made in line with the WRC’s employment equity plan and individuals with a disability and designated groups are encouraged to apply. Applications must be submitted to Human Resources at  response3@multilead.co.za and CVs should contain at least three (3) references. No hand delivered applications will be accepted.
Closing date will be 04 September 2026. If you are not contacted by 31 January 2027, please consider your application as unsuccessful.

• Competencies: Willingness to handle mechanical and refrigeration work, availability for standby and shift work (including mechanical and electrical standby two weeks per month), mentoring apprentices, plus a valid driver's license and own transport.
