The Stock Controller is responsible for maintaining accurate, well-organised, and readily traceable inventory across PABT's warehouse and stores environment. The role owns the day-to-day flow of stock from goods receipt through to issue and dispatch and the integrity of the bin location system
Key Responsibilities
• Manage and monitor the end-to-end movement of stock: goods receiving, put-away, internal transfers, picking, issuing to production, and dispatch to customers
• Monitor stock levels against min/max and re-order thresholds, and flag shortages, slow-moving or obsolete stock to the Warehouse Manager
• Track incoming deliveries and outgoing shipments, ensuring paperwork (delivery notes, GRNs, picking slips, invoices) matches physical stock movements
• Investigate and resolve stock discrepancies between physical counts and system records, identifying root causes and corrective actions
• Own and maintain the warehouse bin location system, ensuring every stock item has a designated, logical, and system-recorded location
• Allocate and update bin locations for new stock lines, considering item size, weight, turnover rate, and picking efficiency
• Ensure all bin locations are correctly labelled
• Conduct regular bin location audits and cycle counts, correcting mismatches between physical placement and system data
• Perform regular cycle counts and assist with full annual stocktakes
• Ensure compliance with company procedures, health & safety standards, and housekeeping standards (5S or similar) within the warehouse
• Identify and recommend process improvements to reduce stock losses, picking errors, and turnaround timesMinimum Requirements and skills
• Grade 12 / Matric certificate (essential).
• A relevant qualification in Logistics, Supply Chain Management, Warehousing, or Inventory Management (advantageous).
• Proficient in Microsoft Excel for stock reporting and analysis
• Strong organisational skills, with the ability to manage multiple stock movements
• Good numeracy and problem-solving skills for resolving stock discrepancies
• 2–4 years' experience in a stock control, inventory, or warehouse role, ideally within a manufacturing, engineering, or industrial parts environment
• Experience with cycle counting and stocktake processes.

About the Role
Lesaka’s Enterprise Division operates at the intersection of regulated payments and technology. Its products are built and distributed on software platforms - digital channels, APIs, integrations and the data infrastructure behind them - and the legal work follows accordingly. This is as much a technology law role as a payments law role, and the successful candidate will be expected to be genuinely interested in how the products work.
The role attends to the day-to-day legal requirements arising from the Enterprise Division, under instruction from the division’s Head of Legal and the management team, and works alongside the existing legal counsel across the Lesaka Group. It is a junior position, with structured support, supervision and mentorship as experience builds.
Key Responsibilities
Commercial and technology contracting
• Draft, review, comment on and assist in negotiating the agreements relevant to the conduct of the business - arrangements with suppliers, customers, distributors and business partners, and customer-facing terms and conditions.
• Technology contracting specifically: software licensing and SaaS, development and systems integration agreements, API and platform terms, cloud and hosting arrangements, data processing and information security schedules, service levels, and intellectual property ownership and licensing.
• Digital channel documentation - application, USSD and web terms of use, privacy notices, consent flows and electronic contracting mechanics.
• Interpret and advise on existing contractual arrangements across the commercial and technology estate.Payments, risk and regulatory
• Advise on the legal and regulatory position applicable to the business within the National Payment System and support new product development from the design stage by assessing the regulatory perimeter early.
• Attend to data privacy in practice: POPIA compliance, cross-border transfer arrangements, data subject requests, and legal support when a security incident arises.
• Identify and assess legal risk across the products, platforms, processes and functions, develop practical mitigation strategies, and stay abreast of developments in the payments, technology, data and consumer frameworks.
• Assist with litigation, disputes and regulatory queries, including instructing and liaising with external counsel, and provide administration and other legal-related support to Lesaka ADP.Qualifications and Experience
• A Bachelor of Laws (LLB) from an accredited university within South Africa.
• An admitted attorney of the High Court of South Africa with at least 1 year post-admission experience, gained at a solid South African law firm, or in an in-house legal team.
• Experience drafting, reviewing and negotiating commercial agreements, with the appetite to be developed on more complex technology and payments transactions.
• Advantageous: knowledge of the frameworks applicable to the business - the National Payment System Act and applicable SARB directives and position papers; the Protection of Personal Information Act, Electronic Communications and Transactions Act and Cybercrimes Act; the Consumer Protection Act and National Credit Act; and the Financial Intelligence Centre Act and Companies Act.
• Advantageous: exposure to technology contracting, or a demonstrated aptitude for it. Candidates comfortable reading an integration flow or a product specification - and who can hold a credible conversation with an engineer or product manager - will have a distinct advantage.Competencies
• A commercial approach rather than technical legalese - advice that enables a decision.
• Takes initiative: arrives with a proposed solution rather than a problem and follows through without being chased.
• Able to run routine matters from instruction to conclusion, with the judgement to know when to escalate, and self-directed in building an understanding of unfamiliar products and frameworks.
• Excellent analytical skills and impeccable attention to detail.
• Collaborates across product, engineering, operations, commercial and finance teams, and translates between technical and legal language in both directions.
• Organised, and able to prioritise a varied workload under pressure without dropping quality.

Role Purpose
The Sourcing Specialist is responsible for securing continuity and security of supply through effective sourcing, supplier management, commercial negotiations, tender processes and contract administration. The role supports the achievement of competitive pricing, reduced contractual risk and improved supplier performance while ensuring procurement activities align with business, supply chain and financial objectives.
Key Responsibilities
Sourcing & Procurement
• Identify, evaluate and select suitable suppliers based on quality, cost, capability and business requirements.
• Analyse market dynamics, cost drivers, supplier alternatives and areas of innovation to support sourcing decisions.
• Manage procurement processes from sourcing and supplier evaluation through to appointment and implementation.
• Develop and maintain sourcing strategies for key or high-risk categories.
• Support the preparation and execution of procurement plans and sourcing activities.
• Ensure procurement activities comply with relevant policies, procedures, legislation and BBBEE requirements. Supplier & Contract Management
• Manage a portfolio of suppliers and monitor supplier performance against agreed requirements and service levels.
• Build and maintain effective supplier relationships and address performance gaps.
• Negotiate commercial terms, pricing, service levels and contractual requirements with suppliers.
• Manage contracts, including contract administration, service-level agreements, amendments and changes.
• Identify opportunities to renegotiate, improve or replace supplier arrangements where required.
• Monitor contract compliance, supplier deliverables and associated risks. Tender & Bid Management
• Prepare and coordinate Requests for Proposals (RFPs), Requests for Tenders (RFTs) and other sourcing documentation.
• Gather and analyse information relating to tender requirements and assess feasibility.
• Coordinate tender evaluation processes and ensure the correct evaluation criteria and methodology are applied.
• Analyse supplier proposals, pricing and commercial submissions and provide recommendations.
• Coordinate stakeholder input and communication throughout the tender process.
• Ensure tender submissions and procurement documentation are complete, accurate and submitted within required timelines. Commercial & Financial Management
• Analyse supplier pricing, cost structures and commercial information to identify value and cost-saving opportunities.
• Apply financial and quantitative information to support procurement and sourcing decisions.
• Assist with costing, budgeting and expenditure management relating to procurement activities.
• Evaluate the overall commercial value, risks and benefits of alternative sourcing solutions.
• Monitor supplier invoices, payments and contractual financial obligations where applicable. Data, Analysis & Reporting
• Collect, analyse and interpret procurement, supplier and market data to support decision-making.
• Identify trends, cost drivers, supplier risks and opportunities for improvement.
• Prepare accurate procurement, supplier performance, tender and management reports.
• Maintain accurate procurement records, supplier information and supporting documentation.
• Ensure information is properly captured, structured, controlled and accessible. Stakeholder Management
• Build effective working relationships with internal stakeholders, suppliers and external partners.
• Understand and balance the requirements of multiple stakeholders when developing sourcing solutions.
• Communicate procurement requirements, recommendations and commercial outcomes clearly.
• Negotiate effectively with stakeholders and suppliers to achieve mutually beneficial outcomes.
• Escalate procurement, supplier and contractual risks appropriately. Administration & Process Improvement
• Provide effective administrative support across sourcing, procurement and contract management activities.
• Prepare routine correspondence, reports, tender documentation and procurement records.
• Maintain appropriate documentation and audit trails throughout procurement processes.
• Identify opportunities to optimise procurement processes, systems and ways of working.
• Support continuous improvement and the implementation of efficient procurement practices.
• Maintain knowledge of relevant legislation, regulations, technology, market developments and industry best practice.

Harness Pro, a specialist manufacturer of electrical wiring harnesses for the automotive, mining, rail, agriculture, military, marine, and bus and truck industries, and we are looking for an accomplished General Manager to lead our Richards Bay and Johannesburg-based manufacturing operations.
This is a senior operational and commercial leadership position requiring more than traditional factory-management experience. The successful candidate will assume full accountability for the performance, stability and future development of the business, bringing together production excellence, financial discipline, customer delivery, employee engagement and continuous improvement.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
Operational and production leadership
• Assume full accountability for the day-to-day performance of the manufacturing operation.
• Translate customer demand and forecasts into credible production, labour, material and capacity plans.
• Ensure effective production scheduling, line balancing, workflow management and allocation of resources.
• Drive output, productivity, quality, OTIF delivery and cost-per-unit performance.
• Identify and resolve production bottlenecks, material shortages, equipment constraints and process inefficiencies.
• Reduce scrap, rework, wire recuts, material wastage and avoidable overtime.
• Ensure the integrity of BOMs, production data, job packs and related master data.
• Maintain effective coordination between Production, Engineering, Planning, Quality, Stores, Procurement, Customer Service, Finance and HR. Commercial and financial management
• Take accountability for the profitability and financial sustainability of the business.
• Manage budgets, forecasts, operating expenditure, gross margin and working-capital performance.
• Analyse production and financial data and convert it into practical corrective action.
• Identify opportunities for cost optimisation, operational growth and customer diversification.
• Prepare and submit accurate monthly executive reports and rolling operational plans.
• Present business performance, risks and recovery plans to executive management and the Board where required. People leadership and employee relations
• Provide visible, fair and consistent leadership across the operation.
• Rebuild trust between employees, supervisors and management through honest communication, follow-through and respectful engagement.
• Lead effectively within a unionised environment and maintain constructive relationships with employee representatives and organised labour.
• Address conflict and employee concerns diplomatically while maintaining appropriate standards, discipline and accountability.
• Develop supervisors and managers, clarify responsibilities and establish measurable performance expectations.
• Create a culture in which employees understand the production plan, customer expectations and their contribution to business performance. Technology and continuous improvement
• Champion the effective use of ERP systems, production data, digital dashboards and management information.
• Improve planning accuracy, production visibility, traceability and data-based decision-making.
• Drive lean manufacturing, root-cause analysis, standardised work and continuous-improvement initiatives.
• Evaluate appropriate automation, equipment and manufacturing technology that will improve quality, capacity and efficiency.
• Ensure that system and production data—particularly SAP dates, BOMs, material status and order information—are accurate and actively managed. Quality, safety and governance
• Maintain compliance with applicable quality, safety and environmental standards.
• Ensure effective internal controls, audit readiness, risk management and statutory compliance.
• Promote a zero-harm culture and ensure that operational pressure never compromises safety or product quality.
• Maintain disciplined quality controls throughout the manufacturing and testing process. This role will suit a commercially minded manufacturing leader who is equally comfortable reviewing a margin report, interrogating a production schedule, walking a manufacturing line, engaging a key customer and having a difficult but respectful conversation with employees or union representatives.
The successful candidate should be:
• Diplomatic, emotionally intelligent and credible.
• Decisive without being authoritarian.
• Fair, consistent and accountable.
• Technologically confident and data-driven.
• Commercially astute and financially disciplined.
• Structured, resilient and calm under pressure.
• A strong communicator across production-floor, customer, union and Board environments.
• Capable of stabilising an operation while building its longer-term capability. Key Performance Areas
Performance will be measured against defined operational and leadership outcomes, including:
• Gross margin performance.
• Operating costs against budget.
• On-time and in-full delivery.
• Production quality, scrap and rework.
• Labour productivity and overtime control.
• Rolling production and capacity planning.
• Supervisor and management performance.
• Customer satisfaction and recovery-plan execution.
• Safety, audit and governance compliance.
• Employee engagement and labour-relations stability.
• Timely and accurate executive reporting.
If you are a progressive manufacturing leader who can combine operational discipline with strong, human-centred leadership, we invite you to apply.

Location: Lynnwood
Industry: Operational Systems / Data Governance
Employment Type: Permanent
Urgency: Immediate
Salary: R50,000 CTC per month (negotiable)
Introduction
An established organisation in Lynnwood is seeking an experienced Data Analyst to take full ownership of data integrity, workflow monitoring, and controlled data movement across multiple operational systems.
This role carries real accountability: ensuring reliable data flow, preventing data loss, identifying risks, and implementing practical solutions that support business continuity and operational excellence.

Role Purpose
The Bookkeeper is responsible for managing the day-to-day accounting, payroll, reconciliations, statutory submissions and financial administration of the business. The role ensures accurate financial records, effective cash and creditor controls, timeous payroll processing, compliance with statutory requirements, and accurate month-end and year-end reporting.
The incumbent will also oversee the accounting office and provide financial and administrative support to management and the Directors.
Key Responsibilities
Accounting & Financial Administration
• Capture and process all financial transactions on the approved accounting system.
• Perform bank reconciliations covering cash, EFTs, card transactions, debtor deposits and company payments.
• Process and reconcile creditor accounts and ensure payments are made within approved terms and limits.
• Complete month-end creditor statement reconciliations and investigate discrepancies.
• Manage month-end accounting procedures and prepare monthly and year-end financial reports.
• Maintain accurate accounting records through trial balance.
• Apply sound accrual accounting principles across the accounting function.
• Complete and maintain financial documentation required for credit applications and audits.
• Assist with year-end audit preparation by providing accurate financial information and supporting documentation.
• Manage and resolve accounting and financial queries, escalating material issues to the Directors. Payroll Administration
• Manage and process monthly payroll, including salary and wage calculations and payments.
• Capture and maintain accurate payroll data on the approved payroll system.
• Process and reconcile statutory and employee-related deductions, including PAYE, UIF, SDL, provident funds, medical aid, garnishee orders and relevant union deductions.
• Investigate and resolve payroll queries timeously.
• Maintain accurate employee payroll and leave records in liaison with HR.
• Prepare and submit relevant employment-related reports, including WRA or IOD documentation, within prescribed timelines.
• Liaise with bargaining councils, statutory bodies and other relevant organisations where required. Tax & Statutory Compliance
• Prepare, reconcile and submit VAT201 and EMP201 returns and ensure payments are made within statutory deadlines.
• Assist with EMP501 mid-year and annual reconciliations and submissions.
• Maintain accurate supporting documentation for all statutory submissions.
• Ensure compliance with applicable financial, payroll, tax, POPIA/PAIA and other legislative requirements. Reconciliations & Financial Controls
• Perform regular and accurate bank, creditor, payroll and balance sheet reconciliations.
• Investigate and resolve reconciliation discrepancies.
• Maintain effective financial controls and ensure transactions are properly authorised and recorded.
• Manage the site change float and ensure all checks, balances and monthly reconciliations are completed.
• Manage and safeguard petty cash and ensure all transactions are properly recorded and supported.
• Report any financial discrepancies or control weaknesses to the Directors. Records & Filing
• Maintain an accurate, organised and confidential filing system for financial, payroll and employee records.
• Ensure records are retained and archived in accordance with company standards and statutory requirements.
• Maintain employee records and documentation in liaison with HR.
• Ensure financial and employee information is handled in accordance with POPIA/PAIA requirements. Management & General Administration
• Manage the accounting office and coordinate day-to-day accounting activities.
• Monitor the accuracy and timeliness of accounting inputs performed by other administrative employees.
• Provide guidance and support to employees regarding finance, payroll and accounting queries.
• Liaise regularly with Directors and senior management regarding financial and accounting matters.
• Ensure delegated accounting responsibilities are properly completed and controlled.
• Perform additional accounting and administrative duties as reasonably required by management.

Job Purpose:
The National Sales Manager designs and executes the commercial sales strategy to drive revenue growth, market share, and brand presence across all retail and wholesale channels. This role leads, mentors, and holds accountable regional sales teams, key account managers, and field forces. The position ensures optimal product availability, excellent in-store execution, and maximum profitability while building sustainable long-term partnerships with major retail chains, distributors, and independent traders
Duties and Responsibilities:
Strategic Planning & Commercial Growth:
Develop and implement comprehensive annual sales plans, forecasting models, and market expansion strategies aligned with overall corporate objectives.
Analyze market trends, competitor activities, consumer behavior, and demographic data to identify new business opportunities and threats.
Allocate regional sales targets, commercial budgets, and resource distribution to maximize return on investment (ROI).
Collaborate with Marketing and Product Development teams to align trade promotions, product launches, and brand strategies with field execution capability.
Channel & Key Account Management:
Oversee relationships with top-tier modern trade (supermarkets, hypermarkets), traditional trade (wholesalers, independent mom-and-pop stores), and e-commerce accounts.
Lead annual joint business planning (JBP) negotiations regarding trading terms, listing fees, margins, rebates, and promotional slots.
Ensure optimal product assortment, stock depth, and promotional compliance across all trading channels.
Intervene directly in high-stakes negotiations or operational bottlenecks with major distributors and retail buyers.
Team Leadership & Performance Management:
Recruit, train, mentor, and manage regional sales managers, key account executives, and field forces.
Establish clear, measurable performance benchmarks and conduct regular monthly and quarterly performance reviews.
Design and implement competitive commission structures, incentive programs, and sales contests to motivate the field force.
Conduct regular field visits to coach team members on negotiation skills, relationship building, and route-to-market efficiency.
Trade Marketing & In-Store Execution:
Partner with the Trade Marketing team to design and deploy point-of-sale materials (POSM), endcaps, and secondary displays.
Enforce strict compliance with Planograms, share of shelf (SOS) agreements, and pricing structures across all outlets.
Monitor and optimize the field force routing plans to maximize store visit frequencies and reduce travel overheads.
Direct the execution of trade activations, sampling campaigns, and seasonal promotional events.
Supply Chain Collaboration & Financial Governance:
Provide accurate rolling sales forecasts to the Supply Chain and Production teams to minimize out-of-stock (OOS) situations and prevent excess inventory.
Manage the departmental sales budget, tracking commercial spend, travel allowances, and promotional discounts.
Monitor customer credit limits, payment histories, and outstanding receivables to minimize bad debts and improve cash flow.
Review profitability reports by product line, region, and channel to eliminate low-margin practices.
Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) & Measurables:
Financial Metrics:
Revenue Target Attainment: Percentage of monthly, quarterly, and annual gross and net sales value achieved versus budget.
Gross Profit Margin: Maintenance of targeted profit margins across specific product portfolios and sales channels.
Trade Spend Efficiency: Return on investment (ROI) on promotional spend, rebates, and discounts, measured as a percentage of net sales.
Days Sales Outstanding (DSO): Average time taken to collect payments from accounts, keeping write-offs below a defined threshold (e.g., <0.5% of sales).
Sales Volume & Distribution Metrics:
Numeric and Weighted Distribution: Percentage of target retail outlets stocking the core product portfolio (Numeric) and the volume share of those shops (Weighted).
Volume Growth (Tonnage/Cases): Total volume growth of units or cases shipped compared to the previous financial year.
New Account Acquisition: Number of high-volume retail outlets, wholesalers, or distributors successfully onboarded and activated each quarter.
Strike Rate / Order Conversion: The ratio of successful orders taken relative to the total number of customer visits made by the field team.
In-Store Execution Metrics:
Share of Shelf (SOS): Percentage of linear shelf space secured for the company's brands relative to direct competitors.
On-Shelf Availability (OSA) / Out-of-Stock (OOS) Rate: Minimizing out-of-stock incidents at the shelf level, aiming for an OSA score of 95% or higher.
Planogram and Pricing Compliance: Audit scores measuring team adherence to agreed corporate shelf layouts and recommended retail pricing (RRP).
POSM Deployment: Percentage of targeted stores with fully functional, approved trade marketing materials placed in high-traffic locations.
Team Capability & Operational Metrics:
Sales Force Automation (SFA) Adoption: Team compliance with daily CRM logging, route tracking, and digital order processing tools.
Retention and Talent Development:Annual turnover rate of high-performing sales staff and completion rates for team functional training modules

Job Summary:
The Financial Manager serves as a core strategic partner to the executive team, directing the financial operations, accounting functions, and capital management of the organization. This position ensures absolute financial compliance, designs rigorous internal controls, and manages the annual budgeting and forecasting processes. The Financial Manager transforms complex accounting data into actionable insights, driving cost-efficiency, profitability, and sustainable business growth across all operational departments
Key Responsibilities and Performance Goals:
1. Financial Reporting and Corporate Governance:
Compile Statements: Direct the preparation of accurate, monthly, quarterly, and annual financial statements, including balance sheets, income statements, and cash flow analysis.
Ensure Standards: Guarantee that all accounting entries and disclosures comply strictly with relevant financial reporting frameworks (e.g., IFRS or GAAP) and statutory tax regulations.
Lead Audits: Coordinate the entire external audit process, acting as the primary point of contact for auditors, resolving technical inquiries, and closing audit cycles on schedule.
Maintain Ledger: Oversee the integrity of the general ledger, reconciliations, fixed asset registers, and subsidiary ledgers managed by the accounting team.
2. Financial Planning, Budgeting, and Forecasting:
Drive Budgeting: Lead the annual corporate budget formulation, working with department heads to build justifiable revenue projections and expense limits.
Analyze Variance: Conduct monthly budget-versus-actual variance analyses, identifying operational inefficiencies and proposing corrective actions to executive management.
Build Models: Develop rolling cash flow forecasts and mid-to-long term financial models to evaluate capital constraints, profitability pipelines, and growth targets.
3. Treasury and Capital Management:
Optimize Liquidity: Monitor daily corporate liquidity, manage working capital requirements, and optimize banking relationships to secure competitive credit facilities.
Evaluate Investments: Conduct financial feasibility studies, net present value (NPV) analyses, and internal rate of return (IRR) calculations for proposed capital projects or investments.
Manage Tax: Oversee corporate tax planning, ensuring timely and accurate compliance with corporate income tax, VAT, payroll taxes, and statutory filings.
4. Internal Controls and Organizational Leadership:
Mitigate Risk: Design, enforce, and audit internal financial controls to safeguard company assets, minimize risk, and prevent fraud or operational waste.
Direct Staff: Provide leadership, performance management, and continuous technical training to the corporate accounting and corporate finance personnel
Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and Targets:
Financial Closing Timeline: Complete the monthly financial close process and deliver reporting packages within 5 business days following month-end.
Forecast Accuracy Ratio: Maintain a forecast variance of less than ±3% for quarterly revenue and operational expenditure projections.
Audit Compliance Index: Achieve a clean, unqualified external audit opinion annually with zero material weaknesses or significant deficiencies identified.
Working Capital Optimization: Optimize the working capital cycle to increase the current ratio to a target range between 1.5 and 2.0.
Budget Variance Threshold: Limit unapproved departmental budget overruns to 0%through proactive monthly expense monitoring and system-enforced alerts

Regional Director | GWK
Lead a Region. Shape the Future.
Introduction to the VKB Group
The VKB Group is an agricultural company, providing support to farmers and producing straight-from-the farm-foods for consumers. Apart from the various consumer brands, the VKB Group is also represented by its regional brands: VKB, GWK and NTK. Our roots are firmly planted in agriculture with farming at our core, continuously growing and evolving throughout the years.
Starting with providing everything needed on the farm to produce food, we now also operate in all areas of the food supply chain: processing, logistics, and national and global market channels.
This “house of brands” we’ve established with the support of our farmer shareholders is the foundation for building the agribusiness of the future.
About the Role
GWK is seeking an exceptional executive leader to take responsibility for one of the organisation's most strategically important regions. This is an opportunity for a commercially astute and relationship-driven leader to influence regional strategy, unlock growth opportunities, strengthen market positioning, and build a high-performing culture that delivers sustainable value.
Reporting directly to the Group CEO, the Regional Director will provide strategic leadership across a diverse regional portfolio, ensuring strong financial performance, operational excellence, governance, and long-term growth. The successful candidate will play a pivotal role in connecting people, strategy, and market opportunity while strengthening GWK's presence and impact across the region.
This role is ideally suited to a proven executive who combines strong financial and commercial acumen with exceptional people leadership and the ability to build trusted relationships at every level.
What You'll Be Responsible For
Strategic & Commercial Leadership
• Lead the development and execution of regional strategy aligned with GWK's long-term objectives.
• Identify and capitalise on growth, trading, and market opportunities that strengthen regional and organisational performance.
• Contribute to executive decision-making and strategic planning at Group level.
• Drive sustainable profitability and strengthen GWK's competitive position within the region.Financial Performance & Business Growth
• Oversee regional financial performance, including budgeting, forecasting, reporting, and performance management.
• Apply strong commercial and financial insight to support trading opportunities and business decision-making.
• Facilitate business development initiatives and expansion opportunities across the region.
• Ensure resources are optimally utilised to maximise return and value creation.Leadership & Culture
• Inspire and lead high-performing teams across multiple business and support functions.
• Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, execution excellence, and continuous improvement.
• Build strong partnerships with internal and external stakeholders, customers, and industry partners.
• Champion the development of a world-class regional culture where people thrive and perform at their best.Governance & Operational Excellence
• Ensure sound governance, compliance, risk management, and operational discipline.
• Strengthen collaboration across business units to improve efficiency, service delivery, and organisational effectiveness.
• Drive alignment between strategy, operations, and people to achieve sustainable business outcomes.Who We're Looking For
You are a respected executive leader known for your commercial judgement, financial expertise, and ability to bring people together behind a common vision.
You can confidently move between boardroom strategy and operational execution, balancing growth ambitions with disciplined business management. Most importantly, you build trust naturally and create environments where strong relationships, collaboration, and performance flourish.
Your leadership style is characterised by credibility, humility, influence, and a genuine commitment to developing people and strengthening culture.
Minimum Requirements
• Relevant postgraduate qualification in Finance, Accounting, Business, Agriculture, or a related field.
• More than 10 years' senior leadership experience with increasing levels of responsibility.
• Proven experience in financial leadership, strategic planning, and business performance management.
• Demonstrated success in driving business growth, market expansion, or commercial development initiatives.
• Experience leading diverse teams and functions within a complex organisation.
• Strong understanding of governance, risk management, compliance, and performance management.
• Exposure to agriculture, agribusiness, commodity markets, or a diversified group environment will be advantageous.Success Profile
The ideal candidate will demonstrate:
• Exceptional commercial and financial acumen.
• Strong strategic thinking and decision-making capability.
• Outstanding relationship-building and stakeholder management skills.
• Executive presence and credibility.
• The ability to influence and align diverse stakeholders.
• Sound judgement in complex and dynamic environments.
• Resilience, adaptability, and a results-driven mindset.
• A passion for people leadership, team development, and culture building.Why Join GWK?
This is more than a regional leadership role.
It is an opportunity to influence the future of one of South Africa's leading agricultural businesses, contribute at executive level, and leave a lasting legacy through sustainable growth, strong partnerships, and exceptional leadership.
If you are a visionary leader with the commercial capability, leadership maturity, and relationship-building strengths to make a meaningful impact, we invite you to apply.
Lead with purpose. Grow with impact. Shape the future with GWK.

The Warehouse Optimization Manager is responsible for improving warehouse efficiency by analyzing, designing, and implementing effective processes, systems, and workflows. Process Improvement & Workflow Optimisation

Cost Reduction & Efficiency
• Identify cost-saving opportunities within warehouse operations, including labor, storage, and handling.

• Monitor and report on cost efficiency and operational performance.
• Drive initiatives to reduce waste, rework, and inefficiencies.
Performance Monitoring & Reporting
• Define and track key performance indicators (KPIs) for warehouse operations.
• Prepare reports on productivity, efficiency, accuracy, and cost metrics.
• Provide actionable insights and recommendations to management.
Training & Change Management
• Train warehouse staff and supervisors on new systems, processes, and procedures.
• Drive adoption of best practices and continuous improvement culture.
• Support operational teams during implementation and transition phases.

Summary:
We are looking for intelligent and motivated graduates to join our Onboarding team as Financial Assessors, ultimately progressing into the Financial Consultant role within 6-12 months. First, you will gather their information and then you’ll provide them with an initial/light assessment of their financial position and educate them about the ways in which we can help them with our solutions.

job_title: Senior Infrastructure Demand Management Server Coordinator
about_role:
ROLE PURPOSE
The Senior Infrastructure Demand Management – Server Lead is accountable for end‑to‑end ownership and governance of server infrastructure demand across physical, virtual, and cloud environments. The role provides senior technical and service leadership to ensure that infrastructure demand is optimally planned, prioritised, governed, and delivered in alignment with business strategy, client commitments, security standards, and service management frameworks.
The incumbent acts as the primary authority on server demand intake, demand shaping, and delivery readiness, translating complex business and project requirements into executable infrastructure demand plans. The role operates with a high degree of autonomy, influencing delivery outcomes across multiple technical teams, and ensuring infrastructure demand is delivered predictably, compliantly, and at scale.
ROLE REQUIREMENT
• Strategic Infrastructure Demand Ownership
• Own and govern the server infrastructure demand pipeline across physical, virtual, and cloud platforms.
• Shape demand through early engagement with business, programme, and project stakeholders to ensure feasibility, cost awareness, and technical alignment.
• Act as the senior escalation point for complex or high‑risk infrastructure demand initiatives.
• Influence prioritisation decisions to balance capacity, risk, cost, and delivery commitments.
• Senior Build Governance & Delivery Enablement
• Translate approved demand into standardised, scalable build architectures and demand artefacts for execution by infrastructure engineering teams.
• Provide senior oversight of server build readiness, ensuring all technical, security, and operational prerequisites are met before execution.
• Govern complex builds, migrations, and environment expansions, including hybrid and cloud‑integrated solutions.
• Ensure infrastructure delivery adheres to agreed architectural, operational, and service standards.
• Service Management Leadership & SLA Assurance
• Provide senior operational leadership across the full lifecycle of infrastructure requests, from demand intake to production handover.
• Monitor delivery performance against SLAs, KPIs, and contractual commitments, proactively addressing systemic issues.
• Drive alignment with ITIL practices across Incident, Change, Problem, and Release processes.
• Champion service stability, predictability, and continuous service improvement.
• CMDB, Data Integrity & Asset Governance
• Own the accuracy, integrity, and auditability of server configuration items within the CMDB.
• Define and enforce standards for CI lifecycle management, data quality, and reconciliation.
• Lead investigations into CMDB discrepancies and implement corrective and preventative actions.
• Ensure infrastructure assets are fully traceable, compliant, and governance‑ready at all times.
• Security, Compliance & Risk Management
• Ensure all server infrastructure demand complies with organisational security, risk, and regulatory requirements prior to production release.
• Coordinate senior‑level sign‑offs with Information Security, Risk, and Compliance stakeholders.
• Identify infrastructure‑related risks early and drive mitigation strategies across delivery teams.
• Support internal and external audits by providing authoritative infrastructure evidence and documentation.
• Reporting, Optimization & Continuous Improvement
• Produce executive‑level reporting on infrastructure demand trends, delivery performance, capacity constraints, and risk exposure.
• Analyze demand data to inform forecasting, capacity planning, and investment decisions.
• Drive continuous improvement initiatives focused on automation, standardization, and process efficiency.
• Act as a thought leader within infrastructure demand management, contributing to best practice and maturity uplift.
PROFESSIONAL COMPETENCIES
• Deep understanding of Windows and Linux server environments (physical, virtual, and cloud)
• Advanced knowledge of virtualisation platforms (e.g. VMware)
• Strong exposure to cloud infrastructure (AWS, Azure, or equivalent)
• Expert use of ITSM tools (e.g. BMC Remedy, ServiceNow, Jira)
• Strong command of ITIL‑aligned service management practices
• Advanced understanding of CMDB architecture and configuration management
• Ability to translate technical complexity into business‑relevant insights
QUALIFICATIONS & EXPERIENCE
• Grade 12
• Diploma or Degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, or related discipline
• 10–15 years’ experience in enterprise ICT infrastructure, with demonstrated senior accountability
• 5+ years’ experience operating in complex, multi‑stakeholder delivery or project environments
• ITIL Foundation certification (required); ITIL Intermediate or equivalent advantageous
• Proven experience across server hardware, operating systems, storage, and networking
• Enterprise‑scale exposure to hybrid and cloud infrastructure environments Experience in server infrastructure (hardware, OS, storage, networking)
• Working knowledge of BMC Remedy or similar ITSM tool
• Exposure to cloud infrastructure (e.g., AWS, Azure) advantageous

Job Purpose:
The Materials Resource Planner is responsible for ensuring that the right materials, components and resources are available at the right time and in the right quantities to support uninterrupted manufacturing operations. The role coordinates demand planning, material requirements, inventory management and supplier performance while balancing production requirements, working capital and customer service objectives.
Key Responsibilities:
Develop and maintain material and resource plans aligned with the production schedule, customer demand and business requirements.
Translate production requirements, bills of materials (BOMs) and forecasts into material requirements and purchasing requirements.
Monitor material availability and identify potential shortages, excesses, obsolete stock and supply risks.
Maintain accurate MRP parameters, including lead times, safety stocks, minimum order quantities and reorder points.
Generate, review and manage planned and firm purchase orders in accordance with MRP recommendations.
Liaise closely with Procurement, Production, Warehousing, Quality, Engineering, Finance and Sales/Customer Service.
Work with suppliers to confirm delivery dates, quantities and capacity commitments.
Expedite critical or delayed materials to prevent production stoppages.
Develop and maintain production and material planning schedules.
Analyse inventory levels and recommend actions to optimise stockholding without compromising production continuity.
Monitor supplier performance and escalate recurring delivery, quality or capacity issues.
Manage material changes arising from engineering changes, new product introductions, product discontinuations and changes to production requirements.
Participate in capacity planning and identify resource constraints that may affect manufacturing output.
Maintain accurate planning data within the ERP/MRP system.
Investigate material variances, planning exceptions and root causes of supply disruptions.
Support continuous improvement initiatives aimed at reducing inventory, improving material availability and increasing planning accuracy.
Prepare and communicate relevant planning, inventory and supplier-performance reports.

Senior Product Manager: Market & Innovation
Location: Cape Town, hybrid   ·   Type: Permanent, full-time   ·   Reports to: Chief Product Officer
About Lesaka
Lesaka Technologies is a Southern African fintech building the connected ecosystem for financial inclusion, transactional banking, lending, insurance, payments and cash management for merchants, consumers and enterprise clients across the region. We’re publicly listed (Nasdaq: LSAK / JSE: LSK) and growing fast. EasyPay powers airtime, data, electricity, vouchers and 600+ bill payments through the largest retail footprint in South Africa.
The role
This role decides what’s worth building. You own the intelligence and opportunity pipeline across our entire product portfolio; vouchers, virtual products, bill payments and utilities, turning market signal, competitor moves and customer demand into a prioritised stream of validated ideas. Your role is to bring substantiated opportunity; you define the product; engineering builds it.
What you’ll own
• Maintain a live view of the competitive landscape- categories, fees, UX, partner coverage and flag gaps and threats before they hurt us.
• Run the innovation pipeline: new voucher categories, bundles and novel selling constructs, framed as testable hypotheses rather than pet projects.
• Gather signal from partners, sales, market trends and customers and filter it ruthlessly into a ranked, defensible opportunity list.
• Identify cross-vertical levers, such as using vouchers to drive adoption of other products, and size the upside.
• Write clear problem statements and opportunity cases; hand engineering the what and why, not a spec.
• Partner with Commercial on price and revenue cases, and measure adoption and validation post-launch.
What you bring
• 5+ years in product management, ideally in fintech, payments, retail or telco/VAS.
• A track record of taking new products from market insight to launch.
• Strong competitor analysis and market research instincts, you teardown rivals as a habit, not a once-a-year deck.
• The judgement to filter noise from real patterns and say no to fads.
• Fluency working with commercial, engineering and partner stakeholders.
• Comfort owning outcomes (adoption, validation) without owning the day-to-day build.
Nice to have
• Experience with voucher, gift-card or VAS ecosystems.
• Exposure to partner and merchant integration models.
Our culture — what we expect from you
Lesaka is a fast-paced fintech. The people who thrive here have a few things in common:
• You don’t wait to be asked. If something is broken or unclear, you call for the ball and fix it.
• Fast adaptation. Priorities shift, markets move, regulations change. You don’t flinch, you re-plan and move.
• Execution mindset. Ideas are cheap. Shipping is the job. You walk slow, run fast: think it through, then move with urgency.
• Customer first. The merchant, consumer or enterprise client is why we exist. Your decisions trace back to them.If you’d rather optimise a process to perfection over six months than ship something useful in six weeks, this won’t be the right fit.

about_role:
KINDLY TAKE NOTE: Applications may only be submitted online through the official UFS vacancy website: https://ufs.hua.hrsmart.com/hr/ats/JobSearch/viewAll  - Applications submitted through any other platform will not be considered. The system allows a maximum of eight attachments. To avoid upload issues, we recommend merging some or all documents into fewer files before submitting.
INCOMPLETE APPLICATIONS WILL NOT BE CONSIDERED!
To ensure your application is complete, you must submit ALL documents listed under the inherent requirements, as well as the following standard documentation:
•    A detailed Curriculum Vitae.
•    Copies of your qualifications, or official proof of qualifications obtained (If you hold foreign qualifications, please include SAQA accreditation).
•    A copy of your identity document (South African ID or passport for foreign nationals).
•    Confirmation of employment in the form of a letter, appointment contract, service certificate, or recent payslip from your current or most recent employer (applicable to external applicants only).
Duties and responsibilities:
•    Teach undergraduate and postgraduate modules in Economics and Finance, specifically Microeconomics and Macroeconomics, Introduction to Mathematical Economics, Statistics for Economics, Econometrics, International Economics, Development Economics, and Personal Finance.
•    Participate actively in research and publications.
•    Ensure active participation in and contribution to the Faculty’s research activities.
•    Supervise and provide consultation sessions for undergraduate and postgraduate students.
•    Work as a team with colleagues within the faculty.
•    Serve as a member of various academic committees within the faculty and university.
•    Participate in formal self-development programmes within the UFS aimed at strengthening aspirations and skills as a researcher and lecturer.
•    Contribute to research coordination and perform administrative tasks related to the discipline.
Inherent requirements:
Senior Lecturer:
•    PhD on NQF Level 10 in Economics or a related discipline.
•    Proven experience in presenting papers/posters at national and international scholarly conferences.
•    Proven national recognition for specialist expertise and research in a specific area of scholarship.
•    An NRF rating or demonstrated potential for obtaining an NRF rating.
•    Proven experience in successfully supervising master’s degree students through to graduation.
•    A proven research record of relevant publications in peer-reviewed national and international DHET-accredited scientific journals.
•    Demonstrated ability to use Econometric software package(s) such as EViews, Stata, and R
•    Demonstrate sound knowledge and proficiency in coding using Python and apply this in the disciplines of Economics and Finance.
•    Proven experience of service as an active member of a national or international scholarly society or committee or agency concerned with research at higher-education levels.
Associate Professor

Cyber Risk Management

Governance & Security Program Support

Pos Vakature: Spesery-Tegnikus (Monster- en Kleurpassing)
Posbesonderhede:
• Posbenaming: Spesery-Tegnikus (Spice Technician – Sample & Colour Matching)
• Arbeidsveld: Voedselvervaardiging, Speserye en Geurmiddels (Food Manufacturing)
• Werkplek: Roodepoort, Gauteng (Op die perseel / On-site)
Beskrywing van die Pos: Die Kliënt is 'n groeiende speseryvervaardigingsonderneming in Roodepoort wat spesialiseer in hoëgehalte speserye en geurmiddels. Hulle is op soek na 'n vaardige en noukeurige Spesery-Tegnikus om die span te versterk. Die primêre doel van die pos is om kliënte se monsters te ontleed en akkuraat te pas, met 'n spesifieke fokus op kleur, smaak en algehele gehalte—veral ten opsigte van witpeper en ander gemaalde speserye.
Pos Pligte en Sleutelwerksaamhede:
• Monster-analise: Ontvangs en deeglike ontleding van kliëntemonsters vir kleur, aroma, tekstuur en smaak.
• Kleur- en Smaakpassing: Akkurate passing van monsters deur speserye te meng om die presiese kleur en geur te bereik wat aangevra is.
• Monster-produksie: Voorbereiding van monster-duplikate vir kliënt goedkeuring voor produksie.
• Rekordhouding: Hou van akkurate rekords van alle formules en monster-passings.
• Produksie-koördinering: Noue samewerking met die produksiespan om te verseker dat die finale produk streng ooreenstem met die goedgekeurde monster.
• Kwaliteitsbeheer: Uitvoer van gehalteteste op rou moedermateriale sowel as klaar produkte.
• Laboratoriumbestuur: Handhawing van 'n skoon, georganiseerde en higiëniese werkswinkel / monster-laboratorium in ooreenstemming met voedselveiligheidstandaarde.
BOEHOEFTE VEREISTES VIR POS:
• Kritiese Vereistes:
• Uitstekende sensoriese vaardighede: Skerp sin vir kleur (oog vir detail), reuk en smaak.
• Eerlikheid, uiterste netheid en noukeurigheid met metings en weegwerk.
• Goeie kommunikasievaardighede en die vermoë om onafhanklik te funksioneer onder druk.
• Moet in of naby Roodepoort / Wes-Rand woon.
• Voordelige Vereistes:
• Vorige ondervinding in 'n speserymaatskappy, voedselaboratorium of geurmiddels-mengomgewing.
• Matriek of 'n Diploma in Voedseltegnologie (Food Technology).
• Basiese Eienskappe & Voorkeure:
• Aangesien die rol spesifieke laboratorium- en fynmotoriese take behels, word vroulike kandidate verkies.
Werksomgewing:
• Tipe: Voltyds, op die perseel by South Spice International in Roodepoort.

The VKB Group is an agricultural company, providing support to farmers and producing straight-from-the farm-foods for consumers. The successful candidate will be responsible for the maintenance, servicing, repair, and inspection of agricultural equipment and machinery to ensure safe, reliable, and efficient operation. Content Creator
Core objective. Shoot, edit and optimise native short form video and photography that drives awareness, engagement and sales for Curve Gear across TikTok, Instagram, Facebook and YouTube Shorts.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
Content production and editing
• Shoot and capture. Record vertical and horizontal video, clean audio and photography on mobile and studio gear, on location at farms, sites, workshops and stores.
• Rapid editing. Cut raw footage fast in CapCut, DaVinci Resolve or Adobe Premiere Pro with dynamic captions, sound design and pacing built for each platform.
• Format repurposing. Turn single long form assets into multiple high performing short clips. One interview should yield five posts.
• Brand voice. Write hooks, captions, on screen text and calls to action that sound like Curve Gear, not like an advert.
Paid media and UGC creative
• Ad creative. Build creative made to run on Meta and TikTok, not repurposed organic posts.
• Hook testing. Deliver multiple hook variations of every concept so the media buyer can test openings against each other.
• Scaling winners. When an ad performs, cut new angles off it rather than starting from zero.
• UGC production. Script, cast, direct and edit UGC style content. A real person talking to a phone camera about a real experience.
• UGC craft. Hook in the first two seconds. One message, not a feature list. Specific over general. Phone quality on purpose, because over polished UGC stops working.
Strategy and trend agility
• Trend tracking. Monitor audio, formats, comment culture and algorithm shifts daily, and pitch content while the trend is still alive.
• Content pipeline. Source and book real customers and crews. Keep a rolling pipeline of at least six confirmed shoots.
• Cross platform fit. Match content style to the audience on each platform. Facebook carries our core customer, TikTok carries the growth.
Analytics and optimisation
• Performance tracking. Review views, hold rate, watch time, saves and shares weekly across organic and paid.
• Iterative learning. Use what the data says to sharpen the next round of hooks, formats and posting experiments.
• Reporting. Report monthly on what worked, what died and what you are repeating.
REQUIRED SKILLS AND QUALIFICATIONS
Technical skills
• Video and photo software. Proficiency in mobile and desktop editors. CapCut, Adobe Premiere Pro, Photoshop, Lightroom or Canva.
• Production fundamentals. Solid grasp of lighting, framing and clean mobile sound recording.
• Platform native literacy. Deep personal or professional familiarity with how TikTok, Instagram, Facebook and YouTube actually work.
• Copywriting. Hooks, captions and short scripts in plain English.
Soft skills
• Adaptability. Comfortable in a fast environment where priorities shift daily around what is trending.
• Storytelling. Turns brand messaging into human, entertaining content.
• People skills. Puts a stranger at ease on camera in two minutes.
• Resilience. Works early, works in the field, and keeps going when a post flops.
Other requirements
• Valid code B driver's licence, willingness to travel across South Africa and stay overnight where a shoot requires it
• Availability for early morning and occasional weekend shoots
• South African citizenship or a valid work permit
PREFERRED EXPERIENCE
• Portfolio. A live portfolio or active social channel showing content you produced and the engagement it earned.
• Background. One to three years in digital marketing, video production or organic social media management. A relevant diploma or degree is an advantage, not a requirement.
• Paid exposure. Experience producing paid social or UGC ads, and reading creative performance data in Meta Ads Manager.
• Sector. Retail, apparel, agriculture, construction or industrial experience.
WORKING CONDITIONS
• Office based editing combined with regular field work on farms, construction sites, workshops and retail floors
• Travel is required, including overnight stays. Travel and accommodation costs are covered by the company
• Shoots may begin before sunrise. Hours are managed flexibly against a standard full time week
HOW TO APPLY
• A curriculum vitae of no more than two pages
• A link to a portfolio, showreel or social media account showing your own work

Location: Remote (South Africa)
Salary: Negotiable, based on experience
Employment Type: Permanent via Employer of Record (initial 12-month contract)
A growing international organisation operating across legal, finance and global payroll services is expanding its international payroll team. The business works with a diverse client base spanning multiple countries, delivering payroll processing, compliance and advisory services. Alongside those offerings, the team handles HR and employment law coordination, working closely with in-country specialists and partners across Europe and beyond to ensure that every payroll outcome is accurate, compliant and on time. This is a fully remote role based in South Africa, with genuine cross-border exposure from day one.
This is not a high-volume processing role. Think of it more as the central nervous system of an international payroll operation, where your value lies in keeping multiple moving parts aligned, making sure nothing slips through the cracks, and knowing exactly when to act, when to escalate and when to loop in a legal specialist. The successful candidate will collate and quality-check payroll data, manage client communication over email and Teams, liaise with in-country partners across European markets, and coordinate HR and employment law matters including terminations that carry strict country-specific requirements. Local legislative expertise lives with the in-country specialists, so the focus here is on execution, coordination, judgement and client outcomes.
Minimum Requirements
A relevant qualification in accounting, finance, tax or payroll is required
CIMA, SAIPA, AGA or CA qualification is advantageous but not essential
At least 3 years of relevant experience in accounting, payroll or a closely related field, broadly equivalent to a newly qualified SAIPA clerk
Prior hands-on experience with payroll processing, including preparing payroll journal entries
Strong Microsoft Excel skills and comfort working with detailed data and documentation
Exposure to payroll systems and payment tools or platforms is advantageous
Experience working with international clients or cross-border processes is a plus
Excellent written and verbal communication in English
Comfortable working independently in a fully remote environment
Ambitious, with a genuine interest in building a long-term career in international payroll
Key Responsibilities
Process payroll payments for international clients accurately and on time using relevant payment tools and payment files
Understand payroll calculation structures including employee tax, employer tax and statutory requirements across different countries
Check payroll data and payment files for completeness before processing
Prepare journal entries to account for payroll transactions accurately
Communicate with clients over email and Teams to gather required information and follow up on missing details
Answer client questions on international payroll matters, escalating complex legislative questions to in-country specialists as needed
Liaise with local in-country partners across European and other international markets to gather and confirm payroll-related information
Filter and route information appropriately between clients, partners and the legal team
Help interpret and explain country-specific HR and employment law requirements to clients in plain, practical terms
Apply sound judgement to identify when matters, particularly around terminations, need to be escalated to legal or a specialist
Keep clear, organised records of client communications and payroll processing steps
Support project management of international payroll portfolios across multiple countries and partners
Communicate proactively when deadlines or processing agreements are at risk
Build relationships with wider payroll, tax and legal teams across the organisation

Location
Cape Town, South Africa
Reporting To
Chief Operating Officer (COO) – Enterprise
Role Purpose
The Product Manager – Operational Capabilities is accountable for translating the COO's operational capability roadmap into shipped, adopted products that measurably improve how Lesaka Enterprise runs.
The role owns the end-to-end product lifecycle for operational capabilities — onboarding, activation, service management, reconciliation, observability, automation, and operational intelligence — from problem discovery through delivery, adoption, and measured impact.
Where the COO sets the direction for what operational capability the business needs, this role is accountable for building it: defining requirements, sequencing delivery with engineering and business-change partners, and ensuring capabilities are actually adopted and moving the operational metrics they were built to shift.
This is a hands-on, delivery-accountable role. Success is not a roadmap slide — it is a capability in production, in use, with a measurable before-and-after.
Role Context
Lesaka Enterprise's operating environment spans multiple business lines (ADP, Utilities, Transact, Crypto, and future Enterprise businesses), each with distinct operational demands but shared underlying capability needs.
The COO is accountable for a defined set of operational capability domains, and this role is the product owner for building them out. The domains include, but are not limited to:
• Service Operations — IT Operations, Customer Operations, and service/incident management
• Reconciliation & Settlements — multi-way reconciliation, settlement file processing, and financial operations controls
• Onboarding & Activation — customer, merchant, and partner onboarding, and go-live/cutover management
• Operational Analytics & Observability — KPI frameworks, dashboards, and performance visibility
• Operational Automation & AI — workflow automation, AI-enabled tooling, and operational data platforms
• Escalation Management — structured triage and resolution of operational escalationsThe COO function is building an operational capability platform to serve these needs at scale, including workflow automation, AI-enabled operational tooling, operational data and observability platforms, and graph-based operational intelligence.
This role sits inside the COO's team as the product owner for that capability build-out, working closely with the Head of Operations, Head of Business Change, engineering and technology partners, and the business-line operational leads who will use and depend on these capabilities.
Primary Responsibilities
• Product Ownership of Operational CapabilitiesOwn the product backlog and delivery plan across the COO's capability domains — Service Operations, Reconciliation & Settlements, Onboarding & Activation, Operational Analytics, and Automation & AI — translating the roadmap into concrete, sequenced product work.
• Domain-specific requirements: e.g. reconciliation matching logic and control gaps, service-desk escalation workflows, onboarding go-live checklists
• Backlog ownership, prioritisation, and sprint/delivery planning
• Product quality, usability, and fitness for operational purpose — judged against how each domain actually operates, not generic product standards
• Clear definition of done tied to operational outcomes, not just feature completion
• Roadmap Translation & PrioritisationConvert the COO's capability priorities into a sequenced, resourced delivery roadmap, making the trade-off calls needed to move the needle fastest.
• Impact-based prioritisation across competing capability requests
• Clear articulation of what is in scope, what is deferred, and why
• Regular roadmap review and re-sequencing as operational priorities shift
• Delivery Partnership with Engineering & TechnologyAct as the primary product counterpart to engineering, ensuring capabilities are built to solve the real operational problem, not just the stated request.
• Requirements definition, user stories, and acceptance criteria
• Close partnership with technical leads through design, build, and release
• Unblocking delivery risks and making scope calls under time pressure
• Adoption & Change ManagementOwn adoption as a product outcome, not an afterthought — a capability that is built but not used has not moved the needle.
• Rollout planning in partnership with Business Change and operational leads
• Training, documentation, and enablement material for end users
• Feedback loops from users back into the product backlog
• Data, Measurement & ImpactDefine and track the operational metrics that prove — or disprove — that a capability is working.
• Baseline and post-launch measurement for every capability shipped
• Operational KPI definition in partnership with the COO and Operations leadership
• Root-cause use of data to decide what to build next
• Stakeholder ManagementManage a wide set of internal stakeholders with competing priorities, keeping delivery credible and expectations realistic.
• Regular reporting to the COO on roadmap progress and impact
• Direct engagement with business-line operational leads on their needs
• Alignment with Technology, Product, and Business Change on shared dependencies
• Continuous Discovery & ImprovementKeep the capability roadmap grounded in real operational pain, not assumption.
• Ongoing discovery with operational teams to surface friction and gaps
• Benchmarking of capability maturity against operational needs
• A bias toward iterating and improving shipped capabilities, not just shipping new onesKey Responsibilities

Dis-Chem Pharmacies in Durban Security Stores has a an opportunity for a security guard to Render a security service in terms of the Private Security Industry Regulations Act 56 of 2001 as amended for the Dis-Chem Group that meets Dis-Chem’ security requirements to protect assets, property and staff by creating a safe and secure environment, through identifying signs of criminal activities or disorder and investigating disturbances while adhering to legislation relevant to the industry and best practice.
Minimum Requirements…
Essential:
• Grade 12 – Matric or a Senior Certificate
• Grade C accreditation with the PSIRA
• A general minimum exposure of at least 3 years in the retail industry, such as shopping malls and warehouses
Advantageous:
• At least 1 year specific previous experience in a similar role
Job Specification…
• Be vigilant and alert of surroundings to identify suspicious activities and apprehend criminals or remove violators according to the legal authority invested in the industry and Dis-Chem standard operating procedures for the specific post through.
• Random patrols of the premises on regularly basis to ensure optimal visibility and reduce risks.
• Monitor and control access to the premises by documenting and regulating entrance into the site by vehicles or pedestrian’s access points to allow entry only to individuals with the correct authorization.
• Investigate and report signs of damage or unlawful entry as it occurs to management and act accordingly in the best interest of protecting Dis-Chem assets.
• Be clearly visible as far as reasonably possible as deterrent to discourage criminal activities, prevent theft, - damage, - personal injury, and other dishonourable acts.
• Be professionally courteous and friendly, approachable, and willing to help others when receiving guests, customers and employees.
• Access control – searching of staff, suppliers and company merchandisers.
• Maintain and complete all registers and occurrence books.
• Cancel staff purchasers and goods declared.
• Supervise and check refuse removal according to Dis-Chem standards
• Protect the property and assets of the business from all dishonest persons, action or any acts of malicious behaviour that could result in the company suffering loss.
• Be present at your post at all times when on duty.
• Practice good customer service relations for all Dis-Chem internal and external customers.
• Report any unusual or suspicious behaviour by staff, customer or suppliers.
• Opening and closing procedures-to be present observant and vigilant at the opening and closing of the site.
• Ensure that all doors and windows are locked at the end each day.
• Ensure that all water taps turned off when applicable.
• Do continuous personnel frisking and searches on a daily basis.
• Do thorough and proper vehicle searches throughout the day.
• Report any suspicious incidents verbally to management in detail with the submission of a written detailed report as soon as conveniently possible.
• Contact policing and emergency authorities and make written or verbal reports to law enforcement officers when needed as legally required and in accordance of Dis-Chem procedures.
• When problem situations or crisis arise or have been dealt with to maintain observing surroundings and report to management on findings and or changes in identified that intensify the situation.
• After a crisis, report the incident to management, the police or the appropriate authorities (such as the fire services in the case of a fire outbreak) with a detailed written report concerning the incident and your activities around the incident.
• Monitor the alarm systems and or video cameras and operate detecting/ emergency equipment when needed.
• When working during the night or alone e.g. after hours render on-going surveillance of the premises by patrolling the grounds and using closed-circuit camera monitoring or alarm systems to detect and investigate suspicious activities to ensure that only legal entrance to the premises is maintained.
• In emergency situations provide assistance and the emergency teams e.g. alert first responders, clinic sisters, managers etc.
• Maintain order during evacuation procedures and at assembly points by providing exact directions or decisive actions to ensure the safety of lives and property by preventing stampedes and breakdown of law and order or illegal entrance to the premises.
• Offer on-going security advice and safety warnings and tips to ensure that all security and safety precautions are adhered to.
• Be vigilant - watch out for any suspicious activities that may mean a breach in security measures that have been put in place on the site.
• Interpret quickly whatever is seen and act accordingly.
• Respond quickly and correctly during crisis - be alert to avoid being caught unaware.
• Know how best to respond to various dangerous situations according to industry and Dis-Chem standard operating procedures.
• Getting help - During some very dangerous situations (such as armed robbery attacks or assaults with deadly weapons), waste no time in calling the police to prevent loss of lives or property.
• Take accurate notes of unusual occurrences and daily activities.
• Enforce rules and regulations to prevent criminal activity before it happens.
• Perform special duties - receive phone calls, respond to text and email messages, and run vital errands for the department according to Dis-Chem and industry standard operating procedures.
Competencies
Essential:
• PSIRA knowledge
• Fire emergency and relevant Health and Safety Training and exposure
• English – Read, write and speak well as it is the organization’s official language.
Advantageous:
• 3rd Language
Special conditions of employment:
• PSIRA registered.
• Grade C PSIRA accreditation.
• South African
• MIE, clear criminal and credit.
• Driver’s license and own reliable transport and PDP when deployed as a driver.
Remuneration and benefits:
• Market related salary
• Kaelo
• Provident fund (PSSPF)

• Assist with call centre scripts and patient service telephone calls.
• Provide information to individuals in order to promote health.

• Receive dispensary stock in accordance with the SOP set out by the company.

• English and 2nd language – Read, write and speak.
• Time management, deadline driven, dealing with pressure, attention to detail.

• Computer, numerical skills.

• Retail FMCG, Dis-Chem front shop experience and a good performance record.

Dis-Chem Pharmacies in PMB Security Stores has a an opportunity for a security guard to Render a security service in terms of the Private Security Industry Regulations Act 56 of 2001 as amended for the Dis-Chem Group that meets Dis-Chem’ security requirements to protect assets, property and staff by creating a safe and secure environment, through identifying signs of criminal activities or disorder and investigating disturbances while adhering to legislation relevant to the industry and best practice.
Minimum Requirements…
Essential:
• Grade 12 – Matric or a Senior Certificate
• Grade C accreditation with the PSIRA
• A general minimum exposure of at least 3 years in the retail industry, such as shopping malls and warehouses
Advantageous:
• At least 1 year specific previous experience in a similar role
Job Specification…
• Be vigilant and alert of surroundings to identify suspicious activities and apprehend criminals or remove violators according to the legal authority invested in the industry and Dis-Chem standard operating procedures for the specific post through.
• Random patrols of the premises on regularly basis to ensure optimal visibility and reduce risks.
• Monitor and control access to the premises by documenting and regulating entrance into the site by vehicles or pedestrian’s access points to allow entry only to individuals with the correct authorization.
• Investigate and report signs of damage or unlawful entry as it occurs to management and act accordingly in the best interest of protecting Dis-Chem assets.
• Be clearly visible as far as reasonably possible as deterrent to discourage criminal activities, prevent theft, - damage, - personal injury, and other dishonourable acts.
• Be professionally courteous and friendly, approachable, and willing to help others when receiving guests, customers and employees.
• Access control – searching of staff, suppliers and company merchandisers.
• Maintain and complete all registers and occurrence books.
• Cancel staff purchasers and goods declared.
• Supervise and check refuse removal according to Dis-Chem standards
• Protect the property and assets of the business from all dishonest persons, action or any acts of malicious behaviour that could result in the company suffering loss.
• Be present at your post at all times when on duty.
• Practice good customer service relations for all Dis-Chem internal and external customers.
• Report any unusual or suspicious behaviour by staff, customer or suppliers.
• Opening and closing procedures-to be present observant and vigilant at the opening and closing of the site.
• Ensure that all doors and windows are locked at the end each day.
• Ensure that all water taps turned off when applicable.
• Do continuous personnel frisking and searches on a daily basis.
• Do thorough and proper vehicle searches throughout the day.
• Report any suspicious incidents verbally to management in detail with the submission of a written detailed report as soon as conveniently possible.
• Contact policing and emergency authorities and make written or verbal reports to law enforcement officers when needed as legally required and in accordance of Dis-Chem procedures.
• When problem situations or crisis arise or have been dealt with to maintain observing surroundings and report to management on findings and or changes in identified that intensify the situation.
• After a crisis, report the incident to management, the police or the appropriate authorities (such as the fire services in the case of a fire outbreak) with a detailed written report concerning the incident and your activities around the incident.
• Monitor the alarm systems and or video cameras and operate detecting/ emergency equipment when needed.
• When working during the night or alone e.g. after hours render on-going surveillance of the premises by patrolling the grounds and using closed-circuit camera monitoring or alarm systems to detect and investigate suspicious activities to ensure that only legal entrance to the premises is maintained.
• In emergency situations provide assistance and the emergency teams e.g. alert first responders, clinic sisters, managers etc.
• Maintain order during evacuation procedures and at assembly points by providing exact directions or decisive actions to ensure the safety of lives and property by preventing stampedes and breakdown of law and order or illegal entrance to the premises.
• Offer on-going security advice and safety warnings and tips to ensure that all security and safety precautions are adhered to.
• Be vigilant - watch out for any suspicious activities that may mean a breach in security measures that have been put in place on the site.
• Interpret quickly whatever is seen and act accordingly.
• Respond quickly and correctly during crisis - be alert to avoid being caught unaware.
• Know how best to respond to various dangerous situations according to industry and Dis-Chem standard operating procedures.
• Getting help - During some very dangerous situations (such as armed robbery attacks or assaults with deadly weapons), waste no time in calling the police to prevent loss of lives or property.
• Take accurate notes of unusual occurrences and daily activities.
• Enforce rules and regulations to prevent criminal activity before it happens.
• Perform special duties - receive phone calls, respond to text and email messages, and run vital errands for the department according to Dis-Chem and industry standard operating procedures.
Competencies
Essential:
• PSIRA knowledge
• Fire emergency and relevant Health and Safety Training and exposure
• English – Read, write and speak well as it is the organization’s official language.
Advantageous:
• 3rd LanguageSpecial conditions of employment:
• PSIRA registered.
• Grade C PSIRA accreditation.
• South African
• MIE, clear criminal and credit.
• Driver’s license and own reliable transport and PDP when deployed as a driver.
Remuneration and benefits:
• Market related salary
• Kaelo
• Provident fund (PSSPF)
