job_title: Sales & Marketing Manager - Blackheath, Cape Town - Salary dependent on experience
about_role:
Sales & Marketing Manager - Blackheath, Cape Town - Salary dependent on experience
Drive sales growth and lead the sales and marketing function in a hands-on, commercially focused management opportunity.
About Our Client
Our client manufactures standard and custom-designed mobile products, including mobile toilets, showers, kitchens, offices, and site-based infrastructure solutions. The company provides specialized trailer-based units and custom solutions to B2B clients across various industries, including construction, mining, agriculture, and events.
The Role: Sales & Marketing Manager
This role exists to lead and manage the Sales & Marketing function while remaining actively involved in the full sales cycle. The position focuses on identifying new business opportunities, managing client relationships, driving sales through to closure, and overseeing the external website and SEO service provider to support lead generation and business growth.
Key Responsibilities
• Must have a minimum of 8–10 years’ proven sales experience, with strong exposure to B2B sales and new business development.
• Proactively identify, target, negotiate, and close new business opportunities to achieve company revenue and growth targets.
• Lead, coach, and manage a small Sales & Marketing team, setting objectives and monitoring performance against KPIs.
• Maintain and update the company price list while costing new, modified, and custom products based on materials, manufacturing requirements, and margins.
• Manage the external website, SEO, and digital marketing service provider, holding them accountable for deliverables, timelines, and search performance.
• Develop and execute sales and marketing strategies, including content creation, market research, client visits, cold calling, and pipeline management.
• Provide technical advice, practical solutions, and troubleshooting support to clients and internal sales teams.
• Prepare accurate sales forecasts and regular reports covering sales pipeline, performance, market opportunities, and digital marketing results.

• Ability to prioritise workloads and meet deadlines

• Grade 12
• 3–5 years' experience in inventory control or stock management
• Previous supervisory or team leadership experience
• Experience with inventory systems, stock reconciliation, and inventory reporting
• Relevant qualification in Supply Chain, Logistics, Inventory Management, or a related field will be advantageousJoin a team that keeps our inventory accurate and our operations moving. Apply now!

job_title: Sales Administrator Intern | Kickstart Your Career With Frogfoot - JHB
about_role:
Ready to kickstart your career in Sales Administration?
Frogfoot is looking for a Sales Administrator Intern to join our Sales team and gain hands-on experience supporting the sales process from customer requests and feasibility checks through to quotations, orders, and installations.
If you're organised, detail-oriented, comfortable working with computers, and enjoy helping people, this is your opportunity to gain real-world experience, develop your administrative skills, and learn how a fast-paced sales environment operates.
If you're ready to hop into the pond, learn new skills and make an impact, we'd love to meet you!
About Frogfoot
Frogfoot is a leading open-access fibre infrastructure provider in South Africa. We build and operate fibre networks that connect homes, businesses and communities, working with multiple Internet Service Providers to deliver reliable connectivity across the country.
We're passionate about connectivity, innovation and developing people who are ready to grow their careers with us.
Purpose of the Role
The Sales Administrator Intern will provide administrative and operational support to the Sales team, assisting with customer requests, feasibilities, quotations, service orders, change orders and general sales administration.
The role provides practical exposure to the sales process while developing the intern's administrative, communication, customer service, computer and organisational skills.
You'll work closely with the Sales team and internal departments to ensure that customer information is captured accurately and that sales requests are processed efficiently and timeously.
What You'll Be Doing
Sales Administration
• Assist with the day-to-day administrative functions of the Sales Administration team.
• Capture and maintain accurate customer and sales information.
• Assist with processing feasibilities, quotations, service orders and change orders.
• Ensure required information is captured correctly and completely.
• Assist with maintaining accurate sales records and documentation.
• Support the Sales team with general administrative tasks.Quotes, Orders & Feasibilities
• Assist with capturing customer requests for feasibilities and quotations.
• Support the preparation and processing of quotes.
• Assist with capturing and processing service orders.
• Assist with change order administration.
• Follow up on outstanding information required to process customer requests.
• Learn and understand Frogfoot's products, services, and sales processes.Customer & Internal Support
• Assist with collecting outstanding customer information required for:
• Quotes
• Orders
• Installations
• Billing of services
• Communicate professionally with customers when information is required.
• Liaise with internal departments to obtain information and resolve queries.
• Support the Sales team with customer-related administration.
• Ensure queries and requests are directed to the appropriate team member when required.Data & Systems
• Capture information accurately on relevant systems.
• Maintain accurate records and trackers.
• Assist with checking information for completeness and accuracy.
• Work with spreadsheets and sales administration reports.
• Learn and use Frogfoot's sales systems and processes.
• Keep customer and sales information organised and up to date.Team Support
• Work closely with Sales Administrators, Sales teams and other internal departments.
• Assist colleagues during busy periods and with high-volume administrative activities.
• Follow up on outstanding actions and information.
• Take ownership of assigned tasks and meet agreed deadlines.
• Ask questions and seek guidance when unsure.Who We're Looking For
We're looking for someone who is organised, reliable, eager to learn and excited about building a career in sales administration.
You should:
• Be a South African Citizen.
• Be between 18 and 35 years of age.
• Have completed Grade 12 / Matric.
• Have a relevant 3-year Degree or Diploma in:
• Business Administration
• Sales / Marketing
• Business Management
• Office Administration
• Customer Service
• or a closely related field
• OR have a relevant Higher Certificate or Occupational Qualification at NQF Level 5.
• Be currently unemployed.
• Not be enrolled in any MICT SETA or other SETA-funded programme.
• Have good administrative and organisational skills.
• Have good written and verbal communication skills.
• Be comfortable working with computers and spreadsheets.
• Be able to manage multiple tasks and deadlines.
• Be detail-oriented and accurate.
• Be comfortable working as part of a team.
• Have a positive attitude and willingness to learn.No previous formal sales administration experience is required.
Computer Skills We Value
You don't need to be a computer expert — we're looking for someone who is comfortable with technology and willing to learn new systems.
We value:
• Microsoft Excel – strongly required
• Microsoft Word
• Microsoft Outlook and email
• Microsoft Teams
• General Microsoft Office skills
• Data capturing and spreadsheet management
• Online systems and digital platforms
• Shared documents and digital filing
• The ability to learn new sales systems quicklyExcel is Important
Because this role involves capturing and managing customer, quotation, and order information, we're particularly interested in candidates who are comfortable using Excel for data capturing, sorting, filtering, formatting, and basic reporting.
The Frogfoot Person We're Looking For
We're looking for someone who is:
• Organised: You can keep track of information, requests, and deadlines.
• Detail-Oriented: You understand that accurate customer and order information is critical.
• A Good Communicator: You're comfortable communicating with customers, colleagues, and different internal teams.
• Tech Comfortable: You enjoy working with computers, systems, and spreadsheets.
• A Team Player: You're willing to support your colleagues and contribute to the team's success.
• Accountable: When you're given a task, you take ownership and follow it through.
• A Quick Learner: You're curious, ask questions, and are excited to learn new products, systems, and processes.
• Able to Multitask: You can manage different requests while keeping your work accurate.
• Can-Do: You're ready to get involved, learn, and make an impact in the Frogfoot pond!What You'll Gain
This internship will give you practical exposure to:
• Sales administration
• Customer service and support
• Fibre products and services
• Sales processes
• Feasibility requests
• Quotation processing
• Service orders
• Change orders
• Customer information management
• Internal stakeholder coordination
• Microsoft Excel and business systems
• Professional workplace communication
• Working in a fast-paced sales environmentYou'll work alongside experienced professionals and develop the skills and confidence needed to take the next step in your career.
Internship Details
Job Type: 12-Month Internship | Fixed Term
Duration: September 2026 – August 2027
Department: Sales
Location: Johannesburg
Reports To: Sales Administration Team
Salary: Market-related internship
READY TO KICKSTART YOUR CAREER?
If you're organised, customer-focused, comfortable with computers and ready to learn, this is your opportunity to gain real-world experience and build your career in Sales Administration.
Come hop into the Frogfoot pond and start building your future!
Your career journey starts here.

Job Overview
The Junior Surfacing Foreman is responsible for assisting in the supervision and coordination of road surfacing operations on construction sites. The incumbent ensures that surfacing activities are completed safely, efficiently, and in accordance with project specifications, quality standards, and programme requirements. The role involves supervising surfacing crews, monitoring production, maintaining quality standards, and assisting with plant and resource management. This position provides a development path towards a Surfacing Foreman role.
Minimum Requirements
• Grade 12 (Matric)
• National Diploma in Civil Engineering or Construction Management (advantageous)
• 2–5 years' experience in road construction and surfacing operations
• Knowledge of asphalt paving, chip seals, slurry seals, and road rehabilitation processes
• Ability to read and interpret construction drawings and specifications
• Good leadership and communication skills
• Basic computer literacy (Microsoft Excel, Word, Outlook)
• Valid Code EB Driver's Licence
• Valid medical fitness certificate
• Knowledge of Occupational Health & Safety requirements
• Willingness to travel and work on construction sites across various regions

VEHICLE STOCK CONTROLLER
Mahindra Paarl | New Dealership Opening 1 October 2026
Join us as we launch a brand-new Mahindra dealership in Paarl!
We are looking for a detail-oriented and highly organised Vehicle Stock Controller to join our new dealership team. This is an exciting opportunity to be part of the dealership from the beginning and play a key role in ensuring that our vehicle stock is accurately controlled, documented and available to support our sales operations.
About the Role
As the Vehicle Stock Controller, you will be responsible for the day-to-day administration and control of the dealership's vehicle stock. You will work closely with the Sales, Management, Finance and Logistics teams to ensure that vehicles are accurately recorded, tracked and managed throughout the stock process.

• Support implementation and optimization of digital applications used in explosives manufacturing and blasting operations.

• Work closely with operational teams, technical specialists, and OEM developers.
• Support training initiatives and provide technical guidance to trainers and operational teams.

job_title: Change and Post Impact Coordinator - National
about_role:
Frogfoot is in search of a Change and Post Impact Coordinator to join our team.
Purpose of the Role
The Change and Post Impact Coordinator plays a critical role in ensuring the structured planning, coordination, and execution of network changes, while driving accountability and continuous improvement following service-affecting incidents. The role is responsible for supporting change governance, facilitating effective communication between stakeholders, maintaining accurate documentation, coordinating Change Advisory Board (CAB) activities, and identifying and tracking recurring network or service issues to support long-term service improvements.
Key Responsibilities
Change Management
• Review incoming change requests to ensure they are complete, accurate, and compliant with change governance standards.
• Log and track approved change requests in line with organisational change management policies.
• Ensure impact assessments are completed and reviewed before changes are approved.
• Coordinate change communications and ensure all required pre- and post-change checks are documented and shared with relevant stakeholders.
• Act as the first point of contact for change-related queries and provide timely, clear, and professional support.
• Manage rejected changes by communicating feedback, tracking resolutions, and ensuring learnings are shared with relevant teams.
• Maintain the Change Conflict Register and highlight potential scheduling conflicts for assessment.
• Organise and chair regular Change Advisory Board (CAB) meetings, including preparing meeting packs, facilitating discussions, and tracking follow-up actions.
• Prepare and update change request tickets with the required technical and logistical information to ensure CAB readiness.
• Monitor change request queues to ensure response and processing times are managed within SLA requirements.
• Provide operational coordination where required, including stock movements, site access arrangements, and stakeholder communication.
• Participate in a rotational standby schedule to support emergency change requests after hours.
Post Impact and Service Improvement Management
• Document network and service outages accurately, ensuring all relevant technical and operational information is captured.
• Follow up with internal teams, vendors, contractors, and third-party providers to investigate incidents and obtain missing information.
• Identify patterns, recurring outages, network vulnerabilities, and technical faults that require escalation or improvement.
• Coordinate and monitor improvement plans for repeated or high-impact issues.
• Track escalated faults through to the implementation and verification of a permanent fix or suitable mitigation.
• Maintain and update records of known network vulnerabilities and support remediation planning.
• Draft and prepare Root Cause Analysis (RFO) reports for internal and customer-facing communication.
• Compile relevant information for Service Improvement Plans (SIPs) and support the responsible teams with reporting, finalisation, and communication.
What You'll Need to Know
• A strong understanding of administrative and coordination processes, with exceptional attention to detail.
• How to manage multiple priorities and work effectively under pressure and within tight deadlines.
• Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to engage professionally with a range of internal and external stakeholders.
• Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, Word, and collaboration tools such as Microsoft Teams and Google Workspace.
• Familiarity with ticketing systems and change management tools.
• A basic understanding of network operations and ITIL-based change control processes would be advantageous.
• Experience coordinating activities across multiple teams and stakeholders.
• Experience within a Network Operations Centre (NOC), ISP, telecommunications environment, or similar operational environment would be beneficial.
• ITIL Foundation certification or relevant change management training would be advantageous but is not essential.
What Success Looks Like in This Role
Success in this role means ensuring that network changes are well coordinated, properly documented, communicated effectively, and processed in line with established governance and SLA requirements. You will contribute to smooth CAB processes, proactively identify and manage change conflicts, and ensure stakeholders have the information they need to make informed decisions.
You will also be successful when service-affecting issues are thoroughly investigated, recurring problems are identified and escalated, and improvement actions are tracked through to effective resolution. Ultimately, your contribution will support stronger change governance, reduced operational risk, improved service reliability, and continuous improvement across the network.
Qualities We Value at Frogfoot
• Accountability: Taking ownership of tasks and following through until actions are completed.
• Attention to Detail: Ensuring information, documentation, and processes are accurate and complete.
• Collaboration: Working effectively with colleagues, vendors, contractors, and other stakeholders.
• Proactive Problem-Solving: Identifying potential risks and recurring issues and taking action to support resolution.
• Professional Communication: Communicating clearly, respectfully, and effectively, even in high-pressure situations.
• Adaptability: Remaining flexible and effective when priorities change or urgent issues arise.
• Continuous Improvement: Looking for opportunities to improve processes, prevent recurring issues, and strengthen service delivery.

Purpose of Position:
Purpose The Technology Manager is responsible for ensuring that the Company continuously develops, acquires, understands, and applies technology to strengthen its long-term competitiveness. The role exists to ensure that the organisation never becomes dependent solely upon inherited knowledge, historical practice, or established methods, but instead develops a deep understanding of the technologies that underpin every aspect of the business. Technology is defined broadly. It includes manufacturing technologies, materials science, engineering, production processes, automation, artificial intelligence, information systems, quality systems, maintenance, testing, logistics, product technologies, communication technologies, and any other knowledge, process, or system capable of improving the business. The Technology Manager is therefore responsible for ensuring that the Company becomes a true learning organisation, in which technology is continually acquired, evaluated, understood, implemented, improved, and retained. More than simply managing technology, the Technology Manager is the custodian of the organisation's technological knowledge and capability.
Core Mission:
The Technology Manager is responsible for developing the organisation's technological capability.
This includes:
Identifying technologies that improve competitiveness.
Building organisational understanding of those technologies.
Translating knowledge into practical business improvements.
Leading and coordinating technology implementation.
Preserving technical knowledge within the organisation.
Ensuring that the Company continually improves its technological capability.
Strategic Responsibilities
The Technology Manager shall:
Develop and maintain a long-term Technology Strategy aligned with the company's strategic objectives.
Produce and maintain technology roadmaps. Identify technologies capable of improving competitiveness.
Evaluate emerging technologies before competitors.
Recommend technology investments.
Assess technological risks facing the organisation.
Prioritise technology projects according to strategic value.
Ensure that technology decisions support long-term competitiveness rather than short-term convenience.
Advise The Executive on technology-related opportunities and risks.
Technology Intelligence:
Maintain an active understanding of developments relevant to the Company including, but not limited to:
Aluminium processing.
Metallurgy.
Manufacturing.
Surface treatments.
Non-stick technologies.
Tooling.
Automation.
Robotics.
Artificial Intelligence.
Information management.
ERP systems.
Production planning.
Supply chain technologies.
Quality systems.
Testing and laboratory methods.
Energy efficiency.
Environmental technologies.
Packaging technologies.
Industry 4.0 and digital manufacturing.
Technology intelligence should always be translated into practical recommendations and business opportunities.
Organisational Knowledge:
The Technology Manager is the custodian of the organisation's technological knowledge. The objective is not simply to accumulate information, but to develop an organisation that understands its own technologies sufficiently to innovate with confidence. The Technology Manager shall actively develop four forms of organisational knowledge:
Know-how:
The practical knowledge required to perform work correctly.
Know-why:
The scientific, engineering, commercial, and operational principles that explain why processes, materials, and systems behave as they do.
Know-what's next:
An understanding of emerging technologies, market developments, research, and opportunities that may affect the future competitiveness of the business.
Know-who:
Knowledge of where expertise exists, both within the Company and externally, including suppliers, universities, research institutions, consultants, and technology partners. The Technology Manager is responsible for ensuring that this knowledge grows continuously and remains within the organisation rather than residing solely in individuals
Organisational Learning:
Develop systems that strengthen the organisation's technical capability. This includes:
Identifying areas where technical understanding is weak.
Developing learning programmes.
Creating internal technical documentation.
Building knowledge libraries.
Capturing lessons learned from projects.
Recording best practice
Encouraging cross-functional learning.
Promoting technical curiosity throughout the organisation.
Technology Development Lead or coordinate projects involving technological improvement, including:
Manufacturing improvements. • Process optimisation. • Product innovation. • Automation. • Artificial Intelligence. • Information systems. • Digital workflows. • Laboratory capability. • New materials. • Testing methods. • Equipment evaluation. • New production technologies.
Where appropriate, coordinate cross-functional teams to deliver successful implementation. Information Technology Information Technology forms part of the Technology Manager's responsibilities but is only one component of the broader technology function.
Responsibilities include strategic oversight of:
ERP development. • Information architecture. • Data quality. • Digital workflows. • Artificial Intelligence implementation. • Information security. • Systems integration. • Infrastructure planning. • Digital transformation. Operational IT support may continue to be provided by internal specialists or external service providers.
External Technology Network:
Develop and maintain productive relationships with:
Universities. • Technical institutes. • Research organisations. • Equipment manufacturers. • Material suppliers. • Technology consultants. • Industry associations. • Innovation partners.
The objective is to ensure that the Company remains connected to the best available external knowledge and technology.
Technology Governance:
Maintain appropriate technology management systems, including:
Technology Strategy. • Technology Roadmap. • Technology Register. • Technology Risk Register. • Technology Project Portfolio. • Knowledge Repository.
Provide regular reports to The Executive covering:
Progress against the Technology Strategy. • Emerging technologies. • Current technology projects. • Opportunities. • Risks. • Investment recommendations. • Organisational capability development.
Innovation:
Establish innovation as a structured organisational capability rather than an occasional activity. Encourage experimentation. Support rapid evaluation of new ideas. Measure outcomes. Capture successful innovations. Ensure that innovation becomes a repeatable business process.
Success Measures :
Success should be measured by improvements in the organisation's technological capability rather than simply by completed projects.

Role Purpose
The IT Service Desk Team Lead owns the day-to-day performance of the IT Helpdesk and the End User Compute (EUC) function across Weaver Fintech. This role leads a team of 5–6 EUC Technicians, is accountable for service desk SLAs and ticket quality, and acts as the first point of triage and escalation between end users, Engineering teams, HomeChoice, and third-party vendors. The role also coordinates the approval process for SaaS, AI tooling and other software license requests, ensuring requests are properly reviewed before being granted.
Position in the organisation
The role reports into the Head of Technology Operations, within the broader TechOps function. This role is a first-line people management position — the EUC Technicians report directly to this role.
• Head of Technology Operations
• IT Service Desk Team Lead (this role)
• EUC Technician x 5–6 (direct reports)
Key Responsibilities:
Service Desk & SLA Management
• Own the end-to-end performance of the IT Helpdesk, including ticket intake, prioritisation, assignment and quality of resolution.
• Define, monitor and report against SLAs and KPIs (response time, resolution time, backlog, first-contact resolution, customer satisfaction).
• Maintain and continuously improve helpdesk processes, categorisation, and knowledge base articles to reduce repeat tickets.
• Produce regular SLA and volume reporting for the Head of Technology Operations, highlighting trends, risks and resourcing needs.Team Leadership — End User Compute
• Lead, coach and manage the performance of 5–6 EUC Technicians, including workload allocation, rostering/coverage, 1:1s and development.
• Oversee laptop build, imaging, deployment and asset lifecycle management (procurement liaison, allocation, repairs, decommissioning).
• Ensure the EUC team delivers consistent, high-quality support for all end-user compute needs — hardware, peripherals, mobile devices and remote/onsite setup.
• Set standards for EUC service delivery (build standards, security baseline compliance, onboarding/offboarding turnaround).License & SaaS/AI Tooling Coordination
• Coordinate the intake and approval workflow for SaaS application, AI tool and license requests raised by the business.
• Liaise with budget owners, Engineering, Security and Procurement as needed to validate business need, cost and risk before approval.
• Maintain a record of active licenses/subscriptions per app to support renewals, cost control and periodic access reviews.
• Flag duplicate, unused or non-compliant tooling requests and recommend consolidation where appropriate.Triage & Escalation Management
• Act as the primary triage point for issues that cannot be resolved at first line, determining correct routing and urgency.
• Escalate and track issues requiring Engineering team involvement, ensuring clear handover and ownership.
• Manage the working relationship and issue escalation with HomeChoice for services or infrastructure still supported by HomeChoice during the separation period.
• Manage third-party vendors and support partners on escalated incidents, holding them to agreed response/resolution commitments.
• Ensure major incidents are communicated promptly to stakeholders and followed up with root-cause / preventative actions.
Key Relationships
• Head of Technology Operations (line manager)
• EUC Technicians (direct reports)
• Engineering / Platform / SecOps teams (escalation and coordination)
• HomeChoice IT (shared/transitional services during separation)
• Third-party vendors and support partners
• Budget owners and Procurement (license and hardware approvals)
• All Weaver Fintech employees (as end users of the service desk)Requirements:
Experience & Qualifications
• 3–5+ years' experience in IT service desk / end user compute support, including at least 1–2 years in a team lead, supervisory or coordinator capacity.
• Demonstrated experience managing SLAs, ticketing systems (e.g. Jira Service Management, ServiceNow, Freshservice or similar) and helpdesk reporting.
• Experience building/imaging laptops and managing end user compute hardware lifecycle.
• Experience coordinating software/SaaS license requests and working with vendors or third-party support partners.
• Relevant IT certification advantageous (e.g. ITIL Foundation, CompTIA A+/Network+, Microsoft 365 / endpoint management).
• A relevant diploma or degree in IT or a related field is preferred but not essential given equivalent experience.Skills & Competencies
• Strong people leadership — able to coach, motivate and hold a small technical team accountable to service standards.
• Structured and organised, comfortable owning SLAs, backlogs and reporting with attention to detail.
• Confident triaging technical issues and judging what to resolve directly versus escalate, and to whom.
• Clear communicator across technical and non-technical stakeholders, including senior leadership and external vendors.
• Vendor and stakeholder management skills, including holding third parties to agreed commitments.
• Working knowledge of end user compute environments (Windows/macOS, M365, endpoint security, MDM tooling).
• Pragmatic, service-minded approach with a bias towards resolving employee impact quickly.Key Performance Indicators
• SLA adherence (response and resolution time) against agreed targets.
• Ticket backlog and ageing, kept within agreed thresholds.
• First-contact resolution rate and repeat-ticket rate.
• End user / employee satisfaction with helpdesk and EUC support (CSAT).

• Escalation handling — time to correct routing, and vendor SLA compliance on escalated issues.

A company in the manufacturing industry is looking for a Lead AI Engineer to join their team in Johannesburg, GP.
Job Overview:
Our company has moved past experimenting with AI. An internally built, agentic system already runs our planning cycle end-to-end—from customer sales order through to purchase orders and production planning—handling hundreds of orders daily in live production. The Lead AI Engineer is the first dedicated hire into this capability and will become its technical owner.
This role has two parallel mandates. The first is to instill proper engineering discipline around the systems already in production to ensure they are documented, tested, monitored, recoverable, and not dependent on any single individual. The second is to architect and build the next wave of automation across the Group.
This is a hands-on role. Conventional IT, infrastructure, and end-user support are covered elsewhere and do not form part of this position. You will work directly with the Supply Chain and IT Executive and cross-functionally with planning, procurement, production, and finance teams. Success is measured by systems that work in the real business, not by demonstrations.
Responsibilities:
Technical Ownership & Core Engineering
• Assume technical ownership of the Group's existing production AI systems (including the agentic planning and MRP system) and bring them under source control with documented architecture, managed environments, and a defined deployment path.
• Eliminate single points of failure across all production automation to ensure no business-critical system relies on the knowledge of a single individual.
• Architect new systems with clear boundaries, data contracts, defined failure modes, and designs that will still hold when the system is three times larger.
Quality Assurance & Evaluation
• Build and maintain evaluation harnesses for every automated process, using libraries of real historical cases with known good outcomes, and run them against every code change, prompt change, and model version upgrade before release.
• Establish and enforce a rigorous release path from development to production, including shadow mode, pilot phases with defined success criteria, canary releases by product line, and staged expansion of autonomy based on evidence.
• Instrument all automated processes for observability, including full logging, anomaly alerting, and a queryable audit trail.
Safety, Governance & Control
• Design bounded autonomy into every agent, with hard limits on value, quantity, supplier, and scope that the system cannot exceed, triggering a loud failure rather than acting silently outside those bounds.
• Implement human approval gates for irreversible and financially committing actions, only removing them where evaluation history and executive agreement justify it.
• Maintain tested rollback and kill-switch capabilities, along with a documented manual fallback process for every automated business process.
• Ensure all automated processes that create financial commitments meet the Group's control requirements (segregation of duties, approval limits, audit trail) in collaboration with the CFO and external audit.
Strategy & Business Integration
• Identify, scope, prioritise, and build the next wave of automation across planning, procurement, production, logistics, finance, and commercial functions.
• Spend time on the floor and in the business to learn how processes actually work before automating them, rather than automating the process as described.
• Run pilots with pre-agreed success criteria, measurement periods, and decision points, recommending whether to proceed, extend, or stop based on evidence.
• Produce the documentation, runbooks, and user training that allow business users to understand, supervise, and challenge the systems they rely on.
Reporting & Vendor Management
• Own model, vendor, and tooling selection, including cost per transaction, data handling, residency, and exposure to lock-in.
• Report delivery progress, risks, incidents, and accumulated technical debt to the Supply Chain and IT Executive, and present to the executive team as required.
Requirements:
Essential Experience
• Production Release Discipline: Has personally owned software running in production where failure carried commercial consequence and can detail how they staged rollouts, tested before release, detected problems, rolled back, and handled incidents.
• End-to-End Systems: Demonstrable evidence of designing and delivering complete working systems, not components or PoCs, including the unglamorous parts: error handling, data quality, monitoring, documentation, and handover.
• Experience: Minimum of 8 years in software engineering or systems development, with at least 3 years in a senior, lead, or principal capacity.
Technical Skills
• Fluent with AI-assisted development tools such as Cursor, Claude Code, or equivalent.
• Practical experience building with Large Language Models (LLMs) and agentic systems (context and prompt design, tool use, evaluation methods, handling non-determinism) is a strong advantage. Strong engineering fundamentals with limited agent experience will be considered; the reverse will not.
Business & Personal Attributes

job_title: National Head of Sales - Alert Engine Parts
about_role:
Motus Aftermarket Parts is searching for a National Head of Sales to join the Alert Engine Parts division. The purpose of the position is to provide strategic leadership and direction to the entire sales organisation, driving sustainable revenue growth, profitability, customer acquisition, market-share expansion and sales excellence across the national retail business.
The role is accountable for developing and executing the national sales strategy, leading high-performing sales teams, strengthening customer and strategic partner relationships, identifying new market opportunities, and ensuring effective sales, pricing, budgeting, forecasting and performance-management practices.
The role is based in Johannesburg and Pretoria.
Minimum Requirements
• Matric.
• Degree in Marketing and Sales, Business Management, or a related field preferred.
• Minimum 10 years’ relevant sales experience.
• Minimum 5 years’ experience in a senior sales, management or similar leadership role.
• Proven experience in a national or multi-territory sales environment.
• Experience in the aftermarket parts, automotive or related industry is highly advantageous.
• Demonstrated experience in sales strategy, budget management, forecasting, key-account management and team leadership.
• Proven track record of achieving and exceeding revenue and profitability targets.Key Performance Areas and Main Outputs
• Overall Sales Performance
• Achieve overall sales revenue targets on a monthly, quarterly and annual basis.
• Drive sustainable sales growth and increase national market share.
• Ensure the profitability of sales operations through effective management of gross margins and sales expenses.
• Develop, manage and monitor the national sales budget.
• Accurately forecast sales performance, expenditure and market demand.
• Review sales performance data and contribute to the annual budgeting and business-planning process.
• Oversee the end-to-end sales negotiation process, from lead generation through to the closing of significant deals.
• Ensure sales processes are efficient, commercially sound and aligned with company objectives.
• Identify underperforming territories, channels, customers and sales activities, and implement appropriate corrective action.
• Sales Strategy Development and Implementation
• Develop and implement the overall national sales strategy in alignment with the company’s strategic objectives.
• Translate business objectives into clear sales plans, targets and initiatives.
• Identify, assess and develop new market and revenue opportunities.
• Expand the retailer network within the assigned national territory.
• Develop and implement pricing strategies and sales programmes that support both volume growth and profitability.
• Monitor market conditions and adjust sales strategies where required.
• Establish appropriate sales targets and performance measures for the sales organisation.
• Drive continuous improvement in sales processes, methodologies and execution.
• Strategic Partnerships and Customer Relations
• Identify, establish and maintain strategic partnerships that expand the company’s sales reach.
• Build and maintain strong relationships with retailers, workshops, mechanics and other key customers.
• Develop and maintain relationships with key distributors and suppliers.
• Conduct regular visits to retail outlets to understand market conditions and customer requirements.
• Identify non-performing outlets, territories and customer segments and implement appropriate interventions.
• Represent the company at customer evenings, networking events, industry events and relevant trade exhibitions.
• Conduct product demonstrations, product-awareness sessions and sales presentations for retailers and mechanics.
• Strengthen customer loyalty, retention and long-term commercial relationships.
• Ensure customer feedback and market insights are communicated to relevant internal stakeholders.
• Market Intelligence, Marketing and Sales Reporting
• Gather and analyse competitor pricing, promotional schemes, product launches and market activities.
• Monitor industry trends, competitor strategies and changing customer needs.
• Translate market intelligence into actionable sales strategies and commercial opportunities.
• Ensure accurate and timely sales reporting across all territories.
• Monitor sales dashboards and reporting tools, including Repsly and Power BI.
• Track and analyse key sales indicators, including lead-conversion rates, revenue per client and customer-retention rates.
• Maintain accurate records of daily sales visits, sales activity, collections and stock.
• Submit territory-specific performance reports within required deadlines.
• Use data and analytics to identify trends, risks, opportunities and areas requiring corrective action.
• Leverage Power BI reporting and analytics to provide actionable insights into sales performance, customer activity, territory performance and key commercial trends.
• Team Leadership and Collaboration
• Build, lead and develop a high-performing national sales team.
• Establish and maintain a culture of sales excellence aligned with MAP values.
• Set clear performance expectations, objectives and accountability measures.
• Mentor, coach and develop sales leaders and high-potential employees.
• Identify skills and capability gaps and implement appropriate development plans.
• Drive effective performance management and address underperformance proactively.
• Promote collaboration, communication and knowledge-sharing across the sales organisation.
• Collaborate with the Supply and Demand function to ensure timely stock replenishment and product availability.
• Identify product-availability gaps and communicate customer feedback to Product and Marketing teams.
• Collaborate with Finance/Credit on new-customer credit approvals and manage credit risk associated with sales activities.
• Ensure sales decisions balance revenue growth, customer service, profitability and commercial risk.Key Success Measures
• Revenue growth and achievement of national sales targets.
• Market-share growth and expansion of the retailer network.
• Gross profit and overall sales profitability.
• New-customer and strategic-account acquisition.
• Customer retention and strength of customer relationships.
• Sales-team productivity, capability and performance.
• Budget adherence and forecast accuracy.
• Quality and timeliness of sales reporting and market intelligence.
• Effective management of credit and commercial risk.
• Successful execution of the national sales strategy.
• Effective utilisation of Repsly and Power BI to monitor, analyse and improve sales performance.
Role Profile Summary
The Senior Manager: Head of Sales is a strategic and commercially accountable leadership position responsible for the overall performance and direction of the national sales organisation. The incumbent must combine strong strategic thinking with hands-on commercial leadership, customer engagement and people management.
Success in the role requires a proven ability to deliver sustainable revenue and market-share growth while maintaining profitability, strengthening the retailer and customer network, developing high-performing sales teams and ensuring effective collaboration across the broader organisation. The role also requires strong data-driven decision-making and the ability to leverage Repsly and Power BI to enhance sales visibility, performance management and commercial outcomes.

Matric certificate
Clean criminal record
Purpose
This SOP outlines the procedures for ensuring that Company stock is in good condition, the truck is properly equipped and in good condition for loading, and that the load is secured safely and correctly.
Scope
This SOP applies to all personnel involved in the inspection, handling, and loading of Company stock.
Responsibilities
• Warehouse Supervisor: Oversee the entire loading process, ensure compliance with the SOP.
• Checkers: Follow procedures to inspect, handle, and load stock correctly.
• Checkers: Ensure the truck is in good condition, and safety equipment is in place and functional.
• Responsibility: Direct report to transport DPT vice manager and branch manager and checking report monthly share in the DPT meeting.
• Authority: have the right to reject all the stock load into the truck.
• KPI: need to clarify. Procedure
1. Pre-Loading Inspection of Stock
• Inspect Boxes and Units:
• Ensure all boxes are intact, with no signs of damage such as tears, dents, or watermarks.
• Open a random sample of boxes to check the condition of the units inside. Ensure they are clean and free of any defects or damages.
• Total percentage of stock to be checked is 1-2%, in the case that there are more disputes, it needs to be increased to 2-4%, if this still does not eliminate the issue then 100% checking will apply.
• Label to be created, including serial number and model number
• Confirm that the quantity of units matches the packing slip and is consistent with the inventory records.
• Ensure Cleanliness:
• Verify that all units are clean and in good condition before loading.
• Wipe down units if necessary to remove any dust or residue.
• Document Inspection:
• Record the condition of the stock and any issues found during the inspection in the inspection log.
• Notify the Warehouse Supervisor of any discrepancies or damages immediately.
2. Truck Inspection Before Loading
• Truck Condition:
• Inspect the truck for any leaks, or damages that could affect the safety and integrity of the load.
• Ensure that the loading area of the truck is clean, dry, and free of any debris or substances that could damage the stock.
•
• Safety Equipment Check:
• Verify that all required safety equipment is present and in good working order, including:
• Straps, ropes, or other securing devices
• Padding or other protective materials
• Emergency equipment such as fire extinguishers.
• Document Inspection:
• Record the truck inspection results, noting any issues and actions taken to address them.
• Only proceed with loading if the truck is deemed to be in satisfactory condition. 3. Loading Procedure
• Correct Loading of Stock:
• Ensure stock is loaded according to the established loading plan, securing all items to prevent movement during transit.
• Use appropriate securing devices to prevent shifting or damage during transportation.
• Preventing Damage During Loading:
• Handle all stock with care, using proper lifting techniques and equipment to avoid dropping or bumping items.
• Place padding or protective materials between items if necessary to prevent scratches or other damage.
• Verification:
• Confirm that the stock being loaded matches the loading documentation (e.g., delivery order, manifest).
• Double-check that all units are accounted for and loaded as planned.
• Photos of loaded stock to be taken, while loading, beginning of first carriage, mid-way during loading and end of loading of the stock (6m and 12m of trailers). Photos are to be uploaded on a drive and shared for all relevant parties to view. 4. Post-Loading Verification
• Final Inspection:
• Perform a final check to ensure all stock is securely loaded, and the truck is properly sealed.
• Inspect the loading area to ensure no items have been left behind.
• Documentation:
• Complete the loading checklist, including confirmation that the stock matches the loading documentation and is in good condition.
• Submit the completed checklist and inspection logs to the Warehouse Supervisor for review. Quality Assurance
• The Warehouse Supervisor will review the completed checklists and inspection logs at the end of each loading session to ensure compliance with this SOP.
• Any deviations from this SOP must be documented and reported to management immediately for corrective action.

about_role:
Introduction
Grain Field Chickens, a subsidiary of VKB Agriculture (PTY) Ltd, is a dynamic role player in the integrated broiler industry with an abattoir in Reitz in the North-Eastern Free State. We offer you the opportunity to establish yourself within a professional, corporate environment in the countryside.
Job Description
To engage in operating a power-driven mobile hoist/ reach truck with a lifting capacity exceeding 6 000 kg used in the loading, unloading, moving or stacking of goods and/ or pallets, but does not include an internal motor vehicle in alignment with predefined work objectives (as per agreed standard operating procedures).
Job Requirements

Position Purpose
The Hydraulic Cylinder Inspector is responsible for the detailed inspection, assessment, documentation, and quality verification of hydraulic cylinders and components throughout the repair process.
The Inspector ensures that all customer units, service exchange units, and repaired cylinders meet company  SA quality standards, customer specifications, and safety requirements before progressing through the workshop or being released to the customer.
The role serves as a critical link between production, quality control, customer expectations, and workshop planning by providing accurate technical assessments that drive quotations, repair decisions, and final acceptance
Key Responsibilities
Incoming Inspection and Assessment
Receive and inspect hydraulic cylinders upon arrival.
Identify and document visible damage, wear, and failure causes.
Assess components where required.
Measure critical dimensions and tolerances.
Determine repairability of rods, barrels, pistons, glands, and associated components.
Identify replacement parts required for repair.
Capture photographs and supporting evidence for quotations and customer reports.
Ensure all inspection findings are accurately recorded on job cards and inspection reports.
Failure Analysis and Technical Reporting
Determine probable causes of component failures.
Identify abnormal wear patterns and recurring failures.
Provide detailed inspection findings to management and quotation teams.
Assist in recommending repair or replacement options.
Assist with root cause investigations for warranty returns and customer complaints.
Maintain accurate records of inspection findings and recommendations.
Quality Control During Repair Process
Verify components meet repair specifications before assembly.
Conduct in-process inspections throughout the repair cycle.
Confirm machined, welded, and manufactured components meet required standards.
Reject non-conforming components and initiate corrective action.
Ensure workshop procedures and quality standards are consistently followed.
Monitor compliance with customer repair specifications.
Final Inspection and Job Release
Perform final quality inspections before pressure testing.
Ensure correct seal kits, wear rings, bearings, and fasteners have been installed.
Confirm all repair procedures have been completed.
Ensure documentation is complete before job closure.
Authorize cylinders for testing or customer release once quality requirements are met.
Final Release Checks
Component quality verification.
Assembly accuracy.
Dimensional compliance.
Documentation completeness.
Testing readiness.
Compliance with customer specifications.
Service Exchange Unit Management
Inspect all incoming service exchange units.
Assess condition and determine refurbishment requirements.
Ensure exchange units are inspected and approved before returning to stock.
Maintain quality standards of exchange inventory.
Report stock shortages, damaged units, and repair requirements.
Assist in keeping service exchange units ready for customer demand.
Support management in resolving technical queries and concerns.
Job Planning and Production Support
Prioritize inspections according to workshop workload and customer urgency.
Provide timely inspection reports to prevent delays in quotations and repairs.
Communicate repair scope changes to Foremen and Workshop Managers.
Assist production planning by identifying long-lead components and repair requirements.
Provide technical input during production meetings
Documentation and Reporting
Complete inspection reports accurately and professionally.
Ensure job cards are updated with relevant findings.
Maintain photographic records where required.
Assist with quality trend analysis and reporting.
Record non-conformances and corrective actions.
Ensure traceability of inspections and decisions
Safety and Housekeeping
Comply with all company Health and Safety requirements.
Wear prescribed PPE at all times.
Maintain a clean and organized inspection area.
Report unsafe conditions immediately.
Participate in safety meetings and toolbox talks.
Promote a safe and quality-focused workshop culture.

The BI & Solutions Team Lead is a senior role responsible for providing operational, technical, and team leadership across the Business Intelligence (BI), reporting, and data analytics function. The position is responsible for ensuring that BI and reporting solutions are appropriately scoped, designed, developed, quality assured, implemented, and delivered in line with business and client requirements.
The role provides technical direction and guidance to BI developers and analysts, overseeing the end-to-end delivery lifecycle from requirements analysis and solution specification through to development, testing, deployment, and handover. The BI & Solutions Team Lead is also responsible for Finance Management activities relating to BI and reporting projects. This includes supporting project scoping and effort estimation, providing commercial inputs, monitoring delivery effort and resource utilisation against agreed scope, and assisting with pricing, quotations, and tender solution inputs where required.
Under Business Process Management, the role oversees the complete BI delivery lifecycle and ensures that projects are effectively prioritised and delivered. This includes requirements analysis, development specifications, solution architecture, report and data-model development oversight, testing, quality assurance, deployment, and handover. The role is responsible for driving delivery standards, resolving issues, improving processes, and promoting continuous improvement across reporting projects.
The position also has significant responsibility for Learning and Development (Staffing). The incumbent provides day-to-day technical and operational guidance to BI developers and analysts, allocates and reviews work, mentors team members, promotes development standards and knowledge sharing, and supports employee skills development, performance, and delivery accountability.
In addition, the BI & Solutions Team Lead is responsible for Client and Vendor Management, acting as a senior point of engagement for clients, internal stakeholders, and relevant technology or service partners. The role leads requirements and solution discussions, provides demonstrations and progress updates, manages stakeholder expectations, and assists with resolving delivery matters. The incumbent may also represent CCG Systems at client presentations, workshops, exhibitions, industry engagements, and other public-speaking opportunities where required.
The role requires strong knowledge of Business Intelligence and management reporting, Power BI, DAX, SQL, data modelling, reporting architecture, data integration, and reporting platforms, together with the ability to translate business requirements into practical reporting solutions and communicate technical concepts effectively to clients and broader audiences.
Overall, the BI & Solutions Team Lead combines technical expertise, people leadership, project delivery, financial awareness, business process management, and client relationship management to ensure the successful delivery of high-quality BI and reporting solutions while supporting the development and performance of the BI team.

Raizcorp is looking for experienced banking and financial-services professionals to join us as business coaches, working directly with a portfolio of entrepreneurs across finance, strategy, sales, marketing, operations, people and personal development.
This is not a banking role. You will not be selling financial products, assessing businesses for credit or managing a traditional banking portfolio. Instead, you will use your financial and commercial experience to help entrepreneurs understand their businesses, challenge their assumptions and improve their decision-making.
You do not need previous coaching experience. Raizcorp will train you in our internationally recognised business-coaching methodology. What we need is your financial depth, commercial judgement, empathy for entrepreneurs and genuine desire to help others build stronger businesses.
This role is a full-time role with the express requirement to be present at work from 8:00 am to 17:00 on weekdays.

• Hold structured one-on-one coaching sessions with a portfolio of entrepreneurs.
• Help entrepreneurs interpret their financial information and use it to make better commercial decisions.
• Guide business owners in understanding cash flow, profitability, margins, working capital and financial sustainability.
• Help entrepreneurs understand what their numbers are telling them about strategy, sales, pricing, operations and the overall health of their businesses.
• Challenge assumptions, interrogate business thinking and help entrepreneurs evaluate commercial risks and trade-offs.
• Work across the entrepreneur’s entire business, including finance, strategy, sales, marketing, operations, people and personal development.
• Help entrepreneurs strengthen their business models, commercial disciplines and decision-making capability.
• Facilitate business simulations, workshops and group learning interventions using Raizcorp’s programmes and methodology.
• Collaborate with other Guides, specialists and programme teams to support each entrepreneur’s development journey.
This role may be a strong fit for you if you are:
• A retired or retiring banker who still has a strong appetite for business and wants to remain professionally active.
• A former relationship manager, business banker, commercial banker, credit professional, corporate banker, regional banking leader or financial-services executive.
• Someone who has spent a career assessing businesses and now wants to help build them.
• A commercially minded finance professional who understands that the financial statements are often the result of decisions made elsewhere in the business.
• Someone who enjoys understanding how businesses work and helping people think through difficult decisions.
• An experienced professional looking for meaningful work without returning to a traditional corporate banking career.
• Patient enough to develop people, but confident enough to challenge them.
• Able to listen without immediately taking over or providing all the answers.
• Motivated by seeing an entrepreneur become more capable and commercially confident over time.

• Substantial experience within banking, financial services, commercial finance or a closely related environment.
• Meaningful exposure to businesses, entrepreneurs, business owners or commercial clients during your career.
• Strong financial acumen and confidence interpreting financial statements, cash flow, profitability, margins and other drivers of business performance.

job_title: EVA Shoe Injection Moulding Supervisor / Technician (JB6245)
about_role:
EVA Shoe Injection Moulding Supervisor / Technician (JB6245)
Industria, Johannesburg
R30 - R35 000 CTC per month (depending on experience and technical ability)
Permanent
Seeking a hands-on EVA Injection Moulding Supervisor / Technician to operate, set up, troubleshoot and maintain EVA shoe-sole injection moulding machinery while supervising the production team.
This role combines practical machine fault-finding and repair with production supervision, operator training, quality control, safety and the achievement of daily production targets.
This is not a purely supervisory position. The successful candidate must personally diagnose and repair hydraulic, mechanical, basic electrical, temperature-control, injection and material-feeding faults. Candidates unable to troubleshoot and repair injection moulding machinery will not be suitable.
Minimum Requirements:
Grade 12 / Matric or equivalent; a mechanical, electrical, fitter or millwright qualification will be advantageous.
Minimum 3 to 5 years' practical experience with injection moulding machinery; EVA footwear or sole production, Chinese EVA machines, mould changes and EVA raw materials will be highly advantageous.
Demonstrated ability to diagnose machine faults, carry out first-line repairs and return machinery to production - essential.
Strong mechanical and hydraulic troubleshooting experience, including pumps, valves, cylinders, hoses, motors, couplings and bearings.
Basic electrical and PLC fault-finding ability covering switches, sensors, relays, contactors, wiring, heating elements and temperature controllers.
Able to set operating parameters, injection pressure, timing, temperatures, hydraulic pressure and moulding cycles.
Experience supervising production employees, allocating staff, monitoring performance and training machine operators.
Able to identify production and quality problems caused by the machine, mould, material, operator or process.
Able to read technical manuals, keep accurate records and follow machine-safety, isolation, PPE, guarding, emergency-stop and hydraulic-pressure-release procedures.
Duties and Responsibilities:
Start, operate and shut down EVA injection moulding machines correctly and ensure consistent, safe production output.
Set and adjust machine parameters, injection pressure, timing, temperatures, hydraulic pressure, moulding cycles, moulds and material feeding.
Monitor production cycles and identify abnormal noises, leaks, pressure changes, temperature fluctuations and other signs of machine failure.
Diagnose hydraulic, mechanical, electrical, temperature-control, injection-system and material-feeding faults and carry out repairs or adjustments within the limits of competence.
Safely isolate machinery, identify the likely cause and provide accurate technical information when specialist assistance is required, then assist with and test completed repairs.
Complete daily machine inspections and preventative maintenance covering oil levels, lubrication, hoses, fittings, electrical connections, pumps, motors, heating systems, clamping systems, safety switches and emergency stops.
Identify worn components before failure, maintain the preventative-maintenance schedule and keep accurate breakdown, repair and maintenance records.
Allocate operators and production employees to machines and workstations and ensure production schedules and daily targets are followed.
Monitor attendance, punctuality, machine utilisation, hourly output, downtime, bottlenecks, material wastage, rejection rates and employee productivity.
Train operators on the correct and safe use of machinery, prevent unauthorised machine adjustments and ensure only competent employees operate equipment.
Inspect finished EVA products for incomplete injection, deformation, bubbles, overheating, colour, dimensions, surface defects, flash, weight and mould-definition problems.
Determine whether quality defects are caused by the machine, material, mould, operator or process and implement corrective action.
Enforce PPE, guarding, emergency-stop, housekeeping and machine-isolation requirements and immediately stop unsafe work practices.
Report accidents, near misses, dangerous conditions, significant production failures and extended breakdowns to management without delay.
Maintain daily production, machine-operation, downtime, wastage, quality, rejection, attendance and inspection records and submit accurate reports to management.

• Own transport.

• Based in Wadeville, Gauteng.
• South African citizen.MINIMUM COMPETENCY REQUIREMENTS:

• Management reporting systems knowledge.
